News.title: Southport killer is trying to ‘retraumatise families from his cell’ by playing the system, says victims’ lawyer
News.content:
MANIPULATIVE KILLER Southport killer is trying to ‘retraumatise families from his cell’ by playing the system, says victims’ lawyer

THE Southport murderer is trying “to retraumatise the families from his cell”, the victims’ lawyer said.

Axel Rudakubana, who is serving a 52-year life sentence for killing three girls, was earlier this week transferred from Belmarsh Prison to Broadmoor Hospital nearly two years on from the horror attack.



Rudakubana, now 19, murdered Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, Bebe King, six, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, and attempted the murder of eight other children and two adults.

It’s been nearly two years since he carried out the attack at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class on July 29, 2024.



It was confirmed by the Ministry of Justice that the killer was transferred to the category A psychiatric facility.

Chris Walker, who is representing the three bereaved families, told BBC Breakfast that this decision highlighted a concerning “pattern” in Rudakubana’s behaviour that is “retraumatising” for the victims’ families.



Walker said: “It’s a deep concern of mine that this is a pattern starting to develop by him trying to retraumatise the families from his cell, and it’s a deep concern that this is going to occur every anniversary.”

He also pointed out that there was “no suggestion” that Rudakubana was under any form of “psychosis” when he carried out the murders.



The families were only informed of the decision in a letter on July 22, but were not given details on why the transfer happened.

Walker said: “With the vacuum of information, the concern is that he’s manipulating the situation to his own benefit.”

He added: “For it to come out the week before the anniversary seems coincidental to us.

“Whether that’s been poorly handled by the Government, or whether it’s designed by him.”

Sally Jameson, a junior housing minister and former prison officer, said on Friday that Rudakubana would be returned to prison “as soon as possible” but that she was not familiar with why the decision had been taken to move him.



Offenders who present an increased risk, and cannot be managed safely in a prison environment because of mental disorders, can be moved to secure psychiatric units like Broadmoor.

People in these units are treated as patients rather than prisoners.

The Sun revealed that Rudakubana will live in a university hall-style room – and be free to spend his days at Broadmoor reading, watching films and TV and writing to friends and relatives.

The triple child killer will also have access to a state of the art gym, an on-site cafe and shop and even the hospital’s resident hairdresser and dentist.

Walker said: “When he did what he did, it was carefully planned, it was meticulous and it was designed to cause the maximum distress to society.



“There’s no evidence of any mental health disorder being a component of his crime. There’s no evidence of psychosis.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The families say, given that, he needs to serve a prison sentence, he should not be going to hospital. He needs to be in prison.”

Walker said that the letter included the offer of a meeting with the Director for Public Protection, which he will attend on behalf of the families.

News.title: Henry Nowak killer ‘literally shaking with fear’ at ‘Monster Mansion’ jail as bloodthirsty lags have target on his back
News.content:
HENRY Nowak’s killer is said to be “literally shaking with fear” behind bars after becoming a target for some of Britain’s most dangerous inmates.

Vickrum Digwa, 23, is locked up inside HMP Frankland in County Durham, the notorious high-security jail – nicknamed “Monster Mansion” – where he is being monitored over fears he could be attacked.



The prison is home to some of Britain’s most violent killers and terrorists – including Sarah Everard‘s murderer Wayne Couzens, serial killer Levi Bellfield and Lee Rigby killer Michael Adebolajo.

Digwa is said to have arrived there “terrified”, a source told the Daily Mail.



The sicko was transferred to Frankland from HMP Winchester after being jailed for life last month for murdering Southampton University student Henry Nowak.

He must serve a minimum of 21 years – though last month The Sun revealed Nowak’s killer would have his “lenient” jail sentence reviewed after the case sparked fury across the nation.



The source said: “Digwa arrived at Frankland terrified. I mean literally shaking. He was in total fear. There was none of that arrogance you saw on the police camera.

“I think he thought he wouldn’t survive the first night.”



After spending several weeks in segregation, Digwa has now been moved onto a prison wing but remains under close supervision because of the risks he faces.

The source said: “He is on a special watch list because of the recent murders in Frankland and he fits into the category of people who are at risk because of the nature of his crime and the fact that he is now a high-profile prisoner.

“There are cons in Frankland who will have a go at him, physically as well as verbally, because of who he is and so they can boast that they were the one who beat the s*** out of him.”

The insider claimed Digwa’s fearful body language has made him appear vulnerable.

Former prison governor Vanessa Frake-Harris said high-profile prisoners often become targets.



She said: “High-profile prisoners like Vickrum Digwa will always be targets. There are many in Frankland with nothing to lose but a lot of credibility to gain.

“His was a high-profile murder which angered society. This anger may well follow him into HMP Frankland.”

Jurors heard at Southampton Crown Court that Henry was walking home after a night out on December 3 last year when he crossed paths with Digwa.



The killer, carrying an eight-inch dagger around his neck, stabbed the student in the chest before inflicting four more wounds, including two to his back as Henry tried to run away.

Digwa tried to portray himself as the victim of a racist attack and failed to tell officers he had just repeatedly stabbed Henry.

Police bodycam captured the student’s final moments as he pleaded that he could not breathe.

Digwa was convicted of murder and possessing a knife in public before being jailed for life.

His mother, Kiran Kaur, was also convicted after taking the murder weapon from the scene and hiding it at the family home.



She is serving her sentence at HMP Bronzefield in Surrey, where fellow inmates include Lucy Letby, Constance Marten and Sara Sharif‘s killer Beinash Batool.

She and her sicko son are separated by around 300 miles having once sharing the same Southampton home.

Under Labour’s proposed sentencing reforms, which are currently under review, Kaur could potentially be released before the end of the year after time spent on remand is taken into account.



It comes as video footage has revealed the moment murderer Vickrum Digwa told his mother to take the knife he used to kill Henry away from the crime scene.

The Crown Prosecution Service released the clip after Digwa’s mother, Kiran Kaur, was jailed last Friday for assisting an offender.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In the footage taken on Digwa’s phone, which is pointed at the ground, he can be heard speaking to Kaur in Punjabi, asking her to remove the knife.

She then took it back to the family home.

News.title: Moment topless thug sprints off from cops before being rugby tackled & begging ‘let me go, I won’t run’
News.content:
BODYCAM footage reveals moment a cop went flying through the air to rugby tackle a shirtless suspect.

Theman’s escape failed after he tried to escape by jumping over a police car bonnet before being arrested by officers.



West Mercia Police officers were called to a Sainsbury’s supermarket in Malvern, Worcestershire, earlier this week to reports of a man behaving aggressively in public.

The suspect was told by one cop “I need you to be compliant with me” as he’s told he’s wanted on suspicion of a section four public order offence.



The man replies “no no no no” before legging it across a car park and vaulting over the bonnet of a parked up squad car.

A police officer giving chase then leaps through the air and over the bonnet to tackle the suspect to the ground.

The yob can be heard screaming: “Wait, wait. You f***ing tell me what you’re f***ing doing.”

The officer replies: “We’re arresting you.”



As he’s escorted to the police van, with a bloody elbow, he continues to plead with officers: “Please let me off for five seconds.

“I’m not going to run, please just five seconds.”

The unsympathetic offices told him “get in” and the man was arrested on suspicion of a public order offence.

A spokesperson for West Mercia Police said: “Earlier this week, officers in Malvern were called to a report of a man behaving aggressively in a public place.

“They responded quickly, located the individual and took action to safely bring the situation under control.



“A man was subsequently arrested on suspicion of a public order offence.

“Our officers work every day to defuse potentially volatile situations, protect the public and keep our communities safe.”

News.title: Speedboat with 11 European tourists on board vanishes as urgent search operation launched off coast of Indonesia
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BOAT MYSTERY Speedboat with 11 European tourists on board vanishes as urgent search operation launched off coast of Indonesia

A SPEEDBOAT with 11 European tourists and two crew members on board has vanished off the coast of Indonesia.

Rescuers are now searching for the vessel that went missing off a bay on Sulawesi Island more than 24 hours ago.



Sea conditions – including powerful winds and waves reaching up to 2.5 metres high – are making the operation challenging.

A Czech man, a Belgian man, five Dutch nationals, three Germans, a French woman and two Indonesian crew members are believed to have been on board.



The group departed Tojo Unauna regency in Central Sulawesi province on Friday morning bound for Marisa Port in the neighbouring Gorontalo province but failed to arrive as scheduled.

The alarm was raised by a local guide several hours later.

“Concerns arose when their speedboat had not arrived by afternoon,” said Heriyanto, Head of the Gorontalo Province Search and Rescue Office.

“We immediately launched a search mission overnight but until now have not found any signs of the vessel or people on board.

“We hope all victims can be found soon.”

Heriyanto added that dozens of search and rescue teams were deployed to cover approximately 300 square nautical miles of waters along and around Tomini Bay.



The area is a renowned marine tourism destination, with dozens of islands dotting its vast waters, based on the tour boat’s route projections.

A thermal-imaging drone and diving equipment are also being used in the search, he said.

Indonesia is an archipelago with more than 17,000 islands, where boats are a common form of transportation.

Lax safety standards and problems with overcrowding frequently result in accidents.

The incident comes after a passenger boat carrying 76 people sank off Selayar Island, killing at least four people.



Another 14 remain missing, including a 10-year-old boy.

Authorities officially ended the search on Friday after 58 people were rescued over the course of 10 days.

Earlier this month, at least six people died and dozens went missing after a ferry with 65 people on board sank off the coast of Bali.

News.title: Brit tourists flee hotels in middle of night as raging wildfires sweep across France & Spain with 220,000 evacuated
News.content:
BRIT tourists were forced to flee their hotels in the middle of the night as raging wildfires ripping through Europe have driven 220,000 away from their homes.

Terrifying blazes are sweeping across France and Spain, with Emmanuel Macron mobilising more than 1,000 French soldiers to aid fire crews.



Holidaymakers staying at a Holiday Inn near Bordeaux Airport were woken up at 3.30am and told that approaching smoke was forcing the hotel to close.

Wildfires raging in the flash Lège-Cap-Ferret peninsula have sent towers of smoke billowing across the region.



Among those evacuated were several Brits, including Martin and Nicola Smith from Jersey, who are holidaying with daughter Erin, 20, two-year-old granddaughter Arabella and six other relatives.

Nicola, 49, told the Daily Mail: “We were all fast asleep when a member of hotel staff knocked on the door about 3.30am and said that we were having to evacuate.

“It was a shock to the system and quite dramatic but I’d been getting alerts on my phone all night by the local French authorities warning about other areas nearby being evacuated.”

Have you been caught up in wildfires in France, Spain or elsewhere in Europe? Email joseph.mannion@the-sun.co.uk or WhatsApp 07353 096414 to share your story



Martin, 55, added: “It’s not great to be honest but what can you do?

“Apparently everywhere is being evacuated because of all the smoke drifting across to Bordeaux from the fire.



“I must admit you could really smell the smoke when we first arrived, there was a kind of haze in the air.”

A major fire near Madrid is meanwhile “at its peak” and “beyond the capacity” of firefighters to control, according to local emergency management chief Carlos Novillo.

He told the BBC: “It is not possible to attack the fire in that area, so defensive measures are being taken.”

More than 25,000 people were forced to flee their homes as the city’s president Isabel Díaz Ayusohas said the inferno was “the worst fire in the history of the region”.



Another 20,000 Spanish residents are in complete lockdown, Madrid officials said.

Díaz Ayusohas called the situation “catastrophic”, as residents in the capital were warned to stay inside their home and avoid going out unless absolutely necessary.

Two of three major wildfires to the city’s west have now merged, threatening a suburban town.

And an official warned there is “little time left” before a major fire covering 6,000 hectares merges with another 9,000-hectare blaze.



Dramatic footage showed police kicking down doors to rescue residents before the blaze consumed their homes.

Spain has declared a state of emergency, with more than 100,000 hectares – roughly the size of Berlin or Hong Kong – being scorched so far this year.



The country has faced one of its deadliest wildfire seasons in decades after 13 people were killed in the southern province of Almeria.

Seven Brits – including a 93-year-old woman – died in the blaze that consumed 7,000 hectares of land.

Sweltering temperatures brought by repeated heatwaves have exacerbated the rapid spread of fires across the continent’s south.

Cap Ferret, which is often likened to the Hamptons area of Long Island, has been burning since Wednesday.

Brit tourists were warned to “get out in 30 minutes” as a monster wildfire engulfed the resort and massive explosions sent horses bolting along the only road off the peninsula.



France’s Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said more than 14,000 hectares have been claimed by the blaze, while around 50 firefighters were injured yesterday alone.

He told French broadcaster TF1: “We have never seen a convective fire of this magnitude.”

The fire is “self-sustaining” and changes direction, he said – and it is tearing towards Bordeaux, where the airport has been shut.

BBC journalist Joanna Kent, who was on holiday at a Cap Ferret campsite with her family, said they were given just 30 minutes to evacuate.

She said on Instagram: “We saw the smoke about four o’clock (on Wednesday) cycling back from the Cap Ferret Peninsula. There was ash in the air.



“Now the smoke has definitely got thicker this morning. We’ve been wondering all morning if we were going to be evacuated or not.

“In the last ten minutes, the police have come round and they told us that we’ve got 30 minutes to get out.

“So now there’s a bit of a scramble with everyone here just packing up their cars and making a dash for it.”

Terrified tourists could be seen boarding boats yesterday as they tried to escape the fire.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Resident Patrick Martineau, 69, said: “The gendarmes came and knocked on every door, the fire was about 500 metres away – we grabbed some things and left.”



Shocking footage also showed several cars racing to the mainland to get away from the approaching inferno.

News.title: Teen girl sexually assaulted in Asda before hero female shopper stepped in to confront suspect as man, 28, arrested
News.content:

ASSAULT PROBE Teen girl sexually assaulted in Asda before hero female shopper stepped in to confront suspect as man, 28, arrested

COPS have arrested a man after reports a teenage girl was sexually assaulted in the kitchen aisle of an Asda store.

A hero female shopper jumped is said to have confronted the suspect during the horror incident inside the busy supermarket.

Officers rushed to the shop on Asdale Road in Wakefield at around 3.45pm yesterday.

The force confirmed a 28-year-old man was arrested at the scene on suspicion of sexual assault.





He was also arrested for an alleged assault of a police officer.

Detectives are now trying to track down the woman who confronted the suspect to help with their investigation.

Any other witnesses or anyone with information is urged to contact the force, quoting crime reference 13260419558.

News.title: China has likely spied on Burnham for YEARS as he plotted No10 coup & know PM’s next moves before he does, expert warns
News.content:
CHINA’s network of top-secret spies has been tracking Andy Burnham’s every move for years, an intelligence expert has warned.

Beijing knows the new Prime Minister’s next moves before even he does, intelligence analyst and cybersecurity expert Ryan McBeth claims.



The intelligence analyst and cybersecurity expert told The Sun: “China has likely had a file on Prime Minister Andy Burnham for years.

“It’s almost certain that China’s already developed a profile not just on the Prime Minister, but on his inner circle.



“Where they go, what they do, and when they do it.”

Ryan says that Beijing, like many global superpowers, will have a detailed file of information on almost every world leader.



China has around 5,000 people working in information warfare trying to build up as strong a profile on key players as possible, according to Ryan.

One of the units is reportedly known to keep Taiwan and its political figures under constant surveillance.

At least three other Chinese “battalions” are engaged in information warfare and intelligence collection around the globe, Ryan claims.

This means that hundreds of secret operatives are feared to be searching for information on Brits – especially new figures such as Burnham.



For years, Burnham was talked about as the next leader of the Labour Party when he impressed during his time as Greater Manchester mayor.

As pressure piled on Sir Keir Starmer earlier this year and he announced his resignation, Burnham was the first and only name tipped to replace him.

He took office on Monday and already has plans to shake up British politics for good.



But Ryan believes that China would have had its eyes on him for years now – even before his PM dreams were so widely publicised.

He said: “China knows a lot about your Prime Minister. They have likely been tracking him for years.

“They most likely have courses of action for him that they know what he is going to do, perhaps even before he knows he’s going to do it.”

The intelligence expert, who even believes there is a folder on himself due to his public speaking on security issues on YouTube, also detailed how they could get information on a figure like Burnham.

“It’s possible that some of his inner circle might be tracked, perhaps not his entire family,” he said.



“Tracking his inner circle either through intelligence means or intelligence collection with human intelligence, getting to know people in his inner circle, or getting to know people who are ancillary to his inner circle could all be done.

“And they’re almost certainly using electronic means such as evaluating social media posts.”

Social media tracking has the ability to tell a hacker your exact location through phone data.



This can help people get information on what time a person is awake, when they go to sleep and when they go to lunch.

Ryan also warned that Wi-Fi information could be collected from a phone just like how supermarkets access user data to send out offers and coupons.

Dozens of Chinese spies living in the UK have been reported in recent years – including several who had close ties to No 10.

Three political advisers were arrested earlier this year on suspicion of spying for China, the Metropolitan Police said.

David Taylor, 39, married to East Kilbride and Strathaven MP Joani Reid was accused of assisting a foreign intelligence service.



She was reported by a fellow MP who said they were concerned information regarding the UK’s nuclear deterrent could have ended up in China’s hands.

Also arrested included former Welsh Government special adviser Steve Jones, 68, and ex-Labour press officer Matthew Aplin, 43.

All three deny the claims and refute any suggestions they had links to China.

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was also caught up in worrying Chinese spy claims over his friendship with 50-year-old Yang Tengbo.

During a past tribunal hearing, judges found Yang had not been honest about his links to the Chinese state.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

This meant he could exploit his relationship with the former duke and other high-ranking public figures such as ex-Prime Ministers David Cameron and Theresa May.

In a statement, Yang said he had done “nothing wrong or unlawful” and descriptions of him as an alleged spy were “entirely untrue”.

News.title: Six children among eight family members killed in ‘suspicious’ house fire as arson investigators scour scene
News.content:
BLAZE TRAGEDY Six children among eight family members killed in ‘suspicious’ house fire as arson investigators scour scene

SIX children are among eight family members who have been killed in a “suspicious” house fire in Michigan.

Cops are now probing whether the tragedy was a murder-suicide after some of the victims were found with gunshot wounds.



The children ranged in age from around five to 15 years old, according to Captain Jacob Sparks of the Ottawa County Sheriff’s Office.

Police have described the incident as “suspicious”, but Sparks added it was “too early to say that it’s a murder-suicide”.



He continued: “I can tell you that that’s one theory that we have and we’re still looking to see if we can verify that.”

Sparks confirmed that some of the victims suffered gunshot wounds, although police were probing whether “other means” were involved.



“It would be premature for me to say what caused their deaths,” he said.

Sparks added that autopsies will take place on Saturday.

Firefighters were called to the house between 8.30am and 9am yesterday morning after receiving reports of a strong smell of smoke.

They scoured the area without success, but later rushed back to the scene after residents reported white smoke rising from the home on the 14900 block of Riverside Trail.



The neighbourhood where the blaze broke out appears to be an affluent area with pristine green lawns and tall trees.

It comes days after five children from the same family were killed in a horror house fire in Peru.

At least 10 people were found dead inside the home with the youngest being a three-year-old and the eldest being a 72-year-old.

The victims were all members of the same family from Lima, Peru, police chief Oscar Arriola confirmed.



Peru’s president-elect Keiko Fujimori visited the ruins as she called the deaths “a terrible massacre”.

Fire crews rushed to two homes in the southern La Victoria district early on Wednesday after witnesses recalled seeing flames coming out of the windows.

At least 17 members of the family were in the building when the fire started at 3am local time.

Seven managed to escape the blaze, reports Infobae.

Survivor Gina Vilchez told reporters she was able to save herself and her children as they ran through smoke and dodged falling charred debris.



Five children, aged three, six, six, eight and 15, were found dead after the fire was extinguished.

Five adults aged 29, 35, 42 and 72, were also recovered.

Police chief Arriola said their bodies were burned beyond recognition.

One line of inquiry behind the cause of the inferno is a possible arsonist attack by local extortionists.

A group are known to have been threatening local businesses around the same time as the deadly inferno, Peruvian media reported.



Local media say the family owned electric motorcycles and had a mattress business so may have been targeted.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Colonel John Lujan, who is leading the investigation, confirmed “a possible deliberate act or a case of extortion” is among the possible causes.

A statement from the National Police of Peru said: “Today, all of Peru falls silent in the face of a tragedy that plunges our nation into mourning.”

News.title: Spain and France wildfires live: Brits among 200,000 fleeing scorched tourist areas
News.content:
More than 200,000 people in France and Spain have been evacuated as wildfires continue to tear through vast areas of Europe - with temperatures expected to surge higher next week

Huge wildfires are ravaging parts of south-west France and central Spain, forcing the evacuation of an estimated 200,000 people - including British tourists.

French authorities have ordered the immediate evacuation of suburbs in Bordeaux - the largest city in the affected region - as the flames shift towards the area.

British families were among those evacuated from a Bordeaux hotel at 3.30am as staff warned smoke had been travelling over from the raging fires around 20-miles away in the Cap Ferret peninsula.

Around 141,000 people have been evacuated from their homes in France's Gironde and Landes departments, the French interior ministry said. Some residents and holidaymakers even fled by boat as flames swept through the popular tourist area of Cap Ferret on France's Atlantic coast.

In Spain, 60,000 have been forced to leave their homes in towns west of Madrid, the Spanish interior ministry said. Wildfires in the Madrid region and the nearby province of Ávila have prompted the government to declare a national emergency over wildfires for the first time.

News.title: 100 firefighters tackle massive Essex blaze as farm 'explosion' shakes buildings
News.content:
More than 100 firefighters have been tackling a massive fire at a farm off Southend Road between East Hanningfield and Rettendon in Essex

A massive explosion at a farm in Essex has shaken buildings up to 15 miles away, with footage showing a huge fireball erupting from the site.

Essex County Fire and Rescue Service said more than 100 firefighters worked to tackle a blaze involving industrial units at a farm off Southend Road, between East Hanningfield and Rettendon, near Chelmsford, on Friday evening.

The blaze, which is understood to be at Highlands Farm, has been declared a major incident due to its size. Police have cordoned off a large area around the site.

"If you live or are travelling nearby, please continue to keep your windows and doors closed," the fire service said. "Please avoid the area while we deal with this incident."

News.title: 'I lost 7st and married myself after realising truth about bad boy exes'
News.content:
Standing at the altar in a gorgeous white gown, hands clasped around a fragrant bouquet, Louisa Warren had never felt so sure, as she glanced over her handwritten wedding vows. Speaking slowly and confidently, she said: “I will stay true to myself and live without changing myself to please others.”

A kindly celebrant, wearing sparkling, diamante-framed specs, broke the silence, as she spoke to a sea of empty chairs in the Las Vegas chapel. Addressing the single guest in the congregation, she explained how bride Louisa - a 39-year-old film producer from Manchester - was all dressed up, ready to marry herself.

Now, several months on from the November 2025 ceremony, Louisa, 39, says: “I know how mad this sounds, but after being unlucky in love for decades, marrying myself is one of the best things I’ve ever done.”

View 6 Images Louisa Warren poses in her wedding dress (Image: Andrew Stenning/Daily Mirror)

‌



Life for Louisa had not gone to plan. She says: “By 25, I was sure that I’d be married to a gorgeous man who adored me, living in London and pregnant with our first child.” But while she dated, no one was right. She admits: “I knew I was picking the wrong guys. I’d always go for Alpha males, bad boys with muscles and tattoos, who had the gift of the gab.

“They’d make me weak at the knees with their twinkly eyes and compliments, tell me every lie under the sun, and then once we’d been to bed they’d be gone. Heartbroken, I’d swear to myself that I’d make a better choice next time, but I never did.”

Then, aged 29, her world was turned upside down. She explains: “I’d always had a fast metabolism. If I went running, I could eat what I wanted and keep my size 8-10 figure.”

But she started feeling lethargic, craving pints of orange juice and piled on weight - also developing a weird rash on her leg.

‌



Gaining 10 stone and jumping to a size 26, she says: “I became depressed and stopped wanting to socialise, I was just too embarrassed. I did occasionally meet guys on Tinder, but they’d be men who’d openly say, ‘I like big girls.’ It was horrible to be defined by my size like that.”

She went to other people’s weddings, but never her own. She says: “I’d watch my friends say their vows while I sat there without even a plus-one.” Meanwhile, family friends would tell her she’d “catch a husband” if she lost weight.

View 6 Images Olivia Warren when she was. size 26

Her breakthrough came in December 2023. She recalls: “A friend wanted a beauty IV drip and I thought it sounded fun. The medic who administered it said that my blood pressure was incredibly high and asked if I was diabetic. She was so sure I needed a diabetes test that she rang my doctor.”

‌



And she was right. Seven years after her health problems began, Louisa was diagnosed with diabetes. Given medication, the weight began falling away. Confident enough to start dating again, sadly, her dalliances still ended in tears. She says: “I was still an eternal romantic, hoping to meet the ‘one’ who would complete me. It just never happened.”

In October 2025, aged 39 and seven stone lighter than at her heaviest, Louisa went to the US with her friend, Sam. She says: “We went to Universal Studios in Florida and then down to Key West. We were having an amazing time.”

When Sam suggested they pop to Las Vegas on their way home, Louisa agreed. She says: “I’d always wanted to go.” Two days in, they found themselves walking past a wedding chapel. Louisa continues: “I saw these signs outside with prices for their wedding packages. There was even a drive-through, where people were getting married in their cars. It was crazy!”

View 6 Images Bride Olivia Warren in the Las Vegas wedding chapel

‌



Then Louisa realised their casino hotel also had a wedding chapel and dragged her friend in to find out more. Discovering they offered both legally binding and ceremonial weddings, she said to the celebrant: “I’d love to find someone to marry.”

“You can always marry yourself,” she suggested, adding that making a commitment to yourself can be very healing. Louisa jumped at the chance. She says: “After a really tough time in my life, here was the chance to do something just for me. It would be so empowering to marry myself, to show that I didn’t need another person to make myself whole.”

With one click, Louisa paid £80 for a 30-minute ceremony package, with the celebrant and flowers adding another £110. She laughs: “Sadly, Elvis wasn’t available to officiate!”

View 6 Images Louisa Warren trying on wedding gowns

‌



Next stop was the bridal boutique. She says: “When the owner asked me about my wedding and I heard myself say ‘actually, I’m marrying myself’ it seemed crazy.

“But when I stood in front of the mirror in this beautiful £2,250 gown, I began to cry. All these years I’d tried to find love. Now I looked like a bride, and felt so beautiful, and I was marrying myself.”

But, knowing the luxury gown was beyond her budget, Louisa found another she liked for just £100. She says: “I added a lovely veil for £100, smoothing underwear for £89 and remembered that I already had some white shoes.’”

Next came the ring. She says: “There was a gift shop in our hotel and I saw a ring with a lovely red stone for £41. It was perfect.” Running through the hotel for the 10am ceremony, people were calling ‘congratulations,’ assuming Louisa’s friend Sam was the groom - when he was actually her only wedding guest.

‌



He says: “I shouted back, ‘No, I’m marrying myself!’ as I ran past, laughing hysterically to see their totally baffled faces!”

View 6 Images Louisa Warren's handwritten wedding vows (Image: Supplied)

Asked if she had any wedding vows, she wrote them in the chapel, saying: “As I wrote, ‘I will stay true to myself and live without changing myself to please others’ I felt a lump in my throat.”

Recalling her walk down the aisle, she continues: “It was surreal to reach the end, knowing no man would be joining me. That this really was all about me.” And reading her vows was deeply emotional. She recalls: “My hands were shaking and I was trying not to cry. It felt so significant to be making these promises to care for myself.”

‌



Then, placing the wedding ring on her own finger, it was over. Louisa says: “I felt incredible.” After some celebratory chicken wings, it was time to take her wedding dress off and start her ‘married life.’

She says: “I was really sad and emotional. It had been such a special day and now it was over.” Before posting pictures of her big day, she had to tell someone.

“I knew I needed to tell my mum first,” she says. “Mum just sighed – she’s used to me doing crazy stuff. My friends were confused and freaked out when they saw the pictures of me in Vegas in a white dress. Who on earth had I married?"

View 6 Images Louisa Warren's £41 wedding ring (Image: Andrew Stenning/Daily Mirror)

‌



She continues: “They thought marrying myself was hilarious and even though I tried to explain that it was really significant to me, they didn’t understand.”

Eight months later, she knows she made the right choice. She says: “Marrying myself has shown me that I’m a whole person, and don’t need anyone else to complete me. But I haven’t put my married status on my online dating profile – I think that’s the sort of thing to bring up after a few dates!”

And she hasn’t given up on romance. She says: “One day I hope to have a handsome man waiting for me at the end of the aisle. “But until then, I’m very happy that I put a ring on my own finger.”

News.title: 'I looked pregnant but doctors said there was no baby - they missed something that could have killed me'
News.content:
A mum claims doctors repeatedly 'fobbed off' her pregnant-looking belly as IBS - only to discover it was stage four ovarian cancer.

Cydnie Malone said she first started experiencing symptoms including pain under her rib, bloating and nausea in July 2023. The 31-year-old recalled how her bloating was so severe that she 'looked pregnant' and her stomach would 'move around' on its own and 'gurgle and gargle' at her.

Cydnie visited her doctor about her symptoms and was referred for further testing, before being diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). Despite a blood test revealing that her CA-125 marker, a marker for ovarian cancer, was more than triple the normal level of under 35, Cydnie claims her symptoms were repeatedly brushed off.

View 8 Images Cydnie thought doctors would soon get to the bottom of her health issues (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

‌



Weight loss meds could be used to stop alcoholics boozing, study suggests READ MORE :

Surge in Type 2 diabetes cases among women under 40 sparks health time bomb warning READ MORE :

Over the next two years the aesthetics practitioner claims she visited Epsom Hospital and St Helier Hospital between 20 and 30 times but was repeatedly 'fobbed off' - even when her CA-125 levels sky-rocketed. In April 2025, Cydnie visited a different hospital after she returned from a holiday where her belly continued to get 'bigger and bigger' until she looked pregnant.

She claimed doctors told her 'there's no baby' and said it was a fluid build-up, which they drained. But the following day, Cydnie received the devastating diagnosis of stage four ovarian cancer.

In May 2025 she underwent surgery to remove 15 tumours found around her ovaries and underwent a hysterectomy. A year later, Cydnie received the news she was in remission after undergoing six gruelling rounds of chemotherapy.

View 8 Images Cydnie's belly swelled as if she was pregnant (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

‌



The mum-of-one believes her cancer wouldn't have spread if she had been diagnosed earlier - and is urging other women who experience any symptoms of ovarian cancer to visit their GP. Cydnie, from Banstead, Surrey, said: "The doctors said my bloating and pain was from IBS and polycystic ovaries.

"They kept fobbing me off and fobbing me off and fobbing me off. They did my CA-125 ovarian cancer marker and those levels are meant to be 30 and under.

"Anything over 30 and above they panic about. Mine were 97 and they did nothing about it. They kept telling me it was PCOS and IBS and that there was nothing wrong with me."

View 8 Images She felt she was being continually fobbed off (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

‌



Cydnie claimed she visited the doctors with her symptoms up to 30 times as they continued to worsen to the point that she 'looked pregnant'.

Cydnie claimed: "I was at the doctors a good 20-30 times. I kept going back for appointments, my CA-125 kept rising and rising and they kept doing nothing about it. My CA-125 markers reached 497 and they still kept telling me there was nothing wrong with me.

"I kept going back for appointments trying to figure out what it was. My belly was so hard and round, I literally looked like I was pregnant.

View 8 Images An x-ray pinpointing Cydnie's tumours (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

‌



"It would gurgle and gargle and it would wake me up in the night with all of the fluid moving around - it was the weirdest thing in the world. It was so hard and so full I literally had a bump, it was mad. The bloating was painful, it was horrible."

After returning from a trip to New York in April 2025, Cydnie visited a different hospital as her bloated belly continued to grow. Cydnie said: "My belly kept getting bigger and bigger and bigger. I went to New York on holiday with my friend, come back from holiday and my belly had ballooned up.

"My partner took me to a different hospital and they said 'there's no baby, you're full of fluid'. If I didn't got to that hospital with a swollen belly then I wouldn't be here today. They admitted me and drained six-and-a-half litres of fluid out of me."

View 8 Images Cydnie recovering after surgery (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

‌



Cydnie received the devastating diagnosis of stage four ovarian cancer and underwent surgery to have 15 tumours removed, as well as a full hysterectomy on May 13 2025. She said: "It was stage four when I was diagnosed, it had spread to all of my other organs. I felt distraught because I knew something was wrong with me.

"I was frustrated, I was angry, and I felt let down because it was right in front of them and I kept telling them something was wrong with me. I was distraught that I had to have a hysterectomy - me and my partner wanted a child together.

"That [the hysterectomy] has just broken me as well, it feels like your womanhood is taken away from you. You feel like your life has been taken out of your hands."

View 8 Images The tumours were removed in an operation (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

‌



The surgery successfully removed 96% of Cydnie's cancer and this was followed by six rounds of chemotherapy that she finished in October 2025. In May 2026, Cydnie received the news that she is in remission, but she believes the cancer wouldn't have spread if doctors had diagnosed her earlier.

Cydnie said: "It felt surreal when I was told I was in remission. There's obviously a possibility that it could come back in other areas.

"But it could have been avoided and not spread if they'd just listened and opened their eyes to what is in front of them. If I didn't go to a different hospital and go with my gut instinct I wouldn't have made it. I'm glad I've come out of the other side."

View 8 Images She was glad to come out the other side after her op (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

‌



Now Cydnie is urging other people who experience symptoms to visit their GP and 'push' for answers. She said: "They call it the silent killer because there's no symptoms of it really.

"If you've got the bloating and pain, or if you know something is not right in your body, then you've got to push for it because it's your life and it's not a game.

"Don't be fobbed off if the medication they're giving you is not working then it's obviously something deep down. Sending someone for a CA-125 blood test could save their life."

View 8 Images Cydnie is much better - but warns others to make sure they fight for proper diagnosis (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

‌



A spokesperson for Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust said: "We are very sorry to hear about Ms Malone's experience and recognise that her cancer diagnosis must have been an extremely difficult and distressing time for her.

"We’re grateful that this has been brought to our attention so we can carry out an investigation - we will also reach out to Ms Malone so we can listen to her concerns in full."

WHAT IS OVARIAN CANCER? (Info from NHS)

Ovarian cancer affects the ovaries, which are two small organs that store the eggs needed to make babies and produce female sex hormones. The symptoms of ovarian cancer, such as bloating, are not always obvious.

Ovarian cancer is often diagnosed late, but early diagnosis can mean it is more treatable. Treatments for ovarian cancer include surgery and chemotherapy.

News.title: Essex explosion hurls photographer into door and blows in studio roof as fertiliser blast causes mayhem
News.content:
Essex explosion hurls photographer into door and blows in studio roof as fertiliser blast causes mayhem

Scott Johnson, 46, a wedding photographer from Chelmsford, Essex, said the impact of the blast 'threw him into the door' of his studio - firefighters continue to tackle the blaze this morning

View 3 Images Homes were evacuated amid the 'major incident' near Chelmsford, Essex (Image: X)

A man has told of the terrifying moment he was 'thrown into his door' after a huge explosion tore through the Essex countryside.

‌



Police declared a major incident last night and residents were evacuated from their homes after a large container of fertiliser exploded while firefighters responded to a blaze between East Hanningfield and Rettendon.

‌



The blaze, which has engulfed industrial units and a field, created a huge fireball and a shock wave felt up to 15 miles away. Firefighters remained at the scene this morning after tackling the flames overnight.

‌



Scott Johnson, 46, a wedding photographer from Galleywood, Chelmsford, witnessed the blast - and said it was so powerful it pushed him into the door of his studio.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Essex fire live: Inferno rages after explosion as 100 firefighters tackle flames READ MORE :

Cairngorms wildfire declared major incident as hundreds flee their homes READ MORE :

Describing the moment of the explosion, Scott said: “I’ve never seen or heard anything like it in my entire life, I felt it. I was standing by the door, and the force pushed me into the studio door just as I locked it. If the door was open I'd have been blown into the studio.

‌



“I just looked up and there was just a barn raining down on top of me, on fire, bits of metal, bits of wood, bits of Christ knows what. I’ve literally walked away, apart from a fuzzy ear, completely unscathed.

“I think my studio is going to be ok, the roof had been blown in and all the tiles were completely askew but from the aerial footage I’ve seen it’s not on fire.”

View 3 Images Photographer Scott Johnson, 46, said he had 'never seen or heard anything like it in my entire life' (Image: @theedgepics/Instagram)

‌



He explained he managed to save most of the expensive equipment out of his studio, which is located on the industrial estate.

Essex County Fire and Rescue Service deployed 100 firefighters to the scene at the peak of the response last night as evacuations were carried out in the immediate area around the blast.

Residents were told to keep their doors and windows shut as a precaution due to the large plumes of smoke.

‌



Around 50 firefighters remain on scene this morning to put the remains of the fire out.

View 3 Images A fireball was visible for miles around after the fertiliser caught fire

Group Manager Dave Walpole said: "We will likely be here throughout the day and the scene is still producing some smoke so please keep windows and doors closed."

‌



Area Manager Dave Bond said: "We expect to be here throughout the night and into tomorrow. There will still be visible smoke from the site overnight, but the current wind direction is in our favour, and is drifting up away from homes. If in doubt, and you can smell it, keep your doors and windows closed as a precaution. “There will be a thorough investigation carried out to find the cause of the fire."

Area Manager Dave Bond said: "This is a significant fire but we have it under control and there is no wider risk to members of the public. A number of industrial units have caught alight as well as a field and crews have been working to prevent the fire spreading to nearby houses.

"While on the scene, fertiliser inside one of the units exploded and residents across the county have reported hearing and feeling it. This is why we declared a major incident and I want to reassure our residents that there is no wider risk to the public at this time.

Article continues below

"Everybody at the scene is safe, residents nearby have been evacuated while we put the fire out and Southend Road is currently closed to allow us more space to work safely.

"We expect to be at the scene throughout the night. It is producing lots of smoke so we recommended keeping your windows and doors shut if you live nearby. “Roads will remain closed. Please avoid the area."

News.title: Teen girl 'sexually assaulted' in Wakefield Asda as shopper 'confronts suspect'
News.content:
Teen girl 'sexually assaulted' in Wakefield Asda as shopper 'confronts suspect'

Police were called to an Asda supermarket in Wakefield, West Yorkshire, following reports that a teenage girl had been sexually assaulted inside the store

View Image The alleged sexual offence took place at an Asda in Wakefield (Image: Google)

Police have arrested a man on suspicion of sexually assaulting a teenage girl in an Asda supermarket.

‌



Officers were called to the store on Asdale Road in Wakefield at around 3:45pm on Thursday to reports of a sexual assault.

‌



West Yorkshire Police said it understands the suspect was confronted by a woman who was shopping in the kitchen aisle and have urged her to get in touch and assist with the ongoing investigation.

‌



A 28-year-old man was arrested at the scene on suspicion of sexual assault and assault of a police officer, the force added.

West Yorkshire Police said: "We are appealing for a woman to come forward following a reported sexual offence in a supermarket in Wakefield.

‌



"Officers were called to the ASDA supermarket on Asdale Road at around 3.45pm yesterday (23 July) to reports that a man had sexually assaulted a teenage girl within the store.

"A 28-year-old man was arrested at the scene on suspicion of sexual assault and also assault PC offences.

"We understand that a woman who was shopping in the kitchen aisle confronted the suspect and officers are urging her to come forward to assist with the ongoing enquiries into this incident.

Article continues below
