News.title: Africa improves health defences, but it remains vulnerable to pandemics
News.content:
Africa is significantly better prepared for a pandemic than it was five years ago, a major review of the continent’s health security has found.

The review, which tracked dozens of health metrics across the continent, found that local and international investments in Africa’s health sector since the pandemic have “paid off.”

Published by the Brown University Pandemic Centre and the Nuclear Threat Initiative, a US non-profit, the report is the third of its kind and provides an update on two previous reviews from 2019 and 2021.

Investment in health by African governments grew rapidly during the pandemic. Post-pandemic, the average spend now sits at around 7.4 per cent of GDP, roughly $135 billion per year across the continent.

That figure still falls significantly below those of high-income countries, where the average spend on health sits at around 11.2 per cent of GDP.

The new African Health Security Index report found that almost every African country – 53 out of 54, excluding only the Republic of the Congo – has improved its ability to prevent, detect, and respond to disease outbreaks since 2021, the last time the index was updated.

Overall, the continent scores 41.2 out of 100 on its health security – up from 32.9 five years ago.

The score is built from hundreds of specific indicators covering things like how far people live from a hospital, how well infectious patients can be isolated, the size and training level of the health workforce, laboratory capacity, and the availability of vaccines and other critical medicines during an outbreak.

News.title: Ebola death toll passes 1,000 as outbreak shows no signs of slowing
News.content:
More than 1,000 people have now died in the outbreak of Ebola in the Congo, as medics struggle to curb the fastest-growing epidemic of the virus.

Dozens of deaths are being recorded each day and modelling has forecast that, in a worst case scenario, it could become the worst Ebola outbreak in history.

The outbreak, centred on the north east of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), passed the four-figure death milestone little more than two months after it was first declared.

By contrast, the worst outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever on record, which struck West Africa from 2014 to 2016, took eight months from the first case to reach 1,000 deaths. It went on to kill 11,000 people.

The latest figures from the DRC’s national public health institute show 2,536 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,033 deaths, with at least 738 patients in isolation or hospitalised.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

Sports.title: Man Utd’s Joshua Zirkzee blueprint and new ‘Carrick ball’ – what we learnt from Rosenborg win
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED picked up their first pre-season win with a 5-0 thumping victory over Rosenborg at the sunny Lerkendal Stadium.

Bouncing back from their defeat to Wrexham six days earlier, Michael Carrick’s men delivered a statement win — packed with stellar individual displays and a clear tactical revolution.



United well and truly dusted off the pre-season cobwebs against a match-fit Rosenborg side who find themselves embroiled in a relegation scrap 13 games into their domestic season.

Back in 2024, Erik ten Hag was left fuming after a youthful United team featuring Marcus Rashford slumped to a grim 1-0 defeat on this very pitch.



Fast forward to now, and Michael Carrick was left purring over a series of “fantastic goals.”

SunSport brings you three things we learnt from United’s second preseason match without the World Cup players.



Distinct change in ‘Carrick-ball’

There has been more of a focus on controlling possession, dictating tempo and suffocating sides in their own half in United’s first two pre-season matches.

The midfield pivot of Mason Mount and Andrey Santos showed this best, by controlling the rhythm and building phase by phase until Rosenborg retreated.

Front man Joshua Zirkzee and No10 Shea Lacey, with no Benjamin Sesko and Bruno Fernandes in Trondheim, were then responsible for picking up spaces that could be found by line-breaking passes played from midfield.

Carrick’s initial revival was built on rapid counter-attacks—powered by the pace of Bryan Mbeumo and Patrick Dorgu and the magic of Fernandes and Matheus Cunha.



Fans can expect more of Carrick’s slow, methodical build-up next season. But transitions will of course stay, that’s in United’s ‘DNA‘.

Mount shines

Mount has spent the majority of career further forward, but Carrick clearly likes him as a No8.

Off the ball, Mount was unleashed to join the front four press, while Santos held down the fort behind him as a true No.6 enforcer.



Carrick was keen to keep Mount, United have rebuffed inquiries around him and the 27-year-old could impact what the club do in the lead up to deadline day.

United have not ruled out ending the window without a third midfielder, despite Manuel Ugarte‘s nine-month injury diagnosis following knee surgery.

Of course, Mount’s biggest battle is against himself.

He must stay fit in a make-or-break season at United as Youri Tielemans arrives from Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Axed top-tier ref sues bosses over ‘bullying’ after claiming he was put in a choke-hold at a training camp
Sports.content:
REFFING DISGRACE Axed top-tier ref sues bosses over ‘bullying’ after claiming he was put in a choke-hold at a training camp

Credit: Getty

AN axed top-tier ref is suing bosses — claiming he was put in a choke-hold at a training camp.

The unnamed official loses his £100,000-a-year salary as one of five demoted from the Premier League and the Championship next season.



A source told The Sun that during an appeal process the ref raised the allegation he had been put in a choke-hold by his trainer in front of witnesses in September 2024.

He is believed to have later acknowledged it was a less aggressive incident.



But he is still suing Professional Game Match Officials Ltd — now called Pro Ref.

The source said: “The refs are promoted and demoted based on performance, and it is sad to see this action being taken.”

Meanwhile, about 35 refs were told they had to return money to the organisation after a bungle over performance pay-outs.

The source added: “There was talk of rebranding PGMOL after the downfall of Prem ref David Coote. But the rebrand couldn’t have had a worse start.”

Pro Ref said in relation to the pay bungle: “We quickly rectified a human processing error whereby a very small number of officials were initially affected either by underpayment or overpayment. All officials will receive what was agreed based on their performance in 2025/26.”

The demoted refs have lost their money-spinning jobs and guaranteed salary but can still pick up match fees next season by officiating in Leagues 1 and 2 and the National League.



Up to 15 assistant referees have been told their services will not be required next season owing to a “lack of potential”.

The organisation is accused of getting rid of refs to bring in “more diverse, younger officials”.

Sports.title: Man Utd player ratings: Joshua Zirkzee fights way back into first-team contention as Shea Lacey puts in mature display
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED’S wonderkids stole the spotlight as Michael Carrick’s side cruised to a 5-0 pre-season win over Rosenborg in Norway.

With the likes of Bruno Fernandes, Amad Diallo and Senne Lammens all absent following their World Cup commitments, it was United’s academy stars who lit up Trondheim with four debut senior goals.



Carrick’s youngsters took full advantage as Shea Lacey, Jacob Devaney, Harry Amass and Ethan Williams all found the net, while Joshua Zirkzee produced a stunning solo strike.

United continued their preparations without the bulk of their World Cup stars, but the next generation showed they are ready to stake their claim ahead of the new campaign.



Fifteen-year-old sensation JJ Gabriel was an unused substitute after dominating the build-up to the game, with Carrick opting not to hand the academy prodigy his senior bow just yet.

Here are Man Utd reporter Katherine Walsh’s match ratings for the first- and second-half XIs…

FIRST HALF

Radek Vitek – 6

The Czech keeper is hunting for a summer exit—whether on loan or permanently—but had zero chance to advertise his talents on an afternoon where he was left with virtually nothing to do.

Leny Yoro – 7

Back out of position at right-back, the French starlet again was solid in the unfamiliar role.



Is Yoro United’s new aerial threat with Casemiro gone? It looked that way when his glancing header smacked off the crossbar on the stroke of half time.

Harry Maguire – 7

Enjoyed a quiet half and was on hand with several brilliant passes through the lines.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Ayden Heaven – 7



Michael Carrick is preparing to hand Heaven a starting spot in defence on opening day, following Lisandro Martinez’s injury in the World Cup final.

The 19-year-old’s best moment came when he intercepted a Rosenborg attack in the box with a well-timed read.

Luke Shaw – 7

Looked lean and lively. Comfortable in possession and strong in the challenge,

Should have offered more in the final third, especially when United piled on the pressure.



Andrey Santos – 8

Another physical 45 minutes and could have had an assist when he delivered a one-time pass into Patrick Dorgu inside the box.

Despite it being his second match, Santos was extremely vocal in the midfield. A clear leader.

Mason Mount – 8

Back in central midfield with plenty of crisp movement and passing between him and Santos.



His link up play with Joshua Zirkzee improved on Wrexham and he closed the space on Rosenborg.

Shea Lacey – 8

Mature beyond his years. It won’t count in the official record books, but his first senior strike was pure class—cutting inside from the right to bury his signature finish.

The 19-year-old was the only academy player on the teamsheet and he didn’t look out of place as the No10.



Patrick Dorgu – 7

Tried to get forward as much as possible on the left wing. He doesn’t have Marcus Rashford‘s feet but Dorgu was involved in good chemistry with Mount and Zirkzee.

Bryan Mbeumo – 7

Looked sharper than he did against Wrexham, treating the near empty ground to a sublime nutmeg and a well-placed cross from a free-kick that Yoro smacked off the woodwork.

He overhit a cross into Lacey before that, but the Cameroonian found some rhythm.



Joshua Zirkzee – 8

Night and day from the Wrexham display. Capitalising on Sesko’s absence, he backed up his promise to fight for his place.

On top of setting up Lacey’s opener and linking brilliantly with Mbeumo, he netted an outrageous solo goal—driving forward and dummying past two defenders and the keeper. Dropped deep in midfield.



SECOND HALF

Jaydan Kamason (replaced Harry Maguire, 45′) – 8

The full-back was a like-for-like change with Shaw and performed brilliantly. Two top level and skilful assists for Amass and Ethan Williams.

Harry Amass (replaced Luke Shaw, 45′) – 8

Involved in a gorgeous delayed one-two with Zirkzee for 2-0. He scored a back post tap in and should be around the first team this season with Shaw the only out-and-out left back in a busier schedule.

Tyler Fletcher (replaced Shea Lacey, 61′) – 6



Lost his man a couple of times but recovered well. Circulated the ball well in possession.

Jacob Devaney (replaced Mason Mount, 61′) – 7

Will be delighted with a first senior goal as he hooked in a corner, albeit unofficial in the record books. He came on at centre-back again; I’m not sure he’s tall enough for it to be permanent.

Sports.content:
Liverpool, Manchester United and Arsenal are all working behind the scenes to strengthen their squads ahead of the new season, while Chelsea are hoping to add more after signing Morgan Rogers

Welcome to Mirror Football's live transfer blog for Saturday, July 25.

With the conclusion of the World Cup, clubs are continuing their preparations for the 2026/27 season. Manchester United look set to put an end to speculation around Bruno Fernandes' future, with the captain agreeing to extend his stay at Old Trafford.

Liverpool have made an approach for Maghnes Akliouche - a player PSG admire but cannot currently afford due to Monaco's demands. The Reds are also leading the chase for Bradley Barcola, a pursuit that threatens to deal another blow to Arsenal, who have been linked with the winger as well.

Chelsea have made the standout Premier League splash so far, sealing a move for Morgan Rogers after paying a £117million fee. Meanwhile, Alejandro Garnacho has departed west London temporarily, joining Aston Villa on loan.

Arsenal have added Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge to their ranks, but it’s their pursuit of Bruno Guimaraes that's dominating the headlines. Newcastle remain firm in their stance that their captain is not for sale - though the question lingers over whether we're heading for a repeat of the Alexander Isak saga.

Follow all of the transfer news, rumours and updates below:

Sports.title: Alan Shearer's stunning daughter weds England star in lavish ceremony
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer's stunning daughter weds England star in lavish ceremony

Alan Shearer's daughter Hollie has married England star Joe Marchant

View 3 Images Alan Shearer's daughter married her rugby star partner in Winchester (Image: Instagram/alanshearer)

Alan Shearer had to rush back from the World Cup to watch daughter Hollie marry her rugby-playing partner. The ex-Newcastle star's second-oldest child tied the knot with England star Joe Marchant in Winchester.

‌



The pair got engaged in November 2024 having dated for two years. Hollie then moved to France with her beau when Marchant signed for Stade Francais.

‌



Shearer had been on co-commentary duties for the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina last weekend. He swiftly returned to the UK to join the celebrations at the Royal Oak in Winchester.

‌



The wedding party enjoyed the festivities in The Royal Oak pub, which was built in 1002.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Alan Shearer calls for major rule change during Spain vs Argentina World Cup final READ MORE :

The Premier League all-time goalscorer shared pictures of Hollie and Joe becoming husband and wife. One snap showed the grinning bride holding her ring up in celebration as her partner signed the documents to make their marriage official.

‌



Another picture, originally posted by Shearer's other daughter Chloe, captured the newlyweds dancing together after they said 'I do.'

3 View 3 Images Hollie cheered as Joe signed their marriage documents (Image: Instagram/alanshearer) 3 View 3 Images Shearer's daughter shared snaps from her hen do in June (Image: Instagram/alanshearer)

Article continues below

Earlier this year, Hollie hinted at the upcoming nuptials by posting her hen do on Instagram. At the time, the bride-to-be donned a white cut-out dress and bikini as she prepared to marry the rugby star.

The outfit choice that stood out to her Instagram followers was a see-through skirt that had 'Mrs Marchant' printed across the back. With the marriage now confirmed, the loved-up pair will likely jet off on honeymoon as Shearer prepares for another Premier League season as a fan-favourite pundit.

Sports.title: Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes transfer offer, Newcastle's statement and pre-season plan
Sports.content:
Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes transfer offer, Newcastle's statement and pre-season plan

Arsenal are pushing to land Bruno Guimaraes but their offer is set to land well short of Newcastle's value as the Magpies push on with their captain being central to their plans

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes has told Newcastle he wants to leave (Image: Getty )

Newcastle will reject Arsenal's £70million bid for Bruno Guimaraes as they continue to fight to keep their captain, according to reports.

‌



The Gunners are increasing their efforts to sign the Brazilian, who has been given a extended period off by the Magpies following his summer involvement in the World Cup. However the player has told the club he wants out of St James' Park.

‌



Contact between Arsenal and Newcastle has been limited as they go through third parties, but the Evening Standard understands their expected offer of £70m will be swiftly turned down with their Premier League rivals not entertaining anything below £80m.

‌



Personal terms are not expected to be an issue for Arsenal as Guimaraes is keen on making the switch to north London, but getting Newcastle to sanction the initial sale is going to prove a challenge as they dig their heels in to retain their captain following a raft of summer exits.

Arsenal news: Newcastle issue Bruno Guimaraes response with agreement close for midfielder READ MORE :

Arsenal have been left without a choice as Mikel Arteta's transfer frustrations clear READ MORE :

Already Newcastle have lost Anthony Gordon, who joined Barcelona after a poor season for the club. That put them under financial pressure to sell and a major name was always likely to exit. However the later departure of Sandro Tonali, who joined Tottenham in a £100m deal, was more of a surprise.

It means in the last 12 months Newcastle have lost Gordon, Tonali and Alexander Isak - who would've been among their three best players previously. Seeing Guimaraes leave would call the ambition of their project into question.

‌



Guimaraes statement of intent

Newcastle though could not have made it more clear that they see their Brazilian star sticking around following their kit launch. He was central during the launch of their new away kit on Thursday in a clear statement of their intent. The unveiling video starts with the words: "What does the future of Newcastle United look like to us?"

View 2 Images The Magpies will be loathed to see another player leave this summer with Sandro Tonali already departing (Image: Getty Images)

The 28-year-old is expected to report for Newcastle training next week and is expected to travel to La Manga for the club's pre-season camp in Spain. Last summer they saw Isak go on strike in a bid to secure his move to Liverpool, but it would be a massive surprise if Guimaraes repeated that trick.

Article continues below

The former Lyon man was signed in the first transfer window of the Saudi-era at Newcastle and has been a driving force behind their subsequent success. Last season he scored nine times in the Premier League - more than any of his team-mates. Arsenal see him as the ideal midfielder to drive them forward to successive titles as they also look to take the last step in Europe.

Sports.title: Liverpool's Yan Diomande transfer hopes hit again as Real Madrid move for RB Leipzig star
Sports.content:
Liverpool's Yan Diomande transfer hopes hit again as Real Madrid move for RB Leipzig star

RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande is a man in demand this summer but after Liverpool and PSG's efforts it looks like Real Madrid are ready to join the race with a mega offer

View 2 Images Yan Diomande is a man in demand this summer (Image: Stuart Franklin/Getty Images)

Real Madrid have come to the party and are looking to sign RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande - with the Spanish giants ready to outbid PSG and Liverpool.

‌



The Ivory Coast winger has been expected to move on all summer, but so far remains on the books of the German side. Now he's back from the World Cup negotiations are set to accelerate and Los Blancos are prepared to stump up more cash than the Parisians.

‌



Diomande has been on Liverpool's radar as they seek out a replacement for Mohamed Salah, but the Leipzig star had made it clear his preference was a move to Paris, where he has agreed a contract according to Sky Germany.

‌



So far the European champions have yet to offer the kind of sum that will convince Leipzig to cash in, but Real are prepared to join the party and the Athletic reports they're ready to outgun both of their rivals financially as they seek a winger who could replace Brahim Diaz.

Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola confirms plan as Maghnes Akliouche reality laid bare READ MORE :

Man Utd drop clearest hint yet over Marcus Rashford's future as club bosses reach out READ MORE :

Liverpool have made an approach for Diomande this summer, but the Bundesliga side are holding out for a mammoth €130million (£111m) before the green light the player's sale. The Reds have also been eyeing PSG's Bradley Barcola, who could've moved on had the French side signed Diomande, which is now in doubt.

Diomande only joined Leipzig a year ago from Spanish side Leganes, but he's proved to be a sensation and the Germans want to achieve a huge profit or tie him down to a new deal. They remain hopeful he will remain at the club beyond the summer window.

‌



“Our clear intention is that Yan Diomande will play for RB Leipzig next year,” the club’s managing director of sport Marcel Shafer said on the winger’s future.

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho has wasted no time bolstering his options (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Diomande featured in all four matches for the Ivory Coast during the World Cup, helping them reach the Round of 32. Last term he scored 12 goals and provided nine assists in 33 Bundesliga matches as Leipzig finished third and returned to the Champions League.

‌



Madrid have been busy during the summer window after confirming the return of Jose Mourinho. Bernardo Silva and Ibrahima Konate have joined on free transfers whilst Denzel Dumfries and Marc Cucurella have also been signed.

If they do indeed choose to pay top dollar for Diomande then Leipzig will have achieve the greatest sale in their history with his move exceeding the fees paid for Benjamin Sekso by Manchester United in 2025 or Josko Gvardiol, who joined Manchester City in 2023.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim's 11-word comment about Man Utd speaks volumes for Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim's 11-word comment about Man Utd speaks volumes for Michael Carrick

Manchester United have already been working hard in the summer transfer window as they prepare for the 2026/27 Premier League season

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has a big job on his hands (Image: MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Ruben Amorim may not be at Manchester United anymore but comments he made 12 months ago will ring true for Michael Carrick now. A simple statement he made about not requiring a huge squad now acts as a warning to the new manager that his current team will need to grow in order to compete.

‌



The new AC Milan boss made the claim while still at the helm at Old Trafford, explaining that the club's absence from Europe last season had at least made his job more manageable. He said: "We always prepare two plans. With and without the Champions League. Without the Champions League, we also don't need a big squad.

‌



"We can control the squad in a better way. Then we have a plan, that is to bring in some new players, but our big plan is to improve the team we have, to improve the Academy.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd and Arsenal locked in £40million transfer battle as duo hold talks over deal READ MORE :

Bruno Fernandes commits future to Manchester United despite new contract wait READ MORE :

"It was the past, so it can be the future. It can't change much because of Financial Fair Play, we are not allowed to do much, even with the Champions League, so we are prepared."

In 2026, Carrick stepped in to replace the sacked Amorim and guided his side to a third-place finish in the Premier League - meaning European football has returned to Old Trafford. As a result, the new manager must now assemble a roster capable of sustaining a challenge across four competitions.

‌



United will compete for trophies in the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup and Carabao Cup. They suffered early exits from both domestic cup competitions last season, and Carrick will be determined to ensure such embarrassing defeats are not repeated.

View 2 Images Carrick will boost his squad this summer (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

The former club captain has been hard at work reshaping his squad ahead of the new campaign. United have already secured the signings of Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Tynan Thompson and Karl Darlow, with further signings expected as they look to build a roster capable of handling the season's demands.

Article continues below

Manu Kone, Rafael Leao, Alex Scott and Lewis Hall have all been touted as potential targets in a list that will undoubtedly expand as the window progresses.

Departures are also on the horizon, with Marcus Rashford, Joshua Zirkzee and Radek Vitek all attracting interest from elsewhere. Carrick will keep Amorim's warning in mind as he sets his sights on delivering silverware to Old Trafford in his first season as permanent manager.

Sports.title: Price: People make it too easy for Littler
Sports.content:
Gerwyn Price insists he can thwart Luke Littler's bid for back-to-back World Matchplay titles and believes some players ‘make it too easy’ for the defending champion.

Price booked his first World Matchplay semi-final since 2022 with a 16-12 win over Ross Smith at the Winter Gardens, where the 'Ice Man' fired a 102.78 average and closed out victory with a four-leg burst.

The Welshman faces world No 3 Gian van Veen in the last four, with the winner of that semi-final progressing to face either Littler or Dutchman Dirk van Duijvenbode in Sunday's best-of-35 leg final.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gerwyn Price produced a series of stunning checkouts to beat a testing Ross Smith and book his place in the last four

Littler defeated Price in every Premier League fixture between them this season and a final-set decider in the World Masters semi-finals, while 'The Nuke' remains unbeaten in PDC major matches over 20 legs since his 2024 World Championship final loss.

The world No 1 remains overwhelming favourite to become the first player since Michael van Gerwen to defend his World Matchplay crown, having posted a 109.57 average in his win over Josh Rock, although Price insists he can be stopped.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler admits he's playing some of the best darts of his career after a dominant World Matchplay quarter-final win over Josh Rock

"I think there's a lot of players that can get to that [Littler's] level," Price told reporters after his quarter-final win.

"Is there anyone who can do it as long as him? I think I can and I think there's a couple of players, but he's ruthless at the minute - these 109, 110 averages just look so easy for him.

"I think some players play into his hand and just let him play with his rhythm. It's horses for courses, and sometimes you have to play your game, you have to play the game and you have to play the moments.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the quarter-final between Luke Littler and Josh Rock at the World Matchplay

"Sometimes, people make it a little bit too easy for him."

More to come in Van Veen showdown?

Price built a commanding 12-8 lead over Smith in a quarter-final where he threatened to pull further ahead, then found himself level at 12-12 until finishing strongly to reach the last four.

Image: Gerwyn Price, World Matchplay Darts 2026

"I was delighted with the way I played the majority of the game, but there's a couple of legs that I let slip and could have come back to haunt me in the end," Price added.

"I'm thinking I should be 13-7 or 14-6 or whatever it is, because I did waste opportunities and probably shouldn't think like that. I'm just happy to get a win, but frustrated a little bit."

Van Veen admitted he needs to improve after his quarter-final victory over 16-13 James Wade, where he posted a 93 average and also blew a four-leg advantage before closing out victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gian van Veen fires in a magnificent 160 checkout to pull away from James Wade to take a 9-6 lead during their quarter-final

"It felt very poor!" Van Veen admitted to Sky Sports. "My scoring was so terrible. I was so lucky James wasn't scoring as well and my finishing got me through. A win is a win.

"The 118 finish - I really needed it. It was a tight battle but I'm glad I got the job done. Hopefully tomorrow I will be a lot better."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gian van Veen edges past James Wade sealing the tie 16-13 and sets up a tantalising World Matchplay semi-final against Gerwyn Price

What's next?

The 2026 Betfred World Matchplay continues at the iconic Winter Gardens on Saturday, with the two semi-finals being played over the best-of-33 to decide who progresses through to Sunday's best-of-35 final.

Defending champion Littler continues his bid for back-to-back titles when he faces Van Duijvenbode, through to the last four at this event for the first time, with Price playing Van Veen in the opening semi-final.

Sports.title: Calandagan and Masquerade Ball headline King George showdown at Ascot
Sports.content:
Calandagan, Masquerade Ball and a Ballydoyle quartet headline a scintillating renewal of the King George from Ascot - live on Sky Sports Racing.

3.35 Ascot - Calandagan and Masquerade Ball among vintage field

A red-hot renewal of this Group 1 King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes sees last year's winner Calandagan headline a field of nine.

Francis-Henri Graffard's stable star finished last season as the world's best racehorse and has followed a similar path this. Having claimed the Dubai Sheema Classic in Meydan, he was beaten on soft ground at Epsom before bouncing back to land the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud. That was a sixth top-level success, and he sets a high standard under Mickael Barzalona.

Last year's Tenno Sho scorer Masquerade Ball was just a head behind Calandagan in the Japan Cup in November and returned with a solid second behind Romantic Warrior in Hong Kong. That was over 10 furlongs, and he will appreciate the extra distance. Doubts remain about his suitability to the track, but there is no doubt he is a top class operator and Japan have high hopes he will be the one to finally end their King George hoodoo.

Kalpana and Goliath are closely matched on their Hardwicke placed efforts, while Aidan O'Brien saddles four runners, headlined by Benvenuto Cellini. A winner of the Irish Derby on his last outing, he ought to have more to offer as he tackles his elders for the first time, with the booking of Ryan Moore potentially telling.

2.55 Ascot - Progressive Mezcala and Extremely Zain fancied

Mezcala and Extremely Zain feature among a field of 17 for this valuable Moet & Chandon International Handicap at 2.55pm.

Extremely Zain arrives unbeaten in three starts, looking a Group horse in the making when readily defying a mark of 93 at York. The handicapper has reacted with an 8lb rise but this is likely to be his last start in handicaps, and he has options from stall eight under Tom Marquand, who replaces Cieren Fallon in the plate.

Image: Extremely Zain returns to action on Saturday

Jack Channon's Mezcala took the Spring Mile earlier in the season and showed a good turn of foot to claim the Buckingham Palace Stakes on his last start. He makes obvious appeal from stall 13 with George Bass in the saddle.

Completely Random was only just denied in the Wokingham over six furlongs here last time and he looks the type to improve for this extra furlong with Ryan Moore a notable booking.

Back In Black and Aalto complete a long shortlist, with the latter effectively 3lb well in after Bunbury Cup victory the last day. The same can be said for Amazing Journey, who steps up in trip after taking top honours in Class 3 handicap company at Ascot when last seen.

2.20 Ascot - Touleen a hot favourite for the Owen Burrows team

An excellent field has assembled for this Group 3 Valiant Stakes, where all eyes will be on Touleen as she drops in class.

Owen Burrows' three-year-old suffered no luck in running when a fast-finishing runner-up in the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot and takes on her elders for the first time with William Buick replacing Saffie Osborne. She's 7lb clear on official ratings and ought to prove hard to beat if granted a clear passage.

Image: Touleen flies the flag for Shadwell this afternoon

Skydance was last seen beating subsequent Oaks heroine Thundering On in a maiden at Leopardstown and this classy filly remains capable of better with the layoff the only slight concern.

Kon Tiki produced a career best when fourth behind Blue Bolt in a strong running of the Duke Of Cambridge at the Royal meeting and she must be respected in this grade.

Sukanya and Esna rate each-way players.

Best of the rest

Ascot also plays host to the Group 3 Princess Margaret Japan Cup Stakes at 1.45pm, with Dark Issue and Alta Regina towards the head of the betting for a classy renewal of this fillies' contest. Moonrise was unlucky not to get her head in front in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot and is also worthy of consideration for the Oisin Murphy and Andrew Balding team.

Blue RC, Urban Lion and Crown Board all line up for the 4.45pm Betfred Handicap, with Asmen Warrior also holding claims for the James Owen team.

Elsewhere, Chester hosts action with Sea Idol the pick of six runners assembled for the IRE Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Maiden Stakes (3.10pm). The feature on the card is the 3.48pm Wilson Family Handicap, with the Wathnan-owned Postmodern fancied to go close for the Hamad Al Jehani.

At Lingfield, Charlie Appleby fields the Godolphin-owned Catching Dreams in the RJB Agri EBF Novice Stakes (7.00pm). This Showcasing colt could go well on debut for a stable on song.

Sports.title: Inter Milan interested in signing Tottenham captain Romero
Sports.content:
Inter Milan are interested in signing Tottenham captain Cristian Romero, according to Sky in Italy.

It is understood that any deal for the Argentina defender would be a financially complex one for the Italian champions.

Inter want to sign a central defender this summer and Romero is one of their targets for the position, along with John Stones, who is a free agent after leaving Manchester City and has interest from Arsenal and Chelsea.

There is an expectation that Spurs would allow Romero to depart this summer if the right offer arrives. He is under contract until 2029.

The 28-year-old missed the end of last season due to a knee injury and received criticism from supporters when he appeared to be set to watch his boyhood club Belgrano play River Plate in the Argentina Primera Division Apertura final instead of being at Tottenham's crucial last game against Everton.

Romero did attend the final game of the season in which Spurs secured Premier League survival.

He has made 124 appearances for the club over five seasons, scoring 12 goals and being shown four red cards in the Premier League.

Inter also want to sign a full-back in this window and Romero's club-mate Djed Spence has been one of their targets.

However, the interest in a move for Spence appears to have lost some momentum of late. He remains on the list, though, along with Monaco's Vanderson and Feyenoord's Givairo Read.

De Zerbi wants two new Tottenham forwards

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi says the club needs to sign two players in attacking positions this summer.

Spurs have already spent £237m on six new signings, smashing their club record by buying Sandro Tonali from Newcastle for £100m, along with £85m on Mateus Fernandes and £52m on Jan Paul van Hecke.

Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi and Martin Dubravka have also joined on free transfers and De Zerbi wants more additions.

"The target now is to complete the attacking positions," he said.

"We want the first target, the first level, because anyway we are already important players, but I think to start the new project we need another couple of important players, for sure."

De Zerbi added: "It's not finished yet, our transfer market window. We have to finish, we have to bring another couple of, maybe more, maybe not less, but a couple of players."

Juventus considering Vicario move

Juventus are once again considering Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario as an alternative to top target Emi Martinez, according to Sky in Italy.

Work has begun to explore the conditions of a potential deal for Parma's Zion Suzuki.

There is currently a gap in valuation, but it is not believed to be big enough to derail the potential transfer as things stand.

Juve intend to revisit their interest in Vicario to strike a deal on the best possible terms for them.

Vicario, who is expected to leave this summer, has not travelled with Spurs on their pre-season tour due to a "minor injury".

In his press conference, Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs boss, said: "Vicario is injured, not a big injury, but he needs to stay one week in London."

De Zerbi: Spurs must find solution for Bergvall

De Zerbi has not spoken to Lucas Bergvall about his future but says Spurs must find a "new solution" for the midfielder if he wants to leave.

Sky Sports News understands the Sweden midfielder is determined to move on this summer. Nottingham Forest remain at the table for him, while Newcastle have also held talks about figures with Spurs.

Sky Sports News has been told there has been no attempt to convince Bergvall to stay at Spurs despite sources at the club insisting they do not want to sell.

De Zerbi has made it clear he only wants players who are happy to be at Spurs in his squad for the coming season.

Asked about speculation with Bergvall and if his inclusion in the pre-season squad is an indication about his future, De Zerbi said: "I have not spoken with Lucas yet. I will in the next days and we will make the best decision for the club, for Lucas, for me, for every one of us. Without problems, Lucas is a big, big talent.

"There will be a big competition to play because at the end, I think we will be two players for each position. If he wants to stay, I will be happy. Otherwise, we have to find a new solution with Johan Lange, with Vinai. It's not my business after the decision to leave."

Kudus 'very close' to returning from injury

De Zerbi also revealed Mohammed Kudus is "very close" to returning to action.

The winger has been out with a muscle issue since early January.

"Kudus is very close," De Zerbi said. "I think when we come back to London he will be available to start working with us. It's a great thing for us. Kudus is another important player."

De Zerbi also gave an update on goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario and Dejan Kulusevski.

"Vicario is injured, not a big injury, but he needs to stay one week in London," he said.

"Kulusevski, we have to see in the next couple of weeks. He's another important player. After one season, one complete season, without a game, we have to analyse better and better, don't take risks, first of all for him and then for us."

Sports.title: Wilkin: Rowley's Saints dismissal doesn't surprise me - 'Fans voted with their feet'
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Rugby League's Jon Wilkin says the departure of St Helens head coach Paul Rowley did not surprise him, saying Saints fans voted with their feet amid a "bizarre time" for the club.

Thursday morning brought news out of nowhere that Rowley had left St Helens with immediate effect, a day before the club's big Super League derby clash away to Wigan which they ultimately lost heavily 38-16.

Indeed, Rowley had already named his squad for the contest, with his sacking at nine months and 23 games, the shortest St Helens coaching stint of all time, and the shortest in English rugby league for over 50 years.

"I'm not surprised," Wilkin, who played for St Helens for 16 years, said. "I think the writing has been on the wall for Paul Rowley at St Helens.

"The most telling thing in Rowley's demise was the attendance for the Catalans game.

"It's a club that struggles commercially to make ends meet and is under all sorts of financial pressure, and when fans vote with their feet, and with the discord and the vitriol which they've shown towards the appointment of Paul Rowley from very early on in the year when he was at the top, the writing's been on the wall.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League match between Wigan Warriors and St Helens

"For me, the fans are just simply not happy with the substance of the team, the personnel of the team, the style of play, and the change in tack from what's been a champion club.

"In 2024, there was an average of 13,000 at home games, and that fell to 11,000 in 2025. And tonight at Wigan, in a stand that holds 5,500, there are only 1,700 in there. Every time I played here, that stand was full.

"It's the lack of engagement with fans. And I think there's a disconnect between players and fans too."

Image: Paul Rowley's timeline in charge at St Helens over nine months

Wilkin: A bizarre time for this great club St Helens | 'I find it desperately sad'

More from Sky Sports Rugby League's Jon Wilkin on the state his former club are in:

"If you think, only nine months into his [Rowley's] tenure, that he can't get a tune out of players and he's got a decimated team, he's had loads of challenges, but if they need to change the coach to get a group of players towards getting into the play-offs, I'm sorry.

"I was at St Helens for 16 years; it's the most un-St Helens thing that I've ever said.

"'We need to change our coach now to get into the play-offs and get our players motivated.' It's a bizarre time at this great club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player St Helens interim head coach Eamon O'Connell was proud of his side despite a heavy loss to rivals Wigan

"It's a shocking position to be in. But I can't imagine they have made this call without making a plan.

"They are making some loose decisions at the minute, that's safe to say.

"They need a big personality, who gets a big club, to excite fans and players.

"I don't like the state St Helens are in. It makes me sad to look at that stand down there in Wigan. For a club that recently won four in a row, I just find it desperately sad."

Tomkins: Timing of Rowley dismissal is 'horrendous' for St Helens

Sky Sports Rugby League's Sam Tomkins said:

"It's the timing. The timing is horrendous.

"The day before a huge game, their play-off hopes sitting in the balance. The day before they play Wigan, they sack the head coach. It's a lot to process, and I'm as stumped as anybody.

"It could be they feel they're going in the wrong direction this year, although they sit in the balance in sixth, and they'll be looking for a big change in terms of performance on the field.

"You very often see it - a coach changes and the players respond, but it's a big gamble. It's just, again, bizarre timing. It blew my mind.

"I'm shocked. I certainly thought Paul Rowley had a little bit more time. Saints have been up and down this year.

Image: Sky Sports Rugby League's Sam Tomkins says the timing of Rowley's departure 'blew his mind'

"I don't think any coach of a top side after 20 weeks into a season, his first season, would decide that's his time to go. It will have been a conversation between club and coach, and they've decided that's the best way to go.

"It would amaze me if Paul Rowley took it on himself to say I want to leave. But we're a results-based business, and I don't think it's Saints have lost too many games this year, I think it's probably the manner in which they've lost at times.

"This is a side that has always made the play-offs. Never once have they missed the play-offs. There is a chance they could slip out of there.

"St Helens have gone: 'We make a decision now that we go in a different direction, and hope the players react to that and performance on the field changes'."

July 23-July 26 Elimination Play-offs: September 19-September 20

Sports.title: French stars as Wigan add to Saints' disarray | 12-player Wakefield rout Tigers
Sports.content:
Super League - Wigan Warriors 38-16 St Helens: Bevan French star of the show as hosts eventually rip Saints apart to cause rivals more disarray

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League match between Wigan Warriors and St Helens Highlights of the Super League match between Wigan Warriors and St Helens

Bevan French proved the star of the show on his return as Wigan Warriors eventually ripped St Helens apart 38-16 in Friday's Super League, compounding Saints' woes.

St Helens, who came into this derby contest off the back of the shock news on Thursday that head coach Paul Rowley had departed with immediate effect, actually started well, taking the lead twice in the opening 15 minutes through Jack Welsby and Jacob Douglas tries.

French had scored for Wigan in between those two efforts, and the Australian then created two tries for Zach Eckersley before the break for the hosts to lead: the first try via a fizzed cut-out pass, the second off a wonderful kick-pass.

Bevan French scored one try and assisted four more as Wigan Warriors saw off St Helens on Friday

Saints had a potential equalising try ruled out by the Video Ref in the final play of the first half, with replays proving remarkable defence from Jake Wardle had halted Harry Robertson from grounding the ball.

Instead, Wigan went into overdrive in the second half, scoring through Oliver Partington twice and the in-form Adam Keighran - French collecting two more assists, while Harry Smith also produced a sensational kick-pass for Partington's second.

St Helens had the final say through a Lewis Murphy try, but remain outside of the play-off positions and under a wealth of pressure.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 'He's at the heart of everything!' | French sets up Eckersley try with SUPERB kick 'He's at the heart of everything!' | French sets up Eckersley try with SUPERB kick

Welsby: Our performances let Rowley down

St Helens' Jack Welsby told Sky Sports:

"A bit disappointed by the loss, we were right in the game at half-time.

"We just didn't start well in the second half. With everything going on, we can be proud of our efforts but ultimately this is a game we came to win. But we lost by quite a big margin in a Saints vs Wigan derby, so the overriding feeling is disappointment.

"We reacted to the news about Paul Rowley as best as we could. We found out yesterday and then did a training session and a captain's run.

"The senior boys nailed it and the younger lads didn't need an invitation to follow. Tough news to take, a lot of us are gutted and embarrassed, really, because we've let him down. There are some things to hold onto from the first half, but we've got a lot to improve on if we want to make the play-offs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player St Helens stun Wigan again as Jacob Douglas goes over for his second of the night St Helens stun Wigan again as Jacob Douglas goes over for his second of the night

"Our performances let him down, he doesn't go on the pitch and play. I'm sure if we'd have won as many games as Wigan had, he wouldn't be getting sacked.

"We always have to look inwards before looking outwards, as a playing group particularly, so it's a good time to reflect on that this weekend.

"We've got to come together [if we want to make the play-offs]. The group's been together all year but now, more than ever, we're going to need a strong bond."

O'Carroll: I'm proud of my team | 'Saints now in strong position'

St Helens interim coach Eamon O'Carroll told Sky Sports:

"Proud. A little bit lost for words too. I asked the boys to stick together all week, give us effort and intent.

"I can't question any of them. They gave it in bucketloads. I'm really proud of the group for how they've handled this week and although it might sound daft, I think we're in a strong position now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player St Helens interim head coach Eamon O'Connell is still proud of his side despite a heavy loss to their rivals Wigan St Helens interim head coach Eamon O'Connell is still proud of his side despite a heavy loss to their rivals Wigan

"We will build game-by-game. Our preparation is going to be really important. It's not just about producing that in the game, it's about how we turn up in the week.

"We've got a few busted bodies there, so we have to get them right and give the lads every opportunity to perform at the best.

"It's my job to keep us focused on the here and now and let's worry about the process.

"Let's worry about the process. The next challenge is how we turn up tomorrow and Monday, in how we turn up against York."

Peet: Elements of our performance weren't acceptable

Wigan Warriors head coach Matt Peet to Sky Sports:

"I'm not sure, I'm pleased with the win against our greatest rivals.

"There's elements of our performance that could be better but tonight shows how far we have come as a group. It was an important win, but we know we can be better.

"At times we didn't respect the ball and it got a little bit loose. St Helens were more desperate at certain points and that's a credit to them. They made a game of it, but fortunately we come away with two points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matt Peat admitted he wants to see more from his Wigan side despite a big victory over their rivals St Helens Matt Peat admitted he wants to see more from his Wigan side despite a big victory over their rivals St Helens

"I'm talking about our processes, our standards, and the way we want to play. There's elements of tonight that we'll all agree weren't acceptable, there's reasons for that. Like I say, we've got to be better than that.

"We've got to practice hard. The lads will be aware of it when they see it back. There was a looseness in the game, I'm not sure why. It won't be me driving that, the players will want to improve."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oliver Partington gets his second of the night to extend Wigan's lead Oliver Partington gets his second of the night to extend Wigan's lead

French: I've just kept positive mindset through injury setbacks

Player of the match Bevan French told Sky Sports:

"It was great! I think I just had a sense of gratitude and appreciation.

"It's been a great year with the time that I've had off the field. But I've just tried to stay in a positive mindset. In the week leading up to it I've just been enjoying it and lucky it was against St Helens. Just appreciative.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wigan were not behind for long as Bevan French finished off a lovely move to respond perfectly to the strong start from St Helens Wigan were not behind for long as Bevan French finished off a lovely move to respond perfectly to the strong start from St Helens

"The young boys stepped up. We're really blessed with the youth that's coming through. It's great to be a part of this club, seeing everyone grow and become the players they want to be. It's a good place to be.

"We're just striving to be better every day, every year. We're going to have hiccups along the way, we've had plenty throughout this year and we're still here."

Castleford Tigers routed by 12-player Wakefield Trinity

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League match between Wakefield Trinity and Castleford Tigers Highlights of the Super League match between Wakefield Trinity and Castleford Tigers

Tom Johnstone and Lachlan Walmsley scored doubles as 12-player Wakefield ran in nine tries to demolish shell-shocked West Yorkshire derby rivals Castleford 52-14.

The hosts looked to be in trouble at the DIY Kitchens Stadium when they trailed 10-6 after Matty Storton's early dismissal, but they turned in a rampant display to clinch a sixth successive Super League win.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Wakefield were ahead inside 45 seconds of kick-off when Johnstone found space down the left and drew his man before slipping the ball inside to Storton to cross before Max Jowitt added the conversion.

Despite then looking like things would take a turn against Tigers when down a player, Trinity turned on the style for a big win to move them second in the standings, above Wigan on points difference.
