Sports.title: Premier League: club-by-club guide to transfer business so far – and what they still need
Sports.content:
Arsenal

For once, Mikel Arteta is not spending his summer looking for a No 9. Instead the champions have moved to strengthen out wide after the departure of Leandro Trossard with Christos Tzolis arriving for £24m having scored 33 league goals in his last two seasons from Club Brugge’s left wing. After missing out on Morgan Rogers to Chelsea, they will not want to be beaten to Alex Scott’s signature. Defensive cover will probably be necessary after the injury to William Saliba at the World Cup. Billy Munday

Major ins Piero Hincapié (Bayer Leverkusen, £45m, after loan), Christos Tzolis (Club Brugge, £34m) Major outs Leandro Trossard (Besiktas, £15.3m), Jakub Kiwior (Porto, £14.5m)

Aston Villa

It is a very busy summer of comings and goings at Villa Park. Alejandro Garnacho is primed to swap places with Morgan Rogers and there is still scope for Emiliano Martínez to leave, forcing their hand in goal, and Arsenal’s interest in Ezri Konsa is not going away. Striker is another position without guarantees, with Nicolas Jackson one option, especially if Fenerbahce’s interest in Ollie Watkins becomes something more concrete. A left-back to replace the departing Lucas Digne is a must, while Leon Bailey is available for transfer and could head to Hull. Will Unwin

Major ins Johan Manzambi (Freiburg, £51m), João Gomes (Wolves, £34m) Major outs Morgan Rogers (Chelsea, £117m), Youri Tielemans (Manchester United, £35m), Donyell Malen (Roma, £21.6m)

Bournemouth

Plenty will depend on Alex Scott and whether he stays or goes, with interest in the midfielder, who has turned down a new contract, from Chelsea, Manchester United and Arsenal. Regardless of that, Benfica’s António Silva is lined up to replace Marcos Senesi, while the search is continuing for a right-back. With a first season in the Europa League ahead, planning accordingly to ensure the squad is sufficiently robust to cope with a more hectic schedule than usual is paramount. WU

Major ins Álvaro Rodríguez (Elche, £21.4m) Major outs Luis Sinisterra (Cruzeiro, £5.2m)

Brentford

Usually a big sale pushes the Bees into action but not this summer. Experience has been on the agenda, with Jaidon Anthony and Callum Wilson acquired, while the arrival of the young centre-back Jannik Schuster could mean the end of Ethan Pinnock’s time with the club. They are, as always, likely to look at bringing in players with potential. The Manchester United teenager Noah Ajayi falls into this category but whether a deal progresses remains to be seen. WU

Major ins Jaidon Anthony (Burnley, £15m), Jannik Schuster (Red Bull Salzburg, £14m), Callum Wilson (West Ham, free)

Brighton

Investing in the defence early has freed up time to do other critical business, with a central midfield refresh potentially in the offing, while there is a desire to bolster the winger bullpen. Evan Ferguson is back at the club after a loan spell at Roma but whether he has a future at the club remains to be seen. If not, finding suitable support for the 35-year-old Danny Welbeck will be part of the strategy with the a Conference League campaign awaiting. Bart Verbruggen has attracted interest in Europe and a departure would call for a new No 1 to be found. WU

Major ins Luka Vuskovic (Tottenham, £46m), Zadok Yohanna (AIK, £21.5m), Pascal Struijk (Leeds United, £18m), Costinha (Olympiakos, 11m) Major outs Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham, £52m), Diego Coppola (Paris FC, £15.3m), James Milner (retired), Solly March (released)

Chelsea

Marc Cucurella’s sale has left a hole to fill at left-back. Options there include a return for Newcastle’s Lewis Hall or a move for Rayo Vallecano’s Pep Chavarría. The midfield is also looking light with Andrey Santos out the door and Enzo Fernández linked with a move away. The reluctance to sign a goalkeeper suggests 20-year-old Mike Penders is not far from competing for the No 1 spot. The capture of Morgan Rogers will excite supporters, but they still crave a top centre-back and striker. BM

Major ins Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa, £117m), Marco Palestra (Atalanta, £47m), Geovany Quenda (Sporting, £40m), Emmanuel Emegha (Strasbourg, £21.6m) Major outs Marc Cucurella (Real Madrid, £52m), Andrey Santos (Manchester United, £50m), Tyrique George (Everton, £18m)

View image in fullscreen England attacker Morgan Rogers is an exciting signing for Chelsea. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

Coventry

Without putting too fine a point on it, quality across the board is required. The club are still working on bringing the Brighton goalkeeper Carl Rushworth back after a successful loan in the Championship but price and competition for his signature will complicate matters. Finding strikers capable of converting chances will be integral to their chances of survival for Frank Lampard’s side. Norman Bassette has returned to Belgium after spending last season out of loan. WU

Major ins Loum Tchaouna (Burnley, £20m), Aurèle Amenda (Eintracht Frankfurt, £15.4m), Frank Onyeka (Brentford, undisclosed fee)

Crystal Palace

Making sure Maxence Lacroix, Jean-Philippe Mateta and Adam Wharton are still at the club come kick-off is imperative. Chelsea’s interest in Lacroix and Wharton will cause the most concern, while extending Mateta’s deal beyond the end of the season will need to be addressed. The starting lineup is strong but greater depth, with another European campaign in the offing, is imperative for the club. Óscar Mingueza was a sensible signing on a free, especially after not replacing Marc Guéhi in January. Walter Benítez may leave in search of first-team football, which would leave a gap in the goalkeeping department. WU

Major ins Óscar Mingueza (Celta Vigo, free)

Everton

Young, developing potential has been recruited so far in the form of Hayden Hackney – player of the season in the Championship with Middlesbrough in 2025-26 – Tyrique George and Merlin Röhl, the last two after loan spells with David Moyes’s side last season. But established players are still required to fill several weak spots, especially at right-back, a position that has needed strengthening for far too long now, and centre-forward. Left-back, central midfield and another wide player – the return of Jack Grealish possibly – would also be on the wishlist. Andy Hunter

Major ins Tyrique George (Chelsea, £18m), Merlin Röhl (Freiburg, £17.3m), Hayden Hackney (Middlesbrough, £16.5m) Major outs Séamus Coleman (released)

Fulham

It is a new era at Craven Cottage under Álvaro Arbeloa and there is much work to be done. The loss of Raúl Jiménez and, more important, the player of the season, Harry Wilson, means there are holes to fill. Like a year ago, it’s been a slow start to the window and things will need to speed up if they are to find a new striker, winger and a centre-back. Real Madrid’s Franco Mastantuono and Gonzalo García are under consideration, having previously worked with Arbeloa. WU

Major ins Jonah Kusi-Asare (Bayern Munich, £5.2m) Major outs Issa Diop (Ipswich, £8.5m), Harry Wilson (Leeds, free), Raúl Jiménez (Wolves, free)

View image in fullscreen Leeds signing Harry Wilson excelled last season for Fulham. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

Hull

After avoiding an expected six-point deduction for breaching spending rules by selling the goalkeeper Ivor Pandur and the midfielder Aidon Shehu to Rangers and Panathinaikos respectively for a combined £8.5m at the end of June, the playoff winners aim to make 10-12 new signings before September. Reinforcements are required all over the pitch, with central defence, central midfield and attack particular priorities. “Think about us like a volcano,” says Hull’s owner, Acun Ilicali. “It’s boiling right now and it’s going to erupt.” Yet as much as the manager, Sergej Jakirovic, needs new faces he will be anxious to retain last season’s exceptionally powerful team spirit. Inspired loans and free transfer imports could prove crucial. Louise Taylor

Major ins Jack Butland (Rangers, £3.5m) Major outs Ivor Pandur (Rangers, £6m)

Ipswich

Promotion brings enough problems but doing so with a new manager brings added complexity as Gary O’Neil seeks to shape his squad. The aim is to be better prepared for the Premier League than last time by signing those with the physicality to compete in the top flight, preferably having done so before, hence the signing of Issa Diop. Inroads have been made but the spine of the team needs strengthening, especially in midfield and at centre-forward. WU

Major ins Emersonn (Toulouse, £24m), Abdul Fatawu (Leicester, £20m), Issa Diop (Fulham, £8.5m), Chuba Akpom (Ajax, £7m) Major outs Arijanet Muric (Sassuolo, £6m)

Leeds

Daniel Farke has traditionally preferred to operate with a small, closely bonded, first-team squad but acknowledges a little expansion is required. As the defender Joe Rodon recently put it: “We want to make our squad bigger and better.” So far, though, the goalkeeping department has shrunk appreciably, with Karl Darlow and Illan Meslier having left while Lucas Perri is coveted by Torino. If new keepers currently top Farke’s shopping list – and Manchester City’s and England’s James Trafford in particular – the Southampton central midfielder Shea Charles is not far behind. Leeds seem determined to acquire the 22-year-old but the Champonship club are reluctant sellers who will demand top dollar. With Harry Wilson and Tarik Muharemovic having already arrived to reinforce attack and central defence respectively, considerable focus is on midfield where Julian Brandt, a free agent after leaving Borussia Dortmund, is also coveted. LT

Major ins Tarik Muharemovic (Sassuolo, £34.1m), Harry Wilson (Fulham, free) Major outs Pascal Struijk (Brighton, £18m), Karl Darlow (Manchester United, free)

Liverpool

Arne Slot wanted two new wingers and a right-back before he was sacked in May and the change of head coach has not changed Liverpool’s priorities. Victor Muñoz has been signed as a versatile forward but not as an immediate starter under Andoni Iraola, and the pursuit of top wide talent continues. Bradley Barcola and Yan Diomande are of interest, although Paris Saint-Germain may determine both their futures. Iraola is concerned at the thinness of his defensive options and, while in an ideal world he would consider Conor Bradley to be Liverpool’s first-choice right back, the Northern Irishman’s recovery from a serious knee injury is likely to force another transfer move. AH. AH

Major ins Jérémy Jacquet (Rennes, £55m), Víctor Muñoz (Osasuna, £34.5m) Major outs Mohamed Salah (released), Ibrahima Konaté (Real Madrid, free), Andy Robertson (Tottenham, free)

View image in fullscreen England midfielder Elliot Anderson has completed his move to Manchester City. Photograph: Nathan Ray Seebeck/Imagn Images/Reuters

Manchester City

Elliot Anderson may already have joined for a British record transfer fee but City are still in the market for another midfielder, with the 18-year-old Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi being targeted for about £85m. Enzo Maresca also has Malo Gusto, one of his right-backs when he was Chelsea head coach, on the radar. A striker will be on the list, too, if Omar Marmoush leaves. And with Real Madrid retaining an interest, will Rodri sign on again? Spain’s World Cup-winning captain has a year left on his contract and his stock has rocketed. The incomings mean several players could leave, with Kalvin Phillips, Jack Grealish, Tijjani Reijnders, Nico González, Savinho and James Trafford among them. Jamie Jackson

Major ins Elliot Anderson (Nottingham Forest, £116m), Mathys Detourbet (Troyes, £21.6m), Jeremy Monga (Leicester, £12.5m) Major outs Nathan Aké (Fenerbahce, £7m), Bernardo Silva (Real Madrid, free), John Stones (free agent)

Manchester United

Michael Carrick is keen to add a third new midfielder after the arrivals of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, with Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavinga, Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, Roma’s Manu Koné and Fulham’s Sander Berge on the list. He is also considering a move for a left-back: Newcastle’s Lewis Hall and Fulham’s Antonee Robinson are being monitored. There will be outgoings too. At 28 Marcus Rashford is in his prime and available, surely for a fee in the same region as the £26m Barcelona balked at. Player and club want an exit yet at the moment he will start the new season at United. For the right deal this will change. JJ

Major ins Andrey Santos (Chelsea, £50m), Youri Tielemans (Aston Villa, £35m) Major outs Rasmus Højlund (Napoli, £43.2m)

Newcastle

Much hinges on whether Bruno Guimarães stays or departs for Arsenal during a summer already featuring a significant changing of the St James’ Park guard. The adjustment to life after Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali could be eased if Eddie Howe is able to attract a higher calibre central midfielder – Monaco’s Aladji Bamba has joined for £34m – and goalkeeper – Parma’s Zion Suzuki is one possibility. Most signings will be expected to conform to Newcastle’s new transfer policy of recruiting players aged 24 and under, with a valuation broadly between £20m and £40m. Meanwhile Nick Pope, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy could depart. The club are operating under a three-year Uefa settlement agreement after breaching European spending rules but Howe’s overriding current priority is keeping Guimarães. LT

Major ins Bazoumana Touré (Hoffenheim, £43m), Ewen Jaouen (Reims, £21.6m), Sean Steur (Ajax, £20m), Aladji Bamba (Monaco, £34m) Major outs Sandro Tonali (Tottenham, £92.5m), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona, £69.3m), Kieran Trippier (Wolves, free)

Nottingham Forest

Spending the money made from the Elliot Anderson sale is a top priority. Lucas Bergvall leads the list of replacements and the midfielder has told Tottenham his preference is to move to the City Ground but a deal needs to be agreed. If not, Monaco’s Lamine Camara could become part of the thinking. A new right-wingback and striker are also being plotted, with Sporting’s Ousmane Diomande a target in central defence. There is no requirement to sell any key players but the futures of some on the fringes are up in the air. WU

Major outs Elliot Anderson (Manchester City, £116m)

Sunderland

Régis Le Bris says he is hoping to add “six or seven” new players this summer. Sunderland’s manager wants to ensure the squad is sufficiently robust to cope with the twin demands of Premier League and Europa League campaigns but has been bolstered by Granit Xhaka’s decision to recommit to the club amid interest in the captain from Chelsea. If recruiting holding midfield cover for Xhaka is one transfer priority, so too is providing Brian Brobbey with high-calibre attacking competition while also fortifying the right-winger and left-back positions. Le Bris is under no pressure to sell, so any attempts to acquire his increasingly influential attacking midfielder Enzo Le Fée will be strongly resisted. LT

Major ins Thomas Meunier (Lille, free) Major outs Eliezer Mayenda (Rennes, £17.1m)

Tottenham

Despite acquiring a new central midfield and a new central defence, Roberto De Zerbi said Spurs are “not finished yet” in the transfer market. An upgrade on Richarlison up front should be a priority, while Marcus Rashford could be a blockbuster arrival out wide. As for outgoings, Cristian Romero and Lucas Bergvall could follow Luka Vuskovic and Will Lankshear through the door. Interest in Pedro Porro will be high after his outstanding World Cup and there is still uncertainty over Guglielmo Vicario’s future in goal. BM

Major ins Sandro Tonali (Newcastle, £92.5m), Mateus Fernandes (West Ham, £85m), Jan Paul van Hecke (Brighton, £52m), Andy Robertson (Liverpool, free), Martin Dubravka (Burnley, free) Major outs Luka Vuskovic (Brighton, £46m), Radu Dragusin (Fiorentina, loan)

Sports.title: Jürgen Klopp vows to change Germany but threatens to quit if family hounded by media
Sports.content:
Jürgen Klopp said he wants his team to “change a country” after being confirmed as Germany’s new head coach, but threatened to stand down if his family are hounded by the media during his time in charge.

In a forthright first press conference upon his unveiling as Julian Nagelsmann’s replacement, Klopp also suggested the role will be his final job in top-level football and expressed regret after poking fun at his predecessor while working as a television pundit during the World Cup. He is tasked with reviving Germany, who lost to Paraguay in the last 32 and have not made the last 16 since winning the tournament in 2014.

It marks a return to the dugout for Klopp two years after leaving Liverpool, where he ended a glorious nine-season tenure after explaining he felt fatigued. Since January 2025 he has worked as head of global soccer for Red Bull but a comeback to frontline action had appeared inevitable since Nagelsmann departed on 3 July.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp was in forthright mood in his first press conference as Germany head coach. Photograph: Hannes Albert/EPA

Klopp vowed to transform a deeply fractured relationship between the national team and Germany’s public, citing his work at Liverpool as an example of the way football can galvanise a wider community.

“I want to create a situation where fans go home after the game and say: ‘Wow, that was cool,’” he said. “I want people to say: ‘Wow, it was worth putting the TV on for 90 minutes to see Germany play.’ I’ve lived and experienced how football can change a city. And I think it’s not only about cities, it’s also about the country. Ideally, football can change a country.”

The 59-year-old’s contract will run until after the 2030 World Cup. Klopp, however, warned that he would not tolerate invasive treatment from journalists and that he would be prepared to depart without compensation if he felt his family’s privacy had been violated.

“I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you treated Nagelsmann,” he said. “I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you’ve treated, in England, Thomas Tuchel. The day you don’t want me any more, I’m gone, without any severance pay. If you say tomorrow: ‘He’s shit,’ tell me to my face and I’m out. If you behave badly and don’t leave my family in peace, I’m gone, I’ll just turn away.

“Criticise me if something doesn’t work. Jürgen Klopp is not going to have any career after the national team. This is the pinnacle of my career as a coach. I will give it everything I’ve got.”

Klopp was criticised last month when, speaking with the former Germany player Thomas Müller on television during coverage of the group stage match with Curaçao, he appeared to hint Nagelsmann’s days were numbered by saying he was “still” picking the team. That was followed by a quick apology; Klopp repeated the sentiment on Friday and said the pair have yet to speak since his appointment was confirmed.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp, in his role as Magenta TV pundit, with Kylian Mbappé after France’s World Cup quarter-final against Morocco. Photograph: Greg M Cooper/EPA

“We haven’t had any exchange,” he said, wishing Nagelsmann a happy 39th birthday for Thursday. “It was a joke. In retrospect it was one of the worst ‘funny’ remarks I have ever made. I feel awfully sorry, I’ve apologised a million times.

“It was just a rash thing to say, with no ulterior motive whatsoever, and I can only wish him the best.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Now he can go on to pastures new and I’m absolutely sure he will have many opportunities to coach a big team in future.”

Klopp promised Germany will play expansive football with wingers but admitted they must find their own way to compete with the depth of talent available elsewhere. “Success is performance relative to expectations,” he said. “When we ask in Germany: ‘Are we as good as France?’ and the answer is no, that’s not true. If we ask: ‘Do we have players like Dembélé, Mbappé, Doué and Barcola?’, no we don’t, but we can still beat them.

“We don’t want to play like Argentina, Spain, England or France. We want to do it the German way, very intense. Are we the No 1 team right now? No, we accept that. There are 11 teams ahead of us in the ranking. We can beat them, but for this to happen we need to play very good, very intense football.”

International football will demand a change of rhythm for Klopp after a lifetime spent in the domestic game. “I think contact with a team is not necessarily about working with them day in, day out,” he said. “Sometimes it will be 30 minutes or an hour and that will be on the pitch. But all of them have a mobile. I’ll talk to them, listen to them, watch games and give my feedback. That, too, is developing players and making them better.”

Klopp’s reign will begin with a ­baptism of fire in Amsterdam against the Netherlands on 24 September, one of four Nations League games in the space of 11 days. “The players have to show me, and not just say it, that playing for Germany is a super special thing,” he said.

Sports.title: ‘You need to evolve’: Enzo Maresca plots life after Pep at Manchester City
Sports.content:
Relaxed and tanned, Enzo Maresca offered a warm note with his first words to the media as the manager of Manchester City, who must somehow follow the generational Pep Guardiola. “Before we start, I would like to send a message and a big hug to Kevin Keegan’s family for this moment,” said the Italian in tribute to a football legend, following his death on Monday.

Keegan, of course, was a former City manager who had at Newcastle famously locked horns with Sir Alex Ferguson when he led Manchester United, the fierce rivals of Maresca’s new team. When the 46-year-old, sat on the dais occupied for 10 mostly glittering years by Guardiola, offered an unsolicited reference to Ferguson – and Arsène Wenger – you could see he comprehended the mammoth task before him.

How do you follow the man who claimed 20 trophies in a decade and who ranks alongside Ferguson? Well, by mentioning, and so trying to tame, the elephant in the room. “The history of the manager with many years in the same club always struggled a little bit. After Sir Alex, after Arsène,” Maresca said. “But also, it’s a challenge to try to do the right things immediately for this organisation, for the fans, for everyone.”

Speaking in front of a giant “Welcome back Enzo” billboard, a reference to his previous leading of City’s elite development squad in 2020-21 as well as his stint as Guardiola’s assistant manager in the 2022-23 treble season, Maresca would have been aware the font of goodwill will not prove deep if results go south. Certainly not from that most fickle of constituencies – fans. So Maresca cutely pointed to the patience of City’s chairman, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, and his executive. “This club has had three managers in 17 years,” he said. “This is not normal, so this is one of the things that I’m confident we can do a great job and continue to do the job that has been done in the last years. Roberto [Mancini] was here, then Manuel [Pellegrini] and then Pep – for 10 years.”

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca with Pep Guardiola at a June 2023 Manchester City training session. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

Mancini’s tenure began in December 2009, ended with his sacking in May 2013, and was angst-ridden: anathema to al-Mubarak and his chief executive, Ferran Soriano. If Mancini could be volatile, Pellegrini proved serene, and Guardiola was, simply, a genius. Al-Mubarak’s and Soriano’s experience of Maresca during his two previous seasons at City obviously convinced them that he is the full package: an accomplished football man who is of equable character.

Yet Maresca’s exit from his previous post at Chelsea on New Year’s Day ended with an apology from him, and City paying the west London club £17m in compensation. Maresca’s shutters came down for the first – and only – time when his conduct was raised. “I feel quite lucky in terms of my former clubs – Leicester, Chelsea – I think we did a great job,” he said. “In both clubs, the identity of the team was clear, the success of the team was clear, and I feel very lucky to be part of these clubs. But now we are here today. That is the most important thing, just about City. And nothing to add.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Maresca made Leicester Championship champions and the next season took Chelsea to fourth in the Premier League and a Conference League triumph before claiming the Fifa Club World Cup last summer, a 3-0 evisceration of Paris Saint-Germain in the final a calling card that may well have sealed the City job.

He talked of “titles” for the coming season. To aid this mission, Maresca has Elliot Anderson, a £116m buy from Nottingham Forest, to patrol midfield, and potentially Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, who shone for Morocco at the World Cup, to further bolster this department. He also retains an interest in Malo Gusto, one of his right-backs when at Chelsea, and if Omar Marmoush leaves, the market will be entered for a similar, pacy forward.

One player Maresca certainly does not wish to lose is the peerless Rodri, who lifted the World Cup for Spain on Sunday and received the Golden Ball, and whose control of a contest in the ever-more frantic domestic game is priceless. The 30-year-old will have surgery on a back problem on Monday. The word is it is not too serious, though he will miss out when City host Bournemouth on the opening weekend of the season. The more important date is 1 September, when the transfer window closes: will Real Madrid have made a move for a footballer who has a year left on his terms and is declining to sign the new deal offered by City?

Of more immediate concern for Maresca is flying out on Tuesday for a pre‑season tour of Asia that features matches with Inter in Hong Kong and K-League All Stars and Atlético Madrid in Seoul. For the trip Maresca will have back City’s A-listers who exited the World Cup early, including Josko Gvardiol, Mateo Kovacic and Abdukodir Khusanov.

View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson was a key player for England at the World Cup and was Manchester City’s first signing of the summer. Photograph: Marta Lavandier/AP

“I’m working at the moment with many young players,” he said. “That is always good because they are full of energy and some of them are very good. The last group of players are going to join three or four days before the Community Shield and we will have all the squad.” After that Cardiff game with Arsenal on Sunday 16 August, the bid to successfully succeed Guardiola begins in earnest.

“You need to adapt, evolve,” Maresca added in reference to his playing style. “Set pieces, man to man – it’s a little bit the direction where football is going. We managers, it’s our duty to find solutions.” We are about to discover how good he is at this.

Sports.title: Dismissed solicitor is still acting for footballers in brain injury court case
Sports.content:
The solicitor dismissed by a group of over 1,000 rugby players with brain injuries who are suing the sport’s governing bodies is still leading a similar claim on behalf of dozens of former footballers.

Richard Boardman told a hearing at the Royal Courts of Justice this week of his intention to “come off the record,” with the claimants indicating that they had unanimously agreed to terminate their dealings with his firm, Rylands Garth.

Boardman’s management of the case was strongly criticised by the presiding judge, Master Jeremy Cook, who highlighted alleged “widespread non-compliance” and “misleading evidence,” with particular regard to his failure to make good on a pledge to provide the court with all of the claimants’ medical records.

Master Cook is now considering whether to strike off the case entirely, which would leave a large cohort of former union and league players including England World Cup winners Steve Thompson and Phil Vickery with nothing to show for six years of gruelling legal battles.

Despite being dismissed by the rugby players however, Boardman is still acting on behalf of a group of 23 former footballers who are suing the Football Association, English Football League and FA of Wales as a result of permanent brain injuries sustained during their careers.

The group includes the families of World Cup hero Nobby Stiles, former Newcastle manager Joe Kinnear and four former players from the Premier League era. With a far smaller number of claimants, and as a result fewer medical records, the football case is seen as more manageable for Rylands Garth.

Coincidentally, the FA changed their defence team in the case earlier this year and both parties remain in the process of exchanging documents.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The rugby claimants are in the process of appointing new solicitors, but until they have done so Boardman remains notionally in charge despite being absent from court for the last day and a half of hearings this week. The firm Leigh Day has been consulting on the case since February and is considering whether to take it on.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola backs backroom staff to help cure Liverpool’s set-piece ills
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has outlined the roles his backroom staff will play in trying to improve Liverpool’s set-piece record next season and admitted he was “very lucky” to inherit a talented coaching team at Bournemouth.

Iraola has brought several members of his Bournemouth backroom team with him to Liverpool since succeeding Arne Slot last month. Tommy Elphick, a boyhood Liverpool fan, and Shaun Cooper have joined as first-team coaches while Iraola’s long-time colleague Pablo de la Torre has arrived as assistant coach. Alejandro Rosalen has taken over as first-team goalkeeping coach after five years with Napoli.

Iraola worked alongside De la Torre in his first coaching job at AEK Larnaca, and again at Rayo Vallecano, and said having trusted confidants alongside him would be invaluable for his first season in charge at Anfield. “For me, it was important they came with me,” said Iraola, who will take charge of his first Liverpool game on Saturday in a pre-season friendly against Sunderland in Nashville. “Pablo is a physical coach but has been with me almost all the years I have been coaching. So, for me, he is much more than a physical coach really. He is an assistant and we know each other very well.

“I was very lucky with Tommy and Shaun when I arrived at Bournemouth. Because I was unlucky to have the issue with my assistant coach Iñigo Pérez [who was denied a work permit when attempting to follow Iraola from Rayo Vallecano to Bournemouth]. After, it worked out very well for him because now he is coaching Villarreal. Maybe we play him in the Champions League.

“But when I had Tommy and Shaun there, we did not feel the need to bring in another assistant. They were very prepared, they were very helpful for me in terms of understanding the English culture, the mentality of the players, what they were used to, what they like in training, even the small details that maybe in Spain are different. Also the experience Tommy has at Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brighton, Huddersfield; they can be in a closer position to the players. They can feel more identified. I am a little bit older. Some of the players maybe didn’t know I was a player.”

One requirement for Iraola and his backroom staff will be to address Liverpool’s problems at set pieces. Only Bournemouth (26), Crystal Palace (25) and Leeds (24) conceded more set-piece goals than Liverpool’s 23 in what proved Slot’s final season as head coach, having won the title in his first. “They are very good coaches,” said Iraola. “We kind of ­understand the game similarly and they have different roles in the coaching staff, they help with set pieces also. That’s the reason I continued with them.

“Tommy does defensive set plays, Shaun does more offensive, more ­creative ones. But also we are working very well here with the set-piece analyst [Lewis Mahoney], who was very good in the second half of last season. He is already with the club, so they are working on some stuff.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Manchester United and the quest to make mythical midfield a reality
Sports.content:
MIDDLE MEN

Like the urban myth that you are never more than three feet away from a spider, modern footballing lore tells us Manchester United are only ever three signings away from a Premier League title challenge. With the Geopolitics World Cup in the rear-view mirror and the transfer news machine churning once more, you may have missed United being linked with just about every midfielder to ever grace a centre circle. They missed out on Elliot Anderson – who went and dubbed his new club the “kings of Manchester” – and were fooled into thinking they could snare Aurélien Tchouaméni. They danced briefly with Atalanta’s Éderson, before landing on Chelsea resale project prospect Andrey Santos and former Aston Villa linchpin Youri Tielemans. And United aren’t done with their midfield overhaul – rightly so given they have lost Casemiro to Inter Miami and Manuel Ugarte to long-term knee knack. Next up on United’s extensive longlist: Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavinga and Fulham’s Sander Berge, plus France GWC sensation Manu Koné as Michael Carrick eyes the final piece in his midfield puzzle.

The problem with United over the past 13 years has been that it’s never actually the final piece. It would be kind to call their post-Ferguson transfer hit rate scattergun. Ángel Di María was the first final piece in the puzzle. Then it was Alexis Sánchez. Then Fred. And then Jadon Sancho. Something needed to change. So say what you like about Big Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s recent, purse-tightening Old Trafford regime, but they’ve not flopped anywhere near as hard in the transfer market as their predecessors. Only Ugarte and Joshua Zirkzee can be deemed true flops under the Ineos boys. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha were smart additions a year ago, Senne Lammens was a scouting triumph and United are threatening to go again with their sensible signings policy – who’d have thunk it?! – with a combined £85m on Santos and Tielemans representing far better value than splashing that same amount on relegation specialist Matheus Fernandes. Finding value in the market is almost impossible nowadays, but credit to these fellas, they’re giving it a go.

What feels quite apt with Carrick at the wheel is that United’s biggest struggle this summer has been to find a true midfield destroyer. That moniker certainly doesn’t fit Santos, nor Tielemans. Tchouaméni was always unattainable so United are getting creative, as they did when Carrick was sought as Roy Keane’s replacement in 2006, less a like-for-like replacement and more a style shift. OK, it could be argued that Berge – an experienced screening No 6 – could step into the Casemiro void after a promising GWC campaign, but Camavinga and Koné like to charge around putting out fires, so perhaps United are following the mould of other top clubs and dispensing with the idea of the Makélélé role.

Modern football is all about excess, whether that be GWC participants, number of games, or transfer fees going beyond £100m for apparently workmanlike players. United have long threatened to descend into financial overspill, but after a steady season under a steady manager, are they finally grasping the concept of modest frugality? Roll up, roll up: ditch the merch-baiting marquee signing and grab yourself three all-purpose midfielders, all for reasonable prices! It surely cannot last.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“This is ideally the high point of my career, of my life, my professional life. I will give it everything I have [but] if you [reporters] tomorrow start saying: ‘He’s sh!t,’ tell me to my face and I’m out. If you behave badly and don’t leave my family in peace, I’m gone, I’ll just turn away” – Jürgen Klopp takes the Germany job and proves that he should still be good for a quote or two.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp: still got it. Photograph: Markus Ulmer/GES Sportfoto/Getty Images

double quotation mark Re: Simon Mazier’s letter about the location of Iraola’s Amazon parcel (Thursday’s Football Daily). If the delivery guy is anything like ours, the player will turn up at the Etihad” – Dave Eddy.

double quotation mark It would be even worse for Iraola to receive a card saying that his new signing has been left with a neighbour … Everton” – Paul Taverner.

double quotation mark At least if Bezos buys into Liverpool, they get next-day delivery, music, and a TV channel. They can also send back any players they don’t want and get a full refund” – Jeff Bez Peter Arnold.

Sports.title: Austin FC academy players under investigation by police and FBI for allegations of youth-on-youth sexual abuse
Sports.content:
Multiple players in the academy of Major League Soccer club Austin FC are under investigation by Austin police and the FBI over allegations of sexual abuse within the club’s youth system. Multiple sources, who spoke to the Guardian on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the investigation, said the inquiry centers on alleged interactions between academy players. A source with knowledge of the matter said multiple academy families reported the allegations to Austin FC.

The Austin police department confirmed the existence of the investigation to the Guardian on Thursday, adding that because it “involves juveniles and is ongoing”, no other details could be shared. An FBI spokesperson said the bureau could “neither confirm nor deny” the existence of an investigation and declined to comment further. Sources at MLS and Austin FC confirmed the existence of the Austin police department and the FBI’s investigations.

“In December 2025, we became aware of allegations of youth-on-youth misconduct occurring among a group of academy players,” the Austin FC Academy said in a statement issued to the Guardian. “After learning of these issues from concerned Academy families, Austin FC Academy took immediate action.”

The academy said in its statement that its officials immediately reported the allegations to MLS, the US Center for SafeSport and local law enforcement and initiated an internal investigation in coordination with the league. The academy also suspended “all activities” for the age group affected by the allegations while the issues were investigated. The FBI has visited the club’s training facility to conduct interviews, a club source told the Guardian.

Sources within MLS and Austin FC said that multiple academy players had been disciplined as a result of their investigation but that no Austin FC academy staff member had been. That same source said the league and club could pursue additional action if new information arises, but both Austin FC and the league itself have been asked to pause their own proceedings until law enforcement concludes theirs.

“We continue to fully cooperate with law enforcement throughout its ongoing investigation,” the Austin FC Academy said in a statement to the Guardian. “Throughout this process, Austin FC Academy and MLS took decisive actions guided by our unwavering commitment to the health, safety and well-being of our youth players and will continue to do so.”

“MLS takes matters of player safety and well-being extremely seriously,” the league said in a statement to the Guardian. “Throughout the process, MLS and Austin FC have approached this matter from a trauma-informed perspective, prioritizing the safety and well-being of the young people involved, protecting their privacy, minimizing the risk of further harm, and coordinating carefully with law enforcement and other appropriate authorities. MLS prioritizes the safety and well-being of players and will continue to work with clubs to promote a safe and respectful environment.”

The Austin FC academy program comprises five teams, from U-13 to U-18 age groups. At least 100 players are involved in the program, which is overseen by a separate coaching staff and leadership structure from the senior team. The teams compete in MLS Next, the youth competition run by the league that started in 2020. Like many MLS academies, Austin FC recruits from around the country and offers homestay living arrangements for players arriving from out of town. They also provide schooling for their players via an agreement with Florida-based SAI academy, who provide on-site education for many MLS academies.

At the senior level, Austin’s sporting department has changed significantly in recent months, with the club moving on from head coach Nico Estévez and sporting director Rodolfo Borrell in May. On Friday, a club source said those changes were not connected to the allegations. Austin eventually installed former Philadelphia Union head coach Jim Curtin as Estevez’s replacement, though he will not take charge until the start of the 2027 sprint season. The team, led by interim head coach Davy Arnaud, sit 14th out of 15 teams in the Western Conference, three points clear of last-place Sporting Kansas City.

Sports.title: Argentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la Fuente
Sports.content:
Spain’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has hit out at the “intolerable, unacceptable” behaviour of Argentina players in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s World Cup final.

At the forefront were Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes, who attacked Rodri and Eric García respectively at New York New Jersey Stadium as Spain’s players celebrated winning the World Cup for a second time in the country’s history. Paredes also confronted Spain’s Gavi.

“At the time, I didn’t realise it. I was celebrating, hugging teammates,” De La Fuente told Spanish television. “But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed. Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.”

De la Fuente also praised the exemplary behaviour of his own players faced with these “acts of aggression” and “provocations” which he believes could have escalated into more serious incidents.

Although the scenes were filmed and widely shared on social media, they have not yet resulted in any sanctions against the Argentina players. Fifa has opened an investigation into the incidents to determine whether there may have been violations of the world football governing body’s disciplinary code.

Sports.title: Arsenal star compared to Jude Bellingham among trio who could face fight to save their future in pre-season
Sports.content:
Arsenal star compared to Jude Bellingham among trio who could face fight to save their future in pre-season

Arsenal begin their unofficial start to the defence of their Premier League crown with their first pre-season game next weekend.

Mikel Arteta's side are ramping up their preparations for the new season with trips to Girona and Dublin before returning to London.

7 Ethan Nwaneri has reported for duty after the end of his Marseille loan last season Credit: Getty

The Gunners had 15 players at the World Cup this summer, which means that several key players won't be back in training for weeks.

However, their absence presents other fringe players with the opportunity to impress Arteta at the start of pre-season.

The Spaniard has largely kept the same squad intact in recent years, but this summer promises to be a potentially dramatic shake-up.

Arsenal transfer latest

Arsenal have already agreed a deal to sign Christos Tzolis in a deal worth £34million, with Leandro Trossard exiting to Besiktas.

The Gunners have since missed out on top target Morgan Rogers after he instead sealed a record-breaking £117m deal to Chelsea.

The club remain keen to sign Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, though the two clubs differ regarding the Brazilian's valuation.

Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez is another player that is admired, while France winger Bradley Barcola has also been linked.

But it promises to be just as big a summer for some players already in the building - with some facing a fight to prove their worth.

The following names do not include the likes of Fabio Vieira and Reiss Nelson, who seemingly already know that their futures lie elsewhere.

7 Arteta is looking to guide Arsenal to back-to-back Premier League titles for the first time in club history Credit: Getty

The future of Ethan Nwaneri

Arsenal ended a 22-year wait for a Premier League title, but it was a hugely frustrating season for one of their Hale End success stories.

Just a year before, Nwaneri was being compared to Jude Bellingham and Lamine Yamal, with talkSPORT's Adrian Durham even going so far as to say it is a 'sackable offence' for Thomas Tuchel not to pick the teenager in his first England squad in March 2025.

Yet Nwaneri made only four starts across 12 appearances for the Gunners in all competitions last season before he was loaned out.

The 19-year-old joined Roberto De Zerbi's Marseille for the second half of the campaign and scored just 13 minutes into his debut.

Yet he found himself out of the team after the now-Tottenham boss left his role as head coach, and Nwaneri was an unused substitute in five of the club's final six Ligue 1 games of the 2025-26 season.

7 Nwaneri registered six Premier League goal involvements in 2024/25 compared to zero last season

Arsenal's No.22 trained with the England squad in the United States ahead of the World Cup and is now back in pre-season training.

European football expert Andy Brassell expects the Arsenal style to evolve a little bit from last season - which could mean bad news for Nwaneri, with the club eyeing Morocco's teen star Ayyoub Bouaddi.

He told talkSPORT.com: "What do they do with Ethan Nwaneri? Do they bring him back?

"Do they send him out on loan again and hope he plays more than he did at Marseille, or do they decide to cash in and sell him?"

With Martin Odegaard, Gabriel Martinelli, Bukayo Saka, Eberechi Eze, and Noni Madueke all having a delayed return following the World Cup, the start of pre-season will be a huge opportunity for Nwaneri.

7 Nwaneri was loaned to Marseille for more minutes, but his action was limited Credit: Getty

The rise, fall and rise again of Ben White?

Arsenal have confirmed that William Saliba will be out for an 'extended period' with a back injury.

On the opposite end of the scale, England defender White has recovered from his knee problem for the start of pre-season.

The 28-year-old picked up the issue during the Gunners' Premier League win over West Ham in May, which ended his World Cup hopes.

White had been on a run that saw him start the last five matches in all competitions, which also saw him recalled by England in March.

7 White's season was ended prematurely after he was forced off with a first-half injury against West Ham Credit: Getty

Eight injuries across the past two seasons saw the ex-Brighton defender miss 42 matches for Arsenal, leaving his future in doubt.

Now White, who only has two years left on his deal, can reclaim his place as a core part of Arteta's backline with others' fitness issues.

Saliba is sidelined for the foreseeable future, while first-choice right-back Jurrien Timber continues to struggle with a groin problem.

Arsenal have since been linked with moves for England pair John Stones and Ezri Konsa, the latter of whom can play both centrally and at right-back just as White can.

A strong start to pre-season for White may convince Arteta that an approach for Aston Villa's Konsa isn't what is needed right now.

7 Injuries in recent seasons have slowed White, but he was fit to start pre-season Credit: Getty

Taking the Vik

Unlike both Nwaneri and White, Viktor Gyokeres will start pre-season belatedly after spearheading Sweden's run to the World Cup last-32.

The striker is arguably fighting for his future more than most, despite finishing as Arsenal's top scorer in his first season at the club.

talkSPORT revealed Arsenal explored the possibility of offering Gyokeres as a makeweight during initial talks for Julian Alvarez.

Arteta made it clear who he sees as his first-choice striker in the Champions League final, with Kai Havertz tasked with leading the line.

7 Despite finishing as Arsenal's top scorer, doubts remain over Sweden international Gyokeres

The German underwent two surgeries in seven months last year but scored three goals in four World Cup appearances for his country.

Gyokeres could even find himself third in the pecking order, now that World Cup winner Mikel Merino is also back fit and firing.

The Spaniard only returned from injury just before the tournament after fracturing his foot in January.

He then underlined his credentials in front of goal by scoring two late winners for La Roja en route to their run to glory.

Bet of the day

Queens Park to beat Queen of the South @ 20/21

Premiership side Aberdeen have dominated Group A in the Scottish League Cup, winning all three of their matches. But Scottish Championship Queens Park have fared best of the rest and can complete their group campaign with a home win over League One outfit Queen of the South.

Queens Park finished a solid sixth in the second tier last season and made a promising start in this competition with a 3-1 home win over Brora Rangers and a 2-1 away success at Kelty Hearts.
