Sports.title: Earthquake strikes New Zealand hours after Tottenham land for pre-season tour
Sports.content:
Earthquake strikes New Zealand hours after Tottenham land for pre-season tour

A magnitude 5.9 earthquake rocked a region of New Zealand not long after Tottenham Hotspur landed for their pre-season tour.

Spurs have travelled to Oceania for a summer schedule of friendlies ahead of their first full season under Roberto De Zerbi.



3 An earthquake hit New Zealand soon after Spurs arrived for pre-season Credit: Getty

They arrived in Auckland from London in the early hours of Saturday morning, with an earthquake taking place not long after.

According to the Euro-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC), it struck the Manawatu-Whanganui region on the North Island.

At a magnitude of 5.9, it had the ability to cause slight damage to buildings and other structures, as per the scale from Michigan Tech.



It was described as a severe earthquake by GeoNet, a New Zealand-based natural hazard monitoring system.

The New Zealand Herald have also claimed that over 20,000 people felt shaking, and emergency services are 'assessing the situation'.



Luckily for Spurs, the earthquake occurred over 320 kilometres away from where they are in Auckland.

Who do Spurs play in pre-season?

Spurs have already played a friendly match this summer as they beat MK Dons 1-0 earlier in the week.



They are up against Auckland FC on Sunday, with kick-off coming at 4am UK time.

Sydney FC follow on Wednesday, with a more UK-friendly kick-off at 10:45am, in the Sydney Super Cup.

Spurs then face Premier League rivals Chelsea on August 1 with the same kick-off time.

3 Spurs have three matches on their tour, including a clash against Chelsea Credit: Getty



After a hat-trick of matches in New Zealand and Australia, Spurs will return to London and face Getafe at their training ground.

Two friendlies against TSG Hoffenheim conclude the schedule, with one coming at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on August 15.

Spurs begin their Premier League campaign with a trip across the capital to Brentford on August 22.

Who is in the Spurs pre-season squad?

A total of 35 players have travelled for the north London club's tour.



Summer signings Martin Dubravka, Mateus Fernandes, Andy Robertson, Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke are all set to play.

Mohamed Kudus, Xavi Simons, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert remain in London as part of their injury recoveries.

3 Spurs head into the new season off the back of a 17th-place finish Credit: Getty

Guglielmo Vicario, who is understood to have agreed personal terms with Inter Milan, is also absent amid a minor knock he got in training.



Following their World Cup appearances with Uruguay and Senegal respectively, Rodrigo Bentancur and Pape Matar Sarr are on leave.

Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero and Djed Spence, who reached the semi-finals, are also out of the squad.

Sports.title: Chelsea land Aston Villa coach in shock move – and it’s great news for Morgan Rogers
Sports.content:
Chelsea land Aston Villa coach in shock move – and it’s great news for Morgan Rogers

Aston Villa set-piece coach Austin MacPhee is on the brink of joining Premier League rivals Chelsea, talkSPORT understands.

The 46-year-old joined the club in August 2021 after spells with the Northern Ireland national team, Hearts and FC Midtjylland.



3 MacPhee is heading to Chelsea after five years at Villa Credit: Getty

MacPhee has worked alongside Dean Smith, Steven Gerrard and Unai Emery during his five-year stay at Villa.

However, alongside his assistant manager role with Portugal, he will take his set-piece expertise to Chelsea and work with Xabi Alonso.

He is a highly-regarded coach who is regularly seen on the touchline during matches.



Villa scored 29 goals from set pieces during the 2025/26 season, the joint-most in Europe with Arsenal.

And, as per The Athletic, they have netted 74 set piece goals during his time at the club.



News of MacPhee joining Chelsea comes after Bernardo Cueva was given a new role at Stamford Bridge.

He moved from Brentford before the 2024/25 season to become a set piece coach, but he is now working as a technical analyst.



Worked a treat

MacPhee will be the second arrival at Chelsea from Villa this summer after the British record £117million signing of Morgan Rogers.

The 23-year-old looked set to join Premier League champions Arsenal, but it's Chelsea who completed a deal.

Rogers will therefore work with MacPhee once again in the upcoming season, with the duo already having a successful partnership.

3 MacPhee and Rogers are already accustomed to each other Credit: Getty



During Villa's 4-2 win over Liverpool towards the end of the previous campaign, Rogers opened the scoring shortly before half-time.

His goal, a curling strike into the far corner, followed a well-worked sequence of play from a corner.

The television cameras caught MacPhee celebrating the move, which appeared to have been worked on during training.

Emery joined in with him, with Rogers also seen embracing the coach near the dugout.



Chelsea and Villa business

Whilst Rogers has joined Chelsea and MacPhee is en route, Alejandro Garnacho has gone the other way.

The winger has completed a season-long loan move to Villa, and the deal has a conditional obligation to buy clause included.

3 Chelsea have completed the statement signing of Rogers in a record move Credit: Getty

Nicolas Jackson, who was on loan at Bayern Munich from Chelsea last season, is another player to have been linked with Villa.



They are understood to have been offered the chance to sign the Senegalese striker, who worked with Emery at Villarreal.

Sports.title: ‘Shocking’ – Jude Bellingham’s dig at referee in behind-the-scenes video of Argentina clash
Sports.content:
‘Shocking’ – Jude Bellingham’s dig at referee in behind-the-scenes video of Argentina clash

Jude Bellingham made his displeasure with referee Ismail Elfath clear after England were beaten by Argentina at the World Cup.

The Three Lions went ahead in their semi-final clash but ultimately lost 2-1 as the holders reached the final against Spain, who won.



2 Footage of Bellingham's post-match remark to the referee has been released Credit: Getty

Argentina committed 15 fouls during the match and received three yellow cards, whilst England had one booking from 11 fouls.

It was a feisty affair overseen by MLS referee Elfath, who was making his second appearance at a World Cup.

However, Bellingham took issue with his performance in the middle of the pitch and made it clear after the full-time whistle.



In a video posted by TristanTegtmeyer on TikTok, the ref-cam footage from the match shows Elfath's perspective.

Bellingham walks over to shake hands with the officials and, when he looks to the referee, says: "Some shocking ones, but all the best."



The decisions Bellingham refers to are unknown, but it's evident that Elfath was sub-par in his eyes.

Spilling over at full-time

There was little to no cordiality between England and Argentina at full-time in Atlanta.



Morgan Rogers clashed with opposition players, whilst Bellingham slapped Valentin Barco on the back of his head.

Argentina players then unveiled a banner that read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which means 'The Falkland Islands are Argentina'.

The Falkland Islands are a British Overseas Territory, but Argentina have disputed its sovereignty.

2 Bellingham claimed some of the referee's decisions were shocking Credit: @tristantegtmeyer TikTok



Rules set by the International Football Association Board (IFAB) make it clear that equipment must not have political statements or images.

Peter Kyle, the former Secretary of State for Business and Trade, was on hand to call for an investigation from FIFA.

However, there has been no word from the governing body as of yet, and the White House even defended the players' right to the banner.

Argentina were outplayed in their 1-0 defeat in the final against Spain and sparked a post-match brawl, which saw Leandro Paredes throw punches.



The 2022 champions, who also stood with their backs to Spain when they lifted the trophy, were thoroughly criticised for their behaviour.

Argentina president Javier Milei has since claimed people are 'jealous' of his country despite the players' lack of graciousness in defeat.

Sports.title: Folarin Balogun decision flagged in report about possible World Cup betting irregularities
Sports.content:
Potential betting irregularities have reportedly been linked to Folarin Balogun's controversial red card during the 2026 World Cup.

The striker was dismissed for the United States in their 2-0 last 32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was therefore ineligible to feature against Belgium in the next round.

2 A report has flagged Balogun's red card for potential betting irregularities Credit: Getty

However, as talkSPORT revealed, Donald Trump called FIFA president Gianni Infantino to review the one-match ban for Balogun, which was later suspended for a year.

Balogun then played against Belgium in the last 16, but the co-hosts were well beaten 4-1.

The decision to suspend his ban was solely taken by FIFA's Disciplinary Committee chairman Mohammad Al-Kamali, which was unusual given that precedent-setting cases tend to have a three-person panel.

Following the conclusion of the World Cup on Sunday, the Council of Europe have released findings from the Group of Copenhagen - who fight against sports manipulation - into possible malpractice.

Across the 104 matches, 15 were 'placed under increased surveillance', with the final day of the group stage being a particular concern.

Another seven were given 'yellow notices' and '12 major controversies' were 'analysed in light of integrity risks'.

The Athletic have reported that the American cryptocurrency-based site Polymarket opened a market that asked 'Will Folarin Balogun play against Belgium?'

This opened on July 2, which is the same day as the United States v Bosnia and Herzegovina match in which Balogun was sent off.

Balogun was confirmed to have been able to play against Belgium by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee on July 5, a day before the match.

It is said that the report from the Group of Copenhagen shows there were no similar markets for any of the 14 other players who were sent off at the World Cup.

2 Balogun was the only red-carded player to have his ban suspended Credit: Getty

Balogun was the only player to have a ban suspended, whilst England defender Jarell Quansah had a one-match sanction for his dismissal against Mexico increased to two matches.

FIFA have been sent an official request by the Group of Copenhagen for a written explanation in regard to the Balogun case.

Another three incidents have been highlighted as potential examples of irregularities, as per The Athletic's report.

This includes the red card for South Africa midfielder Themba Zwane, which he received in the 84th minute of their opening 2-0 defeat to co-hosts Mexico.

Polymarket receiving around $4.8million (£3.6m) from markets on Spain failing to beat Cape Verde in their Group H match, which ended 0-0, also raised concern.

Another flagged example came during Spain's 4-0 group win against Saudi Arabia, during which the VAR team disallowed a goal scored by Ferran Torres after a three-and-a-half minute delay.

Sports.title: Man United told to sell Bruno Fernandes as ‘assists are meaningless’
Sports.content:
Dean Saunders believes Manchester United should sell Bruno Fernandes to fund a summer rebuild, as he dismissed the midfielder's incredible assist record.

Fernandes has been widely hailed as the Red Devils' best player in recent years, and enjoyed an historic 2025/26 campaign by breaking the Premier League record for the most assists in a single season.



5 Bruno Fernandes has been hailed as Manchester United's best player in recent years Credit: Getty

The United skipper set up a huge 21 goals last term, surpassing the previous best shared by Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

His stunning individual campaign saw him crowned the Football Writers' Association's (FWA) men's Footballer of the Year, and helped propel his team to an impressive third-place Premier League finish.

But with United now set for a first Champions League campaign since 2024, they have set about bolstering their squad ahead of it.



The Red Devils are in the process of a midfield rebuild, having already snapped up Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos from their Premier League rivals, while they are interested in France duo Aurelien Tchouameni and Manu Kone.

'Brainless'

As Man United weigh up how they will fund any further summer spending, talkSPORT's Saunders pointed to Fernandes.



There is currently no suggestion that the 31-year-old will be going anywhere, as he has a year left on his existing contract, with a one-year extension option.

And while many would label Fernandes indispensable - who has 107 goals and 108 assists in his United career - Saunders was less convinced by his exploits in the latter field.



On Friday's Breakfast Show, he floated around the idea of offloading United's talismanic captain this summer to talkSPORT's Chief Football Correspondent, and Red Devils superfan Alex Crook.

To this, Crook responded: “If you're going to say Bruno Fernandes, the answer is no chance.”

He continued: “21 assists last season. Wears the captain's armband, been the best player by a country mile since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club.

5 Fernandes received the Premier League's Playmaker of the Year award in the 2025/26 season Credit: Getty



“Absolutely brainless to even contemplate that.”

Appearances can be deceptive

Despite Crook's adamant response, Saunders argued that Fernandes' incredible assist statistics could be deceptive.

The former Wales international claimed the Portuguese playmaker's numbers are largely dependent on those around him, insisting his teammates can put him in positions to claim easy assists.

Saunders said: “This assist business, I don't get it.

“I asked Jamie O'Hara the other night, how many assists did you get in your career? He went: ‘I don't know'. I said: ‘Yeah, because no one ever told you and we never counted them’.

“The assists depend on who you're playing with.

5 Fernandes has consistently been United's biggest creator, recording double digits in assists in each of his full seasons at the club Credit: Getty



5 But Saunders wasn't buying his label as the Premier League's top creator Credit: Talksport

"So, for example, if Harry Maguire robs the ball off the centre forward and pokes it to Fernandes and he first times it round the corner for me to go clean through and score, who gets the assist? Harry Maguire or Fernandes? Or both?"

Arguing his case, Saunders insisted Fernandes' upturn in goal contributions was due to him having more clinical players ahead of him.

In the 2024/25 campaign, United recorded a record-low 16th-place Premier League finish, with striker Rasmus Hojlund scoring just four league goals.



By contrast, Michael Carrick's side finished third last term with three of their attacking players hitting double digits in league goals - Bryan Mbeumo (11), Benjamin Sesko (11) and Matheus Cunha (10).

Saunders continued: "If you're playing with Robbie Fowler and you're a left winger, John Barnes, say, and he's whipping crosses in the face of the goal, Robbie Fowler's finishing every cross that comes across - 10 goals, 10 crosses.

“Then he plays with Darwin Nunez, who manages to miss from everywhere. So John Barnes' stats are down because they're not getting finished.

5 Fernandes benefitted from having a more clinical front line in front of him last season Credit: Getty



“Tugay [Kerimoglu] played for Blackburn. He hit Damien Duff's chest on the left wing every five minutes [to then cross] - Damien Duff's [assist] stats were up, and then we signed Andy Cole and his stats went up again because he was finishing them. It's a team game.”

Crook was unable to argue with this, who admitted: “It's made a difference that Fernandes was hitting Cunha and Mbeumo and Sesko last season, and not Rasmus Hojlund.”

No debate

However, Crook was insistent that Fernandes' record-breaking statistics are still incredibly impressive, who also set a new record for the most big chances created in a Premier League season last term.

He added: “To set up 21 goals over the course of a Premier League season is not to be shied away from.”



And the talkSPORT reporter insisted Fernandes' influence at Old Trafford cannot be understated, as he has reached double figures in goal contributions in all of his full seasons at the club.

Crook told Saunders: “Take that away, there's no conversation that since Fergie left the club, Bruno Fernandes has been the most important person at Manchester United."

Sports.title: Leeds immediately sanction exit with James Trafford set to sign
Sports.content:
Leeds United’s pursuit of James Trafford appears to be inching closer with goalkeeper Lucas Perri set for a move to Italy.

The Whites are closing in on the Manchester City shot-stopper Trafford, as reported by talkSPORT on Thursday.



3 Lucas Perri is on his way out of Elland Road after just one season Credit: Getty

Trafford, who secured a move back to the Etihad last summer, has found first-team football hard to come by since the arrival of Gianluigi Donnarumma.

And now an impending move to Leeds is set to be finalised after the club entered into negotiations with Torino for Perri.

The Serie A club have made Perri their first-choice target this summer and are confident of completing a deal for the Brazilian.



According to Fabrizio Romano, just a few details remain before the transfer can be completed.

Perri, who enjoyed a 12-month spell at Lyon prior to moving to Elland Road, is understood to be keen on a move to Italy.



Torino had originally proposed a loan deal for the 28-year-old with an option to buy; however, Leeds are understood to want around £8.5million for the star.

His exit should accelerate Trafford’s arrival at the club with the England international keen on a move to Elland Road.



Trafford had been linked with a switch to Newcastle and almost made the move to St James’ Park 12 months ago.

The Magpies’ interest resurfaced again this summer, but no offer has been tabled for the 23-year-old.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke has long admired the ex-Burnley goalkeeper, who is set to become the club’s first-choice between the posts next season.

3 James Trafford is edging closer to a permanent move to Leeds Credit: Getty



3 Leeds boss Daniel Farke is a long-term admirer of Trafford Credit: AFP

A busy window

Farke has been active so far in the summer transfer window, having added two fresh faces to his squad.

Leeds have wrapped up the signing of Bosnian centre-back Tarik Muharemovic, and he joins free-agent signing Harry Wilson after his departure from Fulham.

Farke led Leeds to a 15th-place finish last season, steering his side away from a relegation dogfight.



The Whites finished nine points above the bottom three thanks to a good run of late-season form.

Leeds kick off their 2026/27 Premier League campaign at Nottingham Forest on Saturday, August 22.

Fixtures against Brentford, Brighton and Newcastle follow for Farke's side, who will be confident of getting early-season points on the board.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland leads party-goers in Norway's iconic rowing celebration as he joins Man City stars at team-mate's glamorous Italian wedding
Sports.content:
Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma married his childhood sweetheart yesterday — with a host of his City team-mates in attendance at the lavish reception.

Erling Haaland was among the guests in Fasano, southern Italy, joined by his partner, Isabel Haugseng Johansen.

The Norway star, fresh from accumulating an army of new fans at the World Cup, opted for a black suit, bow-tie and sunglasses as he happily walked hand-in-hand with Johansen.

He was later filmed leading a group of guests in recreating Norway's iconic 'rowing' celebration from the tournament in North America.

City midfielder Mateo Kovacic was also pictured at the wedding. Italian football legend Paolo Maldini, former City boss Pep Guardiola and new Tottenham signing Sandro Tonali were also said to be among the attendees.

Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma married his childhood sweetheart Alessia Elefante in Italy yesterday

City stars Erling Haaland and Mateo Kovacic, joined by their partners Isabel and Izabel, and were among the guests. Haaland later led party-goers in Norway's iconic 'rowing' celebration

Donnarumma and Elefante, an interior designer, have been together for 10 years

Donnarumma, 27, tied the knot with his long-time partner Alessia Elefante, a 28-year-old interior designer.

The pair have been dating for 10 years, having met in their hometown of Castellammare di Stabia, near Naples.

They also have a son together — Leo, born in 2024. The couple announced their engagement in May with an Instagram post that read: 'Long-term contract signed.'

They wed in the Church of Saint George Martyr in the hilltop town of Locorotondo before joining the revellers in Fasano.

Haaland certainly enjoyed the night, excitedly banging a drum as chanting party-goers sat on the floor rowing — copying the post-match celebration that Haaland and his team-mates made famous in their impressive World Cup campaign.

The 26-year-old has been making the most of his break after the tournament, having holidayed in Italy with Johansen this week.

Sports.title: Lando Norris hits out at F1 bosses for running world championship like a business - with half-electric engines introduced to 'make more money'
Sports.content:
Lando Norris hits out at F1 bosses for running world championship like a business - with half-electric engines introduced to 'make more money'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lando Norris has taken a swipe at Formula One bosses for running the world championship as a 'business' rather than a sport.

The world champion was alluding to this year's controversial move to half-electric engines that have diluted the purity of racing as the batteries are depleted and recharged each lap, a process partly dictated by AI algorithms.

This has resulted in frequent and random overtaking that has potential to please uninitiated fans but has infuriated drivers and connoisseurs watching at tracks and on TV.

Norris let rip at F1's American owners Liberty Media, who employ Stefano Domenicali as the sport's chief executive, ahead of the Hungarian Grand Prix.

He said: 'Formula One is heavily led by the fact it's a business nowadays, and not about making the sport the best possible.

'It's about how you make the most money. That's not what it should be. That's not how a sport should be run.

'The fact we have hybrids, 50-50 and all that, (is the problem). It's been done because more teams wanted to come in and you make more money.'

Lando Norris is not happy with the way Formula One is currently being run

He was alluding to Audi, who were seeking a move to all-electric road cars in a mission statement that has, ironically, been watered down due to slower than expected sales, being induced on to the grid by the promise of the new technology.

The most vocal critic among the drivers has been four-time world champion Max Verstappen, who derided the new regulations as 'anti-racing' and like 'Mario Kart'.

Norris, whose McLaren team have not won a race this year, does not see a fix on the horizon despite modifications coming in next year and 2028 to reduce the electric element of the power unit.

'You can't just change your engine in the middle of the year, and you can't change it even with one or two years' notice because, as I say, it's not about doing what's best for the performance of a car – it's a business,' he argued. 'It's a shame.'

Asked if spectators can enjoy the hybrid formula, he added: 'Fans from five years ago, pre-Drive to Survive, would hate this.

Four-time world champion Max Verstappen has compared Formula One to Mario Kart

'But fans nowadays are a lot more personality-based, about the drivers, and not about Formula One as a whole sport, so are less interested in how the actual race goes. They care more about whether a driver has done well or not.

'The fans have changed, and that's completely fine. But the biggest voice should always be ours as drivers. That is not because we're selfish and chasing what we want.

'We're saying that because we have the best idea of how racing should be, how it can be, what's possible, what's not. We want the best for everything, the best for the fans, the best viewing, the best racing for us, the most fun to drive.

'At the minute, we don't have that. We have very, very little say. What they have done is because you can have Audi and other teams in F1, and that is a bigger win than the drivers being happy.'

Formula One and the governing FIA are promising to introduce V8 engines in 2031 in a tacit acknowledgement they have got it wrong.

Sports.title: Reports of Aidan O'Brien's disastrous Flat campaign may have been exaggerated... and Benvenuto Cellini could bring him King George joy today
Sports.content:
Mark Twain famously wrote ‘the report of my death was an exaggeration’, after his obituary had been mistakenly published.

That was back in 1897, but a similar sentiment could well apply to Aidan O’Brien’s 2026 Flat campaign which was this week analysed using Timeform’s ‘Run to Form’ metric.

The microscopic scrutiny conducted by the racing organisation revealed that this July is the most unsuccessful month on record for the Ballydoyle handler since the metric was first introduced 14 years ago.

But not only that, Timeform also revealed their data showed that the current Flat season represents the worst for O’Brien since 2012.

Not a great omen then for his four runners in today’s King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes.

O’Brien goes in search of his fifth success in the summer showpiece and should Irish Derby winner Benvenuto Cellini prevail, it will be his first victory with a three-year-old in the Group One since 2001 with Galileo.

But hang on... it seems just five minutes ago that the talk in racing was about O’Brien chasing his own record of Group One wins in a season off the back of a record-equalling seven successes at Royal Ascot.

Benvenuto Cellini goes off at around 5-1 today, behind favourite and defending champion Calandagan

That array of victories came hard on the heels of Christmas Day’s Betfred Derby win at Epsom and preceded a brilliant display by Constitution River in the Coral-Eclipse.

Surely reports of his demise are premature.

A Thursday night Group race double at Leopardstown may signal the Ballydoyle machine is about to crank back into full gear following a brief mid-summer malaise.

One thing we can all take on trust is that it will not be long before O’Brien is once again namechecking his entire roster of staff following another Group One win.

Who knows, it could be after today’s fabulous feature, but with equine stars from around the world tackling Benvenuto Cellini and Minnie Hauk, both Ballydoyle contenders will be required to post clear career bests to prevail.

The market favours last year’s conquering hero Calandagan, who is back to defend his crown. He renews rivalry with Japanese raider Masquerade Ball, who ran him to a head in an epic renewal of the Japan Cup in Tokyo last November.

Calandagan enjoyed a Saint-Cloud confidence booster three weeks ago following his Coronation Cup no-show, while Masquerade Ball lost nothing in defeat attempting to outspeed the imperious Romantic Warrior on his home patch at Sha Tin in the spring.

The old adversaries form a formidable road block for their rivals to navigate, but could last year’s runner-up Kalpana, the home team’s sole representative in a cosmopolitan affair, trouble the overseas posse and hand trainer Andrew Balding an emotional success?

Aidan O'Brien has not won the King George with a three-year-old since 2001

Andrew’s father, Ian, won this prize 55 years ago with one of Flat racing’s all-time greats in the mighty Mill Reef and, although Balding’s mare could not yet be mentioned in those circles, she has at least accumulated an impressive Ascot record.

Her handler is certainly optimistic and his confidence was increased when his star mare worked well in the lead-up to this race as she bids to turn around a length defeat by Calandagan in last year’s renewal.

‘She worked really well, and I’m very happy with her,’ reported Balding.

‘We were struggling to get weight off her last year, but this year it seems to be easier.

‘She’s very good on her day and loves Ascot, so I’m pretty sure she’ll be there or thereabouts. Calandagan is a very good horse. We couldn’t match him last year, but who knows this year?’

Sports.title: How £75m Bruno Guimaraes can take Arsenal to next level: Better numbers than Declan Rice, leading Mikel Arteta's press and how his deep passes unlock low blocks
Sports.content:
Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Arsenal have been here before with Bruno Guimaraes. The Gunners wanted him four years ago when he was still at Lyon but, in the end, the Brazilian chose Tyneside.

If that were not bad enough, the announcement video he posted on his social media, captioned ‘a beautiful chapter is coming’ began with clippings of news headlines of Arsenal’s interest.

More than four years later and Arsenal are back again. This time, Guimaraes wants them too. He has told Newcastle he wants to join Arsenal and now it’s down to the clubs to thrash it out. A fee of around £75million should do it.

That’s a fair whack for a player about to turn 29, much older than the usual profile of Arsenal signings under Arteta, but in Guimaraes they would have a ready-made addition to take them to the next level, as they bid to retain their first Premier League title in 22 years and expunge the pain of the Champions League final defeat by Paris Saint-Germain.

As owner Josh Kroenke said at the end of the season: ’It is about trying to stay at the top knowing everyone is trying to climb the mountain after you.’

Guimaraes would help them do that. There’s good reason why Arteta wants him. He’s physical. He’s versatile. He can play box-to-box, deep-lying playmaker or destructor. Or, as we’ll come to see, all of them, all at once.

Arsenal are pushing hard to sign Bruno Guimaraes (left) from Newcastle to bolster their midfield as they bid to retain their Premier League title

Arsenal tried to sign Guimaraes from Lyon in 2022, but were beaten to the signing by Newcastle

The 28-year-old Brazilian has 48 caps for his country, representing them at the last two World Cups

BRUNO'S BRAWNS PL midfielders since Jan 2022 Tackles Joao Palhinha (Fulham/Spurs) 410 Moises Caicedo (Brighton/Chelsea) 408 Joao Gomes (Wolves) 380 Bruno Guimaraes (Newcastle) 356 Alexis Mac Allister (Brighton/Liverpool) 353

BRUNO'S BRAINS PL midfielders since Jan 2022 Open play chances created Bruno Fernandes (Man Utd) 359 Martin Odegaard (Arsenal) 276 Bruno Guimaraes (Newcastle) 197 Morgan Gibbs-White (Wolves/Nottm Forest) 197 Bernardo Silva (Man City) 197

Declan Rice needs a rest. The Arsenal and England midfielder played 69 matches for club and country last season. Arteta ran him into the ground – he has previous for this, just ask Bukayo Saka – and, by the end, you could tell.

He played through a hamstring injury from Christmas onwards and was substituted early in England’s victory over Croatia with ‘neural pain’ in his back.

'The body's been through a lot this season,’ he said after England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina. 'I think you can see I'm mentally done, physically done. I need a break now.’

Only, Arsenal’s title defence starts in less than a month. Having Guimaraes will allow Arteta to rest his linchpin.

But that’s only one reason. He’s Rice, and he’s more. In many ways, he’s the complete central player. Over his four and a half years at Newcastle, he ranked in the top five midfielders for both tackles and chances created from open play. Only Rice and Bruno Fernandes have run more miles since Guimaraes joined the Premier League.

His tenacity out of possession will be ideal for Arteta’s intense press. He wins the ball back but then he does something with it.

What has been clear in recent seasons is how over-reliant Arsenal are down the right and, conversely, how under-served they have been at playing through the middle. Saka is the main source of attacking threat while creator-in-chief Martin Odegaard also likes to drift that side.

Guimaraes is the ideal player to fix that. Nine goals for Newcastle last season was as many as Rice and Zubimendi combined, while his five assists match Rice’s figure.

Declan Rice has admitted he is suffering from neural damage in his lower back and hamstring - and did not appear to be at full fitness during the World Cup

Guimaraes' nine goals for Newcastle last season was as many as Rice and Zubimendi combined, while his five assists matches Rice’s figure

So much of his creativity for Newcastle comes through the middle. As you can see from the chances created maps below, many of Rice's come tucked into the left channel and frequently not until he gets into the final third.

Guimaraes is more focused in central areas and, quite frequently, from deep.

That could be crucial for Arteta. His ability on the ball from deeper areas will allow Arsenal to be quicker and more direct when they have possession, an aspect of their play Arteta is keen to improve if they are to push on once more.

Where Rice creates his chances from, focused largely on the left 'half-space' just outside the box

Guimaraes' map is far more varied, and he is able to create chances from deeper - which will help Arsenal against low blocks

For too long, they have struggled to break down defences with cutting passes and instead turned back to set-pieces or Saka.

Towards the back end of last season, we saw Arsenal try to implement this more, especially in their Champions League semi-final victory over Atletico Madrid where they used the pace of Viktor Gyokeres to exploit space in behind the defence.

William Saliba’s ball (below) led to the move that set up Saka’s winning goal. In the same game, however, the Arsenal crowd got on Rice’s back when he had the chance to do the same but turned it down and passed it sideways.

Guimaraes loves a pass from deep to set his team-mates away. Arsenal know that only too well, Guimaraes having sent a defence-splitting ball through to Jacob Murphy to run clear in their clash early in the season.

He attempted more through balls and line-breaking passes per game than either of them too.

William Saliba chips in behind the PSG defence to find Viktor Gyokeres

But Rice was unable to do the same, and instead passed back inside to Martin Odegaard

Guimaraes showed against Arsenal last season that he is eager to get attacks started rather than build up slowly and allow the defence time to settle

Not only that, though, he can dribble the ball with purpose himself too. Guimaraes created 13 chances for his Newcastle team-mates following ball carries last term, more than both Rice (eight) and Zubimendi (three) combined.

His delivery from set plays, the cornerstone of Arsenal’s attack, is also superb with a couple of assists coming from corners last term.

All of that shows why Arteta wants him, and why he’s so keen to splash the cash on a player that’s not far off 30. Because he can play the Rice role or he can play the Zubimendi (or Myles Lewis-Skelly) one. Rice can sit in, Guimaraes can push on. Or the other way around. He can split defences, he can run at them.

What better way to push on again than by signing a player who can do it all.

Sports.title: The clues Enzo Maresca gave away at Man City unveiling: How he'll manage after messy Leicester and Chelsea exits, why he's 'not worried' about Rodri's future or 115 charges and what's happening to Jack Grealish
Sports.content:
The clues Enzo Maresca gave away at Man City unveiling: How he'll manage after messy Leicester and Chelsea exits, why he's 'not worried' about Rodri's future or 115 charges and what's happening to Jack Grealish

Unlock more from our team inside the Manchester City camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

The bald head and stubble were familiar, and so was the casual dress sense. But the man who settled into the chair at Manchester City’s training headquarters on Friday was different to the one who has occupied it for the last decade.

In fact, drive past the terraced houses opposite the Etihad Stadium, and the face on a blue mural dedicated to Pep Guardiola could easily be mistaken for Enzo Maresca.

But Maresca is not Guardiola. As much as he admires the man who brought an unprecedented era of success to City, shares similar principles and spent time with him as recently as last week, the Italian made it clear at his official unveiling that he intends to do it his way.

‘First of all, for me, it's important to make it clear that I'm here to do my job in the way I want,’ said Maresca, sitting at the City Football Academy beneath a large screen with a message welcoming him back to the club where he was previously one of Guardiola’s assistants and manager of the club’s Elite Development System.

‘I'm not here to try to copy someone. I'm just here to try to do my job; to install my idea, the way I see the football.

‘Every manager is different. There can be some similar concepts, but at the end, every manager is different. The way we approach day by day, and the way we approach the games. So we’ll see in which way we need to tweak.

Enzo Maresca was officially unveiled as Manchester City manager on Friday

This is Maresca's third spell at City, having been one of Pep Guardiola's assistants in the 2020-21 and 2022-23 seasons, either side of a brief stint as Parma manager

HIS FIRST SIX MATCHES Aug 16, Comm Shield Arsenal (n) Aug 23, PL Bournemouth (h) Aug 28, PL Crystal Palace (a) Sep 5, PL Coventry City (h) Sep 13, PL Man United (a) Sep 19, PL Sunderland (h)

‘I don't think there are managers that they just copy and paste from another manager (repeating a phrase that Guardiola used in his final press conference). I probably don't see the football in the same way as the other manager, so that's why I don't believe in copy and paste.

‘I spoke with Pep a lot since he decided to leave the club. I was with him a week ago, and we spent some hours together. The relationship with Pep has always been very close since I was with the Under 23s.

‘He needs to enjoy his moment. After 10 years playing every three days, it's quite demanding, and I think now he deserves to relax – and I also need to do my job and find the solutions for myself.’

Looking tanned and relaxed in a black T-shirt, the 46-year-old had to face some thorny issues on Friday after prefacing his opening press conference by offering condolences to the family of Kevin Keegan, who was manager of this club for four years.

There was the matter of his acrimonious departure from Chelsea, who put out a statement after he was confirmed as Guardiola’s successor last month claiming that his resignation after a year in charge was because his ‘head and heart were focused on another club and another opportunity’. City ended up paying their rivals £17million in compensation. Maresca chose his words carefully.

‘I have been quite lucky in terms of my former clubs, Leicester and Chelsea,’ said the Italian, who won the Club World Cup and UEFA Conference League at Stamford Bridge. 'I think we did a great job in both clubs. The identity of the team was clear. The success of the team was clear. But now I think we are here today. That is the most important thing. Just about City. Nothing to add.’

Then there are the 115 Premier League charges that still hang over City. Is it something that concerns him?

‘No, to be honest,’ he replied. ‘The only thing I can say is that three years ago, in the Treble season, I was here and there were the same words about this kind of problem. In three years, it is still the same. So nothing happened.’

'I probably don't see the football in the same way as the other manager, so that's why I don't believe in copy and paste'

Maresca was part of the Treble-winning coaching staff and has relationships still with the players from that team including Erling Haaland (right)

MARESCA'S MANAGERIAL CAREER Years Club Matches Win % 2021 Parma 14 28.6 2023-24 Leicester 53 67.9 2024-26 Chelsea 92 59.8 2026- Man City 0 -

After Elliot Anderson was unveiled as City’s new £116m signing this week, one of Maresca’s first tasks will be to resolve the future of Rodri, who has been linked with a move to Real Madrid as he enters the final year of his contract at the Etihad.

First of all, the Spaniard will undergo back surgery on Monday after winning the World Cup last weekend. Maresca wasn’t giving much away other than to say that Rodri remains a key part of his captaincy committee following the departure of Bernardo Silva to Madrid on a free transfer this summer.

‘We have in this moment three players with Ruben (Dias), Rodri, and Erling (Haaland),’ added Maresca. ‘Probably we need some more because Bernardo left, but we will decide about that.

‘I think every manager wants to have Rodri because he's a top player. But (he will have) surgery on Monday, and he needs a holiday. He needs to rest. He needs to recover, and then he will be back here with us. Around big players, there is always speculation. I'm not worried about that, I think it's normal.’

There was a similar stance over goalkeeper James Trafford, who is being heavily linked with Leeds.

‘When the transfer window is open, now and in January, anything can happen. So we’ll see. But at the moment, he’s one of our keepers,’ said the new City boss.

Maresca was asked about two of the players – Phil Foden and Jack Grealish – who have struggled at times since winning the Treble in the 2022-23 season when he was by Guardiola’s side.

Foden signed a new four-year contract this week, but Maresca’s comment that Grealish is a ‘Man City player at the moment’ does not bode well for the man who spent last season on loan at Everton.

Maresca insisted he is 'not worried' about the future of Spain's World Cup-winning captain Rodri, despite the City midfielder being linked with a move to Real Madrid

Maresca with Jack Grealish after winning the Treble. The England winger's future is in doubt after his loan to Everton last season

‘I just want Phil to be the Phil that we all know, but especially the Phil that we all want,’ said Maresca, who revealed that he spoke to Foden after he was left out of England’s World Cup squad. 'First of all, for him because he needs to enjoy football and in general. Second, because I know how good Phil is. With Phil in a good shape, in a good mood, we can win games.’

So what would success look like next season to the man who has the unenviable task of filling Guardiola’s shoes?

‘I'm here knowing that this is a club that needs to win titles,’ Maresca replied. ‘But if you just focus on the final target, you miss all the previous part. I love the day by day. I love to do my job. I love to prepare sessions, to spend time with the players, and then at the end, for sure, the target is to win titles with this club.’

Either way, the new man is determined to be his own man.

Sports.title: Donald Trump accuses LeBron James of being RACIST in astonishing attack after NBA star's bombshell 76ers decision
Sports.content:
Donald Trump has launched an astonishing attack on NBA legend LeBron James, just hours after the 41-year-old revealed he'd be signing with the Philadelphia 76ers.

In a lengthy statement shared on Friday, James admitted he considered retiring but believes he still has 'more to give,' confirming his new venture after leaving LA.

He is set to sign a modest $8 million, two-year contract in Philadelphia, according to ESPN. He made nearly $53 million last season.

Just hours after LeBron's 24th season in the NBA was confirmed, Trump was asked to weigh in on who holds the title of the greatest basketball player of all time.

'Michael Jordan's a guy that's a friend of mine, I've played golf with him,' Trump said.

'He's a really good guy and I think LeBron is - maybe he's a racist, but maybe he doesn't like Trump, I don't know - but I only like people that like me, so I would say Michael Jordan all the way.'

LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $8 million deal

Trump launched an astonishing attack on James, claiming 'maybe he's a racist'

.@POTUS on the Jordan vs. LeBron debate: "Michael Jordan's a guy that's a friend of mine... and I think LeBron is—maybe he's a racist, but maybe he doesn't like Trump, I don't know—but I only like people that like me, so I would say Michael Jordan all the way." pic.twitter.com/xrfXOg2whP — Rapid Response 47 (@RapidResponse47) July 24, 2026

The comments mark the latest chapter in a long-standing feud between the four-time NBA champion and Trump, which dates back to James labeling him a 'bum' in 2017.

James, 41, has frequently used his platform to criticize Trump, previously endorsing Democratic candidates and launching voting-rights initiatives across the country.

Their bad blood spilled into the public eye during Trump's first presidency after he withdrew a White House invitation extended to Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry over his hesitation to visit.

Outraged by the gesture, James immediately jumped to his rival's defense, tweeting at Trump: 'U bum, Steph Curry already said he ain't going! So, therefore ain't no invite. Going to White House was a great honor until you showed up!'

The public spat escalated in 2018 when Trump announced he was pre-emptively banning both the Cleveland Cavaliers and Golden State Warriors from visiting the nation's capital following that year's NBA Finals.

Refusing to be fazed, James swiftly shut down the snub, declaring at the time: 'Winning a championship is way bigger than getting invited to the White House, especially with him in it.'

Later that year, James voiced his frustration with the President's leadership during an interview with ESPN, admitting it made him 'sick' to see how Trump handled the moral authority of the Oval Office.

'He doesn't understand the power that he has for being the leader of this beautiful country,' James said at the time. 'He doesn't understand how many kids, no matter the race, look up to the President of the United States for guidance, for leadership, for words of encouragement. He doesn't understand that, and that's what makes me more sick than anything.'

Join the discussion How should sports stars use their platforms when clashing with political figures like Trump?

Trump and James previously traded verbal barbs on social media back in 2018

James once voiced his frustration with the President's leadership in an interview with ESPN

James' political opposition to Trump stretches back to 2016, when he penned an emotional op-ed for his local newspaper, the Akron Beacon Journal, endorsing Hillary Clinton for president.

Reflecting on his childhood in a single-parent home, James argued that Clinton was the only candidate who truly understood the plight of underprivileged youth, praising her as a champion for children alongside his 'good friend' Barack Obama.

Turning the attention back to basketball, James joins a menacing 76ers roster that includes the likes of Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey as he pursues an elusive fifth NBA title.

In a lengthy statement on X, the 41-year-old admitted he strongly considered retiring but believes he still has 'more to give' and can turn his new team into a contender.

He wrote: 'I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and decide if I still love this game.

'I still truly love this game, and I have more to give. The last few weeks have really been special. I've never been able to have no clue what to do and take real time to just think. I've had an incredible few months with all the people I love trying to figure it all out.

'This is my last decision. I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship.

'I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time. Thank you LA. Miami I'll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always home!'

James' political opposition to Trump stretches back to 2016, when he penned an emotional op-ed for his local newspaper, the Akron Beacon Journal, endorsing Hillary Clinton for president

Reflecting on his childhood in a single-parent home, James argued that Clinton was the only candidate who truly understood the plight of underprivileged youth

James told the Lakers earlier this summer that he would not be returning to Los Angeles next season.

Reports claimed that James' former teams, the Cleveland Cavaliers and the Miami Heat, were leading the charge to sign him. He was also heavily linked to the Golden State Warriors.

But James joins a 76ers team that has not won an NBA championship since 1983 and has not advanced out of the second round of the Eastern Conference playoffs since 2001.

Philadelphia fans will be hoping he can wipe out that streak just as he did in Cleveland, who had not won a title for 52 years before he led them to success in 2016.

The Athletic reports that Maxey and other key figures with Philadelphia have been relentlessly pursuing James in recent weeks. Their blockbuster trade for Brown with the Celtics also tipped the balance in their favor.

James, who will turn 42 in December, is about to enter his 24th season in the NBA, which is a league record. He is the all-time leading scorer in NBA history and has won four championships, two with the Heat and once each with the Cavaliers and Lakers.

Sports.title: Revealed: Jude Bellingham's brutal dig at World Cup referee as unseen footage goes viral - moments before England star slapped Argentina rival following semi-final defeat
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham furiously hit out at 'shocking' refereeing decisions after England's World Cup semi-final heartbreak against Argentina, footage has revealed.

The Real Madrid star made a point of confronting Ismail Elfath – Lionel Messi's favourite referee – to share his grievances after England's 2-1 loss last week.

Argentina employed roughhouse tactics against England, committing 15 fouls, to book their place in the final against Spain, where they lost 1-0.

Leandro Paredes and Enzo Fernandez were seen as particularly dirty in the opening exchanges of the match.

Both teams came into the match with a heightened sense of rivalry after the South American side's declarations throughout the tournament that the Falkland Islands belong to Argentina.

Fresh footage from the referee's camera has been released by FIFA and in it, Bellingham is seen saying to the referee: 'Some shocking ones there, but all the best.'

Jude Bellingham furiously hit out at 'shocking' refereeing decisions after England's World Cup semi-final heartbreak against Argentina, footage has revealed

He was annoyed at decisions that had gone in Argentina's favour in their tense encounter

Bellingham, who scored seven goals for the Three Lions at the tournament, later slapped Argentina rival Valentin Barco on the back of the head as scenes turned ugly in Atlanta.

In the build-up to the flashpoint, Spurs captain and Argentina defender Cristian Romero was seen goading Bellingham when the final whistle was blown.

He went over to Barco and slapped him on the back of the head.

The full-back then turned around and pushed Bellingham with tempers flaring. Nicolas Otamendi also came over and gave the England man a shove.

Several Argentine players attempted to act as peacemakers, but it looked as if Bellingham and Otamendi wanted more head-to-head action – even when they were separated.

During the celebrations Argentina's stars held aloft a banner that read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates to 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

Despite FIFA's ban on political flags, Romero, Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez and ex-Spurs midfielder Giovani Lo Celso celebrated with the controversial sign after the final whistle.

Captain and star player Lionel Messi was also seen dancing alongside the banner.

Join the discussion Has Messi’s and Argentina’s behaviour at the World Cup tarnished their legacy in football?

Bellingham was goaded by Argentina star Cristian Romero at the final whistle

The midfielder also clashed with Argentina substitute Valentin Barco after the semi-final

Bellingham appeared to slap new Chelsea man Barco on the back of the head

He was also at loggerheads with defender Nicolas Otamendi as other players tried to stop them

FIFA are already looking into disciplinary action relating to the banner and Argentina's behaviour following their loss to Spain in the final.

The South American side's dirty tactics against England, plus the consistent allegations throughout the tournament that things were 'rigged' in their favour, have not done Messi's popularity any favours on these shores.

Messi is now viewed unfavourably among almost half of the participants surveyed by YouGov.

After losing 1-0 to Spain some of the Argentina squad started fights with the Spanish players. Fernandez was sent off in normal time and Paredes was lambasted for attacking Eric Garcia and Gavi after the match.

Even Messi was dragged into their pathetic antics in the final, attempting to get Marc Cucurella sent off for briefly putting his hand over his mouth.

Messi also clashed with Bellingham in the semi-finals, though England fans have to admit that the legend was brilliant towards the end of the match, setting up both of his country's goals.

All of this has had a deleterious effect on Messi's popularity.

Coming into the World Cup, he was viewed favourably by 55 per cent of the public and unfavourably by just nine per cent.

Now, he is seen favourably by only 29 per cent and unfavourably by 44 per cent.

That means that, according to YouGov's poll, Messi's net favourability rating among Britons has fallen from +46 to -15. In short, people don't like him very much.

His score is far worse than his arch-rival Cristiano Ronaldo, whose net rating is -2.

And he certainly lost his stock with Daily Mail Sport's veteran columnist Jeff Powell, who bunged Messi out of his top five all-time players for his antics.

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty's wife Holly watches on as star reaches 100m breaststroke final after bizarre 10-minute delay to heats - and local hero Duncan Scott surges to gold
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty's wife Holly watches on as star reaches 100m breaststroke final after bizarre 10-minute delay to heats - and local hero Duncan Scott surges to gold

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Four police officers in high-vis vests snuck into the back of the Tollcross stand as Duncan Scott stepped onto the blocks. This was 1:56.38s of sporting theatre that nobody in Scotland wanted to miss.

Scott first dived into this east end pool as a ten-year-old boy. He swam here as a sixth-form student at the 2014 Commonwealth Games but those expectations were nothing like what he felt in Lane two on Friday night.

The sell-out crowd waved their Saltires and roared every stroke as Scott won the hosts' first gold medal of the competition. Adam Ramsay-Peaty was on the same ticket but the locals were here to see one man only.

Scott is the posterboy of these Games and his storming victory in the 200m individual medley provided lift-off. It had a similar feel to Antoine Dupont winning France’s first gold medal on the Sevens pitch at the Paris Olympics, hearing the anthem for the first time.

‘I was a wee bit nervous before that,’ admitted the 29-year-old, who held off a late surge from New Zealand's Lewis Clareburt.

Even the coppers were bouncing. Back in 2014, Scott swam here as a 17-year-old dreamer. He returned as one of the country’s most iconic athletes, ready to add an 11th gold (and counting) to his collection of Olympic, World and Commonwealth medals.

Duncan Scott claimed gold for Scotland in the pool at the Commonwealth Games on Friday

Adam Ramsay-Peaty, meanwhile, eased into the final of the 100m breaststroke in the evening

The locals admire Scott for what he stands for. He campaigns against the closure of local leisure centres – of which Tollcross is one. He lobbies politicians for more funding for public swimming pools and stays true to his principles.

At the 2019 World Championships, for example, he refused to shake hands with Chinese swimmer Sun Yang in protest against his doping conviction.

You suspect Scott would have been Scotland’s flagbearer if his race schedule had not clashed with the opening ceremony. These days, he is held in the same regard as Sir Chris Hoy, his countryman who stepped out of Dr Who’s Tardis with the King on Thursday night.

Scott did not hang around to bask in his glory. The adulation does not come naturally like it does for his contemporary, Ramsay-Peaty. The pair have been room-mates and relay team-mates at the Olympics, enjoying similarly meteoric rises.

With a new name on his swimming cap, Ramsay-Peaty is now hoping to follow Scott onto the medal podium on Saturday night, having qualified for the final of the 100m breaststroke.

His famous wife, Holly, was in the crowd as his qualification faced a bizarre snag. Moments before his first race, one of the lane dividers broke off the pool wall, requiring an official to strip down and jump into the pool to reconnect it.

The amusing 10-minute delay did little to change Glasgow 2026’s image as the Poundshop Games, but at least it did not unsettle the Englishman.

‘In any sport, stuff goes wrong,’ said Ramsay-Peaty. 'It doesn’t help losing all the heat when you’re preparing. There’s ten minutes where you’re losing hydration, I guess, but you know what I’ve done a lot better in worse conditions.

Adam was cheered on by wife Holly, who shared a snap of her view to social media

The couple, who have become a celebrity power couple, were married in December last year

‘Even if it’s a first - scoreboards break, clocks break - the guys got it together pretty well. It was only 10 minutes, right? Hopefully it doesn't happen again. It’s a bit of extra time to enjoy the crowd, I guess. Obviously, I’m a sprinter, so every second counts, but you know what? Stuff happens in sport, stuff happens in life, and you’ve got to get on with it.’

Peaty shared this pool with Scott in 2014. Their journeys have taken different routes, but they seem destined for the same place on the podium.

Sports.title: Caoimhin Agyarko used stabbing to fuel attempt at creating history
Sports.content:
Caoimhin Agyarko used stabbing to fuel attempt at creating history

Caoimhin Agyarko will challenge super-welterweight world champion Josh Kelly tonight as he attempts to fulfil his dream

View Image Caoimhin Agyarko challenges for a world title tonight

Caoimhin Agyarko will always carry the scars.

‌



Not just the seven-inch reminder staring back at him in the mirror every morning. But also the mental trauma which lingers nine years after he was stabbed in an unprovoked attack. Agyarko came within inches of death when he was assaulted by a gang in Belfast at the age of 20.

‌



The Irishman found himself having to choose between revenge and motivation. He opted for the latter and tonight has the chance to become Ireland's first black world champion when he takes on Josh Kelly. "I don't think I'll ever mentally recover fully from it," Agyarko admitted.

‌



Anthony Joshua's injuries from car crash revealed before comeback fight READ MORE :

"I've come a hell of a long way since then in terms of what it took from me, but it has also given me a lot. I think it changed my mindset and made me realise that if I wanted to achieve something in boxing that I have to give it my all and live with no regrets. As much as it sounds crazy, I think I'm a better person for getting stabbed.

"I have to look at my scar every single day knowing nobody was ever found guilty and nobody was ever arrested. The guy who stabbed me is still running the streets and living his life The main thing for me is the fact I had to make a very tough decision over whether to seek revenge or continue to chase greatness.

Article continues below

"I had to put my ego and pride to the side which was a very hard thing to do, but I knew the greater cause was to become the first black Irish world champion, and I couldn't mess up those plans because one person did something to me." Agyarko was born in London before moving to Belfast aged seven and the super-welterweight admits he stood out in his white neighbourhood.

"It was difficult in the early years because mine was one of the first mixed-race families in west Belfast," Agyarko added. "It was very unusual for the local people to see someone who was mixed-race. "When I moved to Belfast, I had an English accent and I think it was confusing for them.

"At the start they didn't really think I belonged there, but because my family's Irish, I’ve always considered myself Irish. I always felt like I was one of them and not long after, the British accent faded and I was treated like one of their own. I want to leave a legacy behind that says no matter where you're from, what culture or religion you are, you can achieve great things. I'm just a regular kid from Belfast trying to achieve something great."

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua fight undercard, running order and exact fight times
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua fight undercard, running order and exact fight times

Former two-time heavyweight world champion Anthony Joshua will look to secure a fight with long-time rival Tyson Fury with a win over Kristian Prenga tonight

View Image Anthony Joshua takes on Kristian Prenga tonight

Anthony Joshua will look to make his highly-anticipated fight with Tyson Fury official by beating Kristian Prenga later this evening.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight world champion saw his long-time rival Fury get the job done on Friday night after he forced Mariusz Wach to quit on his stool in their behind closed doors encounter in Thailand. Now, all eyes are on Joshua to see how he fares on his return to the ring.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua ready to defy Tyson Fury in build-up to mega-fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua ready to defy Tyson Fury in build-up to mega-fight

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are on a collision course for later this year and Joshua has vowed not to let his trash-talking rival get under his skin

View Image Anthony Joshua gestures towards Tyson Fury

Anthony Joshua has vowed to haunt Tyson Fury long after they belatedly settle their bitter rivalry.

‌



The two British heavyweights each ruled the world in their prime without ever crossing paths in the ring. But providing Joshua, 36, swats aside Kristian Prenga tonight, he and Fury, 37, will finally collide later this year. Their long-awaited showdown will be a clash of personalities as much as a contrast of fighting styles.

‌



Joshua has held his tongue for a decade in the face of a tirade of abuse from his fellow countryman. The Olympic champion has been a poster boy for his bluechip sponsors while Fury thinks nothing of crossing the line between class and crass. The Gypsy King believes he can shatter his rival's corporate veneer and expose his raw working-class roots. But Joshua is confident he won't let his mask slip.

‌



Watch Anthony Joshua vs Kristian Prenga live on DAZN This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £19.99 or £0 DAZN Order the fight here Product Description Anthony Joshua returns to the ring to face Kristian Prenga on Saturday, July 25, in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Fans can order the fight on DAZN PPV for £19.99 or watch it at no extra cost with DAZN Ultimate.

"Tyson Fury won't get under my skin," he said. "It's about boxing and it's about skill; I'm not trying to win a press conference, I'm not trying to win a weigh-in. I'm trying to win a fight. I don't think the Anthony Joshua from Watford needs to come out in that aspect, it needs to come out in the ring. I will let him talk and let him have his fun.

‌



"I've seen Fury's community, and they're unbelievable talkers; that's the culture they're from. They have no problem calling each other out and saying, 'I'll drive 60 miles next week and meet you down there'. I can't go up against someone who has been doing it since he was 10 years old and think I'm going to win.

"I've got to let him do what he's good at, and my job is to beat him in the ring. There will be nothing better than getting my hand raised." Fury has taken every opportunity to run his mouth throughout his colourful career. He has even allowed Netflix into every crevice of his life through his hit series At Home With The Furys.

Tyson Fury sets up Anthony Joshua fight as rival QUITS on his stool READ MORE :

Tyson Fury sends immediate message to Anthony Joshua after forcing rival to quit READ MORE :

But while Joshua is happy to remain in the shadows for now, he is relishing the day that changes. "I'm too tired half the time, to be honest," he added. "My main focus is the sport and it's draining. Just trying to achieve a little bit in boxing is draining. It's not just turning up and training, it's trying to make the right decisions, trying to sleep better... it's a lot of pressure

Article continues below

"I don't know how Fury has the energy for it, to be honest; he boxes, he does Netflix, and he talks! I don't really get too involved in the he-said-she-said, but once this part of my life is done, you'll hear a lot more from me. When Fury wants to relax, when he's finished, I'll just be revving it up and he will see me coming.

"I'll let him win the first 100m, the first 200m, but after that I will still be going. It will be that last 100m, when the race is ending, that I will be coming for him."

Man Utd stars' body transformations attract attention as they return with new look

Pre-season is a time for fresh starts and a couple of Manchester United stars have reported back this summer sporting transformed physiques

View Image Bryan Mbeumo has reported for Manchester United's pre-season looking noticeably leaner compared to last term (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United fans may do a double-take when looking at two returning stars in particular this pre-season. That's after Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko reunited with the rest of the squad, looking transformed compared to when they were last seen playing for the club.

‌



United's pre-season got off to a less-than-glorious start after succumbing 1-0 to Wrexham in Helsinki last Saturday. Michael Carrick's side are clearly still getting up to speed after the summer break but have time on their hands to reacclimate.

‌



Mbeumo started in the 1-0 defeat to Wrexham, while Sesko is still recovering from the shin injury he suffered in May. However, his time on the sidelines clearly hasn't stopped the Slovenian from training altogether after appearing to have added some significant bulk this summer.

‌



The opposite is true for Mbeumo, whom fans have suggested looks noticeably leaner upon his return to the squad. That's not to say the Cameroonian had a lot of weight to lose in the first place, though it seems his off-season programme has included a fair bit of conditioning at the very least.

A new batch of photos released from United's pre-season camp thus far showed Mbeumo training in a vest alongside his team-mates. And the choice of attire pointed to a trimmed-down version of the winger coming into the 2026/27 campaign.

‌

Then there's Sesko. TNT Sports uploaded a post comparing the striker's frame on arrival at Old Trafford last year, compared to the striker fans are seeing this summer, and it's fair to say United's golden boy has now become a man.

Sports.title: Newcastle United dream squad as World Cup star signs alongside Sandro Tonali replacement
Sports.content:
Newcastle United dream squad as World Cup star signs alongside Sandro Tonali replacement

Newcastle's busy summer could still result in several new recruits ahead of the new Premier League season

View 4 Images Eddie Howe remains on the hunt for new signings at Newcastle (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Newcastle United could execute several transfers in the coming weeks as they prepare for the new Premier League campaign. Eddie Howe's side host Liverpool in their season-opener with less than a month to go until the clash.

‌



Until then, the Magpies' starting XI could be radically reshaped. Newcastle's recruitment drive follows their lowest finish in five years - a disappointing 12th-place campaign that cost them European football.

‌



Determined to climb back up the table, their battle this season will be without Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon, who clinched moves to Tottenham Hotspur and Barcelona, respectively. Despite those major departures, Newcastle show no signs of pumping the brakes regarding incomings.

‌



They have already brought in three new faces - Sean Steur, Bazoumana Toure, and Ewen Jaouen - as a fourth nears with the club agreeing to sign Monaco midfielder Aladji Bamba in a deal worth up to £34million. Mirror Football delves into further acquisitions the Premier League side could secure soon.

Goalkeeping situation

Arsenal make first Bruno Guimaraes transfer approach as £60m plans ripped up READ MORE :

The Magpies have already dipped into the goalkeeper market this summer, splashing out £18.5million on Stade Reims stopper Ewen Jaouen. Yet to feature in top-flight football throughout his career, the 20-year-old's capture appears to be one for the long term.

Given the Frenchman's lack of experience at the highest level, combined with the exits of Aaron Ramsdale, John Ruddy and Max Thompson, Howe's side could look to bring in another new goalkeeper. James Trafford initially attracted interest, although the Magpies' interest appears to have cooled.

‌



View 4 Images Newcastle United were interested in signing James Trafford last summer (Image: Alex Pantling - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

The club are yet to follow up on their initial interest, according to Chronicle Live, with The Athletic reporting Trafford prefers a move to Leeds United, who are in talks to sign the 23-year-old from Manchester City. At present, Newcastle are expected to retain Nick Pope as their number one for pre-season, with Jaouen anticipated to offer competition from the bench.

Two additions in defence

Right-back will be a key talking point for Newcastle before the window ends. With Tino Livramento withdrawing from the England World Cup squad due to injury, question marks persist over whether he will be able to remain fit enough for a consistent run of games.

‌



Guela Doue, brother of France and PSG star Desire, is one of the names on their radar to fill out their right-back options. The club have also been linked with Chelsea defender Josh Acheampong, who would be a savvy addition to Eddie Howe's defence.

Battle looms for midfield target

The £100m departure of Sandro Tonali to Tottenham has left the Magpies requiring midfield additions. Chronicle Live understands Spurs midfielder Lucas Bergvall was made available to Newcastle and the club made enquiries about a potential fee with various figures discussed, but a formal offer has not yet been submitted.

Spurs are confident they can secure £50m for the 20-year-old, who has featured 78 times for the north London outfit. The Swede's top-flight experience, despite his young age, combined with his clear ability, could see him emerge as a cornerstone for the future at St James' Park.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 4 Images Lucas Bergvall could be on his way out of Tottenham (Image: Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty Images)

Tottenham would welcome a bidding war with Nottingham Forest for the midfielder, with Newcastle determined to hold firm on their valuation of the player. Standing at 6'2, the midfielder's imposing physical presence complements his technical prowess on the ball exceptionally well and could develop into an effective partnership with Bruno Guimaraes - assuming the Brazilian stays in the North East this summer.

‌



The Magpies do have alternative targets lined up should a deal for the Swede fall through. Auxerre playmaker Kevin Danois is another player on the club's radar, though he is regarded as more of an attacking prospect.

Transfer for World Cup ace

View 4 Images Danilo Santos has reignited his career since leaving Nottingham Forest (Image: Getty Images)

Another midfield addition Newcastle are pursuing is Brazil international Danilo Santos. The 25-year-old is familiar with the Premier League, having represented Nottingham Forest from 2023 to 2025 before moving to Botafogo.

‌



Danilo's homecoming to Brazil saw him recapture his form and self-belief, securing him a spot in his nation's World Cup squad. His adaptability in both the six and eight roles makes him an attractive proposition for Howe, alongside his prior experience in English football.

The midfielder, who registered 10 goals and three assists in 20 appearances across all competitions for his club, is priced at approximately £25m, and could represent excellent value for Newcastle should he maintain his current upward momentum after reviving his career back home.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
