World.title: Trump tariff wall set to stay after Supreme Court blow: analysts
World.content:
Washington – Circumventing the US Supreme Court, President Donald Trump has found a way to resurrect his tariff wall in a fashion that analysts say could prove more durable to legal challenges.

Just this week, Trump slapped sweeping new tariffs on 60 trading partners and saw 25-percent duties take effect on Brazilian products. Both cases involved an authority that has previously been used to impose levies.

Trump separately tapped an untested justification for 50-percent tariffs on many Canadian goods.

The actions and threats “underscore the president’s continued affection for tariffs, and that they are not going away as long as he is in the White House,” Asia Society Policy Institute senior vice president Wendy Cutler told AFP.

Trump’s latest tariffs of 10 percent to 12.5 percent apply to goods from 60 economies starting Friday.

They came after probes over forced labor concerns, under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

Cutler said this has a lower likelihood of being overridden by courts, noting Trump’s top trade official Jamieson Greer had carefully navigated procedural requirements before imposing duties.

More concerning was Trump’s targeting of Canada using the untested Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, the Atlantic Council’s Josh Lipsky told AFP.

The justification was Canada’s alleged discriminatory treatment of US exports, with duties effective after a month.

“That’s more tariff-as-punishment” and could signal that Washington intends to keep less conventional tools at its disposal, Lipsky said.

This is an “uncertainty generator,” added Scott Lincicome of the libertarian Cato Institute.

– Court’s reluctance –

Already, Trump’s newest tariffs face legal challenges from small businesses.

As courts have earlier allowed the use of Section 301 for imposing duties, arguments against Trump’s latest salvo would likely focus on official findings that justified action, Lincicome said.

“That’s just not something that courts typically want to weigh in on,” he added.

Still, some argue that Trump lacks such broad powers to impose sweeping tariffs.

Within months of returning to the presidency, Trump unleashed a barrage of tariffs on US trading partners.

He invoked emergency economic powers to impose a swath of these duties quickly, a move deemed illegal by the high court this February.

Trump’s sector-specific tariffs, imposed under different legal authorities on steel, automobiles and other goods, are unaffected.

Officials have since launched Section 301 investigations, including on forced labor, to reinstate duties.

Lincicome warns however that past investigations were more substantive. A probe into China during Trump’s first term took a year to result in duties.

This time, probes into 60 economies including major partners like the EU and India spanned just four months.

– Hard to undo –

US tariffs are tough to undo. Former president Joe Biden, the Democrat who succeeded Trump after his first term, kept his predecessor’s tariffs on China intact.

Even if a future leader wanted to reverse Trump’s duties, revenue considerations will complicate the situation, Lipsky predicts.

Many countries were likely hoping the worst of trade wars are behind them, he said, but some may now have doubts.

The Trump administration has struck 19 framework or reciprocal tariff deals. Yet, threats of further duties loom with Washington investigating 16 economies including China, the EU and Japan over excess industrial capacity.

“The administration has been careful not to exceed the tariff levels agreed to in bilateral agreements,” Cutler said. “But partners are concerned that this assurance may not hold.”

Chad Bown of the Peterson Institute for International Economics believes Trump is missing a chance to address bigger problems like China’s rare earth export curbs.

Trading partners have to “fight a two-front trade war –- dealing with Trump’s tariffs and China’s export restrictions –- instead of just being able to focus on China,” he said.

While countries have expressed disappointment, Cutler said, there are no signs of retaliation, “knowing full well they would risk further US tariff escalation.”

World.title: Trump says hasn’t decided on big Iran strikes, Tehran getting ‘serious’
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said Friday that he had not decided on whether to launch major strikes on Iran yet, as Tehran was now getting “serious” in talks with Washington.

His comments came after reports that an increasingly frustrated Trump was meeting senior advisors to discuss launching a large-scale military operation against Iran.

“No I haven’t,” Trump told journalists in the Oval Office when asked if had made a decision.

“Look, we’re talking to them right now. I think they’re getting more and more serious as the days go by, for maybe the obvious reason.”

Trump said Iran had a choice between making a deal or facing a “much higher level” of strikes, after nearly two weeks of US attacks that have left a ceasefire in tatters.

The United States says it is carrying out the strikes to stop Iran closing the crucial Strait of Hormuz. Iran has responded with strikes on US bases that have killed four service members.

“We’re locked and loaded and ready to go. But we’re talking to them, so I think while we’re talking, we’ll see what comes of it. I believe…They’re very serious. They should be,” Trump said.

The war that Trump once predicted would last four or five weeks is now nearing its fifth month, and is weighing on the Republican’s approval ratings ahead of crucial midterm elections in November.

Trump added that he did not know what the “tipping point” would be for a decision, but reiterated his stance that his red line would be if Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon.

– ‘Massive attack’ –

The New York Times reported earlier that Trump had met advisors on Friday, while the Axios news outlet quoted the US leader as saying on Thursday that he was considering a “massive attack” on Iran.

Trump separately doubled down on comments in an earlier social media post in which he said he believed that Russia and China were not arming Iran, despite reports that both countries were giving Tehran intelligence to target US forces.

“I mean, I will tell you that President Xi said he will not partake, and President Putin said the same thing. I think you know I trust them,” Trump told reporters. “I don’t think they’d want to have me disappointed.”

Earlier in a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump had warned Moscow and Beijing not to sell weapons to Iran.

“If they did, it would be very bad for them — Certainly not in their best interests,” he wrote.

Trump said Chinese president Xi Jinping had told him when they met in Beijing in May that he would not arm Iran under any circumstances, and that Russia’s Vladimir Putin had made a similar promise despite the war in Ukraine.

“He understands that I do not sell Weapons to Ukraine, but to NATO Countries. They pay full price, and how those Weapons are distributed, I have no idea,” Trump said.

Trump has frequently taken a more deferential tone towards Xi and Putin than he has towards Washington’s own allies, saying that they must be respected as the leaders of major world powers.

World.title: Canada inaugurates US border bridge after cancelling joint ceremony
World.content:
Windsor – Canada quietly inaugurated a border bridge with the United States on its own on Friday, after cancelling a joint ceremony following this week’s announcement of new US tariffs on several Canadian products.

“This bridge is a testament of what we can build when we work together,” Housing and Infrastructure Minister Gregor Robertson told a ceremony on the Canadian side of the bridge, which opens to traffic on Monday.

“Our relationship has been challenged over the last few years,” Ontario Premier Doug Ford said of US-Canada ties, but added: “Let’s keep working together.”

US President Donald Trump marked the occasion with a social media post and a combative tone.

“Canada disinvited the United States of America to the opening of the Gordie Howe Bridge, which is fine, considering they are paying substantial TARIFFS to the United States,” he said in a post on Truth Social.

He added: “We changed the terms of the Deal so the United States of America now gets 50% of the Profit.”

The 2.5-km (1.5-mile) bridge connects the US city of Detroit and and Canada’s Windsor, and is named after Canadian-born ice hockey great Gordie Howe, who played for US teams.

The CAN$6.4 billion ($4.5 billion) cost of its construction, begun in 2018, was fully financed by Canada.

Trump on Monday ordered a 50-percent duty on many Canadian goods to take effect in 30 days.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he was looking at “all options” in response to the new levies, and that he and Trump had agreed to “intensify discussions” in upcoming weeks.

Carney then faced sharp criticism following Tuesday’s release of a proposed agreement on financial management of the bridge, deemed highly favorable to the US side.

The terms stipulate that Canada will make payments into a US economic development fund of the equivalent of 50 percent of net revenue generated by the bridge for a period of 15 years.

But on Thursday, Carney said revenue sharing would only apply to funds left over after Canada has first met its periodic debt service obligations for the building of the bridge, under terms of a 2012 deal that “remains in place.”

“This is a good deal,” Carney told reporters. “I should have been clearer.”

In February, Trump threatened to fully block the bridge, insisting the United States had been treated unfairly in its construction and that it should be “at least half” US-owned.

World.title: Iraq accelerates journey towards WTO membership
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has increased its attempts to join the World Trade Organization (WTO), with the new administration advancing a process that officials regard as part of a larger agenda of economic reform and diversification.

Iraq’s accession to the WTO would bring it into the rules-based global trading system, compelling the country to match its trade policies with international norms for market access, transparency, and regulation.

While membership does not ensure economic development, many observers regard it as a significant step toward building a more predictable climate for trade and investment.

Iraq’s WTO entrance is part of broader attempts to promote private sector growth, attract international investment, and boost non-oil economic activity. The process also requires considerable legal and institutional changes, such as modernizing trade laws and improving regulatory frameworks.

Last week, a team from Iraq’s Ministry of Trade traveled to Geneva to finalize technical documents with the WTO Accession Division and the International Trade Centre (ITC), marking another step forward in the country’s accession discussions.

Since 2020, the ITC has been supporting Iraq’s WTO accession process through a European Union-funded program.

Its work has focused on providing technical assistance to Iraqi institutions as they prepare for negotiations and implement the reforms required by the accession process.

Beyond the discussions, WTO admission is usually seen as a long-term reform goal.

The process promotes greater transparency, more predictable trade policies, and stronger institutions, while assisting countries in aligning domestic regulations with internationally recognized trade rules.

These measures might help Iraq diversify its economy, enhance its business environment, and integrate more effectively into regional and global value networks.

Their success, however, will be dependent on ongoing political commitment and execution after admission.

As negotiations continue, Iraq’s accession process remains both a trade negotiation and a larger exercise in economic modernization, with assistance from the WTO Secretariat, the ITC, the Ministry of Trade, and the European Union.

World.title: 'To ensure anti-national elements don't benefit from situation': Dharmendra Pradhan resigns - read full letter
World.content:
Read his full statement:



NEW DELHI: Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on Saturday tendered his resignation from the council of ministers amid the ongoing protests over the NEET paper leak.In a letter addressed to his "young friends," Pradhan said that he has sent his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, considering the situation that has developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country."I have been dedicated to students, teachers, and education reform for more than four decades. I have always believed that a strong, inclusive, and visionary education system is the very foundation of a strong nation.I deeply respect the aspirations, emotions, and just expectations of the country's youth. Realizing the dreams of India's young generation has been a moral commitment of all of us in political and social life. I express my gratitude to the Hon'ble Prime Minister for the opportunity he gave me to serve the nation under his visionary leadership.However, irregularities came to light in the NEET-UG examination held on 3 May 2026. The Government of India took immediate cognizance of this, handed over the investigation to the CBI, cancelled the examination, and announced a new date for the re-examination. Alongside this, it was decided that from next year the examination would be conducted in CBT (Computer-Based Test) mode.During this period, our foremost priority was to ensure that the examination for more than 20 lakh (2 million) students was conducted smoothly. This was carried out under a "whole of government" approach. In this, along with the Government of India, the state governments â especially the district administrations â played an important role. With the cooperation of students and parents, this examination was completed on 21 June 2026.From the very first day, I took responsibility and never turned away from this situation. My resolve was that we would not let any meritorious student's chances be ruined because of an examination mafia, and that no injustice would be done to any student.The NEET-UG results declared on 16 July were satisfactory, with many meritorious students from poor backgrounds also achieving success.However, during this time too, certain individuals occupying positions of responsibility tried to mislead students and create obstruction, which caused me deep anguish.I have always been an unwavering believer in the strength of our democracy, and I have always held deep respect for the aspirations, dreams, and expectations of the youth. They are not only India's future, but also the bearers, builders, and architects of a new and developed India.Watching the events of the last 10 days has saddened me. This is not a matter of personal reputation for me.The youth power of India is the real strength of this country.My resolve is that we will not let the country's youth get caught in a web of confusion.Considering the situation that has developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country â that anti-national forces should not take advantage of this situation, that the unity of the country should be preserved, that not even a single student's future should get entangled in legal complications, and that our children should devote their time to studies and focus on building their careers â I have sent my resignation to the Hon'ble Prime Minister.I express my heartfelt gratitude to the Hon'ble Prime Minister for his guidance, trust, and continuous support. I also express my gratitude to all my esteemed colleagues in the Council of Ministers, the officials and staff of the Ministry, and all those with whom I had the privilege of working. Service to the nation is the highest priority of my life, and I shall remain dedicated to it always.By the blessings of Lord Sri Jagannath, I shall continue to dedicate myself in every possible way, in the future as well, to the fulfillment of the aspirations of Mother India, the people of Odisha, and the youth of the country."

World.title: Millions with desk jobs, millions with cervical pain
World.content:
Understanding cervical pain

The Lancet

Is cervical pain becoming a workplace epidemic?

Problem not confined to corporate offices

So what can be done?

For millions of Indians, the workday begins with a laptop and ends with one. Eight to ten hours at a desk, endless video calls, back-to-back meetings and constant screen time have become the new normal. But while productivity has gone up, so has an invisible workplace problem - cervical pain.Doctors say they are seeing a sharp rise in young professionals in their 20s and 30s walking into clinics with neck pain, stiffness, headaches and posture-related disorders. What was once considered an age-related condition is now increasingly becoming an occupational hazard of desk jobs.The growing dependence on laptops, smartphones and sedentary lifestyles has turned cervical pain into a modern workplace health challenge. Beyond physical discomfort, it is affecting productivity, mental well-being and healthcare costs, raising concerns about whether India's rapidly expanding desk workforce is paying too high a price for long hours behind a screen.Cervical pain refers to pain or discomfort in the neck (cervical spine) and surrounding areas, including the shoulders and upper back. It can range from mild stiffness to severe pain and, in some cases, may be accompanied by headaches, tingling or numbness in the arms if nerves are affected.While cervical pain can occur at any age, it is becoming increasingly common among young adults due to prolonged screen time, poor posture and sedentary lifestyles.According to a study published in, nearly 200 million people worldwide were living with cervical pain in 2020. The study projects that this number could rise to 270 million by 2050, driven by ageing populations, sedentary lifestyles and changing work patterns.The impact extends well beyond physical discomfort. The World Health Organization (WHO) says musculoskeletal disorders are among the leading causes of work-related disability and absenteeism worldwide, affecting productivity and quality of life across age groups.A Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2019 analysis estimated that around 1.71 billion people globally live with disorders such as neck pain, low back pain, fractures, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and other musculoskeletal conditions.To understand how widespread the problem is, we spoke to 30 working professionals about their work habits, posture and neck health. Their responses point to a common pattern: long sitting hours, few breaks and recurring cervical pain.Most of the respondents were young professionals. 26 of the 30 participants were between 24 and 35 years of age, underscoring that cervical pain is increasingly affecting younger employees rather than just older adults.Ten respondents experienced cervical discomfort every month, nine reported symptoms every week, and seven said they dealt with neck pain almost every day, highlighting how common the condition has become among desk-based workers.Shashank, 38 years old media professional, said that he suffers neck stiffness, shoulder pain and arm pain very frequently.âI spend around 8 hours sitting every day on a chair which does not provide good support to my neck. I believe more frequent breaks and awareness about the right furniture in the offices can help employees work more efficiently. Bad furniture set up leads to poor posture which ultimately results in all kinds of problems,â he told TOI.Dr Arun Bhanot, Director â Spine Surgery at CK Birla Hospital, Gurugram, said there has been a noticeable rise in younger patients with desk jobs seeking treatment for neck pain."The profile of patients has shifted dramatically. Earlier, it was mostly older people with degenerative changes. Now, we are seeing a steady stream of people in their late 20s and 30s," he said.Long hours at the desk were the norm, with 21 respondents spending more than eight hours seated every day, while another seven reported sitting for seven to eight hours.Despite prolonged screen time, regular movement was uncommon. Twelve respondents said they rarely took breaks during work, while 10 stepped away from their desks only once every two to three hoursâfar less frequently than doctors recommend.Komal Gupta, 30-year-old journalist, while talking to TOI, said that she hardly gets enough time to exercise regularly, even though she knows it would help reduce her neck pain.âMost workdays are packed with deadlines, so taking out time for stretching or a workout becomes difficult.âDr Surender Pal Singh, HOD â Physiotherapy Department at CK Birla Hospital in Delhi advises keeping the monitor at eye level, ensuring proper chair support and avoiding carrying heavy laptop bags on one shoulder, as uneven weight distribution can increase stress on the neck and upper back.However, most of the respondents responded with no furniture or equipment support from the employer.Gupta said, âMy office also doesn't provide an external monitor or laptop stand, so I end up working directly on my laptop for long hours, which puts additional strain on my neck and shoulders.âJyoti Jaiswal, a 29-year-old dentist, says healthcare professionals are equally vulnerable due to the nature of their work."Treating patients often requires us to remain seated or stand in the same position for long periods, which puts considerable strain on the neck," she said.Jaiswal believes better workload management could help reduce the problem. "Proper patient scheduling is essential so that sufficient time can be given to each patient without rushing or compromising body posture. It would also give doctors brief breaks between consultations, reducing physical strain," she added.Tushar Gaur, a 25-year-old accountant from Meerut, says his job requires him to spend long hours seated, entering financial data and working continuously on a computer."The prolonged sitting and constant screen time often cause severe pain on the left side of my neck. I've realised that taking regular breaks helps reduce the discomfort, but during busy workdays it's not always possible," he said.Dr Bhanot said, "The head weighs around 4.5 to 5 kilograms in a neutral position. But tilt it forward by just 15 degrees to look at a screen and the effective load on the cervical spine rises sharply. Hold that posture for eight hours a day, five days a week, and the muscles and ligaments simply give in."Recalling one of his cases of treating a 26-year-old software developer, he said, â he developed severe neck pain, numbness in her fingers and forward-head posture after working from bed for nearly a year with her laptop balanced on a pillow."There was no disc herniation, but significant muscle strain. With ergonomic correction, physiotherapy and scheduled movement breaks, she was largely symptom-free within six weeks," he said.Respondents overwhelmingly felt that preventing cervical pain requires both individual lifestyle changes and employer support. Many said companies should invest in ergonomic workstations, including better chairs, adjustable desks, laptop stands and the option of standing desks to reduce strain caused by prolonged sitting.Several respondents also called for more employee-friendly workplace policies, such as reduced working hours, flexible schedules and better workload management to allow employees enough time to rest, exercise and maintain proper posture.Others suggested that employers should encourage frequent breaks, with some even recommending software-based reminders or applications that temporarily lock screens every 30 minutes to prompt employees to stand up, stretch and move around.While the other things are not in our hands, taking some time to exercise is.Dr Singh stresses that prevention is often simple but overlooked. "Standing up, stretching and walking for just one or two minutes every 30 minutes can significantly reduce pressure on the neck and back," he said, adding that even the best workstation cannot prevent neck strain if a person remains seated for long hours without regular movement.Every notification, meeting and deadline keeps employees glued to their desks. Yet, taking just a couple of minutes to move every half hour could make the difference between a healthy spine and years of chronic pain. In a workplace increasingly driven by productivity, perhaps the next big investment isn't technologyâit's healthier employees.Because the next deadline can wait, your health canât.

World.title: What is the Public Examinations Amendment Bill? Govt proposes sweeping changes to anti-cheating law
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has proposed sweeping changes to the anti-cheating law, seeking to speed up investigations and time-bound trials while introducing tougher punishment for those involved in paper leaks and examination malpractice.

Under the proposed Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, the central government to constitute a special task force (STF), wherever necessary, for investigation of offences under the Act.

Thereupon, investigations into offences under the Act will have to be completed within two months.

After that, within three months from the date of filing of the chargesheet, a time-bound appeal mechanism in the amendment requires the special fast track courts to conduct trials on a day-to-day basis and complete it.

Appeals against judgments, sentences or orders passed by a special fast track court will lie before a two-judge bench of the high court, which will be required to dispose of such appeals within three months of their admission.

To facilitate this, the Bill empowers all state governments and Union Territory administrations to designate any Court of Session as a special fast track court for trying offences under the Act.





According to the Statement of Objects and Reasons, the amendment aims to strengthen the credibility of public examinations by ensuring speedy investigation, time-bound trials and stronger deterrence against paper leaks and organised examination malpractice.

Stricter penalities introduced

For individuals found guilty of offences under the Act, the proposed punishment has been enhanced. The minimum imprisonment has been increased from three years to five years, while the maximum jail term has been raised from five years to 10 years.

The maximum fine has also been increased from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 50 lakh.

The Bill also proposes stricter action against service providers involved in examination fraud. The maximum fine for such entities has been increased from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore, while the period during which they can be barred from conducting public examinations has been doubled from four years to eight years.

Directors, senior managers or other persons responsible for the conduct of the business of a service provider, if found to have connived in the offence, will face a minimum imprisonment of five years, compared with the existing minimum of three years. The proposed fine for such persons has also been increased from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore.

The amendment further enhances punishment for organised crime related to paper leaks. The minimum jail term has been increased from five years to seven years, while the proposed maximum fine has been raised from Rs 1 crore to Rs 10 crore.

World.title: 'First it hurt me, later I took advantage': FM Nirmala Sitharaman's paper leak remarks spark political row
World.content: NEW DELHI: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has come under fire over her remarks on the NEET paper leak controversy after she said some students had used the additional time before the re-examination to improve their performance. The remarks drew sharp criticism from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and Opposition leaders, who accused her of being "insensitive" to students impacted by the alleged leaks.Speaking to news agency ANI, Sitharaman defended the government's handling of the paper leak controversy, saying its response had ensured timely arrests, re-examinations and declaration of results.Sitharaman said the government's response included timely arrests, a re-examination and prompt declaration of results. She said some students had used the additional preparation time to improve their performance, adding, "First it sort of hurt me when the paper leakages happened but later I took advantage of that and prepared even more and my performance has improved and I've done well." She added that such students had "taken this challenge and faced this, and come out bright in bright colours," while asserting that "the government is responding, PM is responding.Sitharaman also accused the Congress of disrupting Parliament despite the government's willingness to discuss the issue.The FM also accused the Congress of disrupting Parliament despite the government's willingness to hold a discussion on the issue. She said the government had agreed to the Opposition's demand for a debate, but the opposition keeps disrupting the house. "The government is willing to have full-fledged discussion in the House, come discuss," she said, accusing the Congress of "disruption of the House" because "the truth will come out, and the government's actions will be placed before the House. They don't want a fair discussion."The remarks come as thousands of students have been protesting for weeks over the alleged NEET paper leaks, with demonstrations centred at Delhi's Jantar Mantar and echoed in several parts of the country. On July 20, protesters marching towards Parliament were lathi-charged and tear-gassed by police and the rapid action force, leaving several students as well as security personnel injured.The government has since reached out to protesters, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi promising strict action against those responsible for paper leaks and Union ministers holding talks with activist Sonam Wangchuk and the representatives of the Cockroach Janta Party.The CJP strongly objected to Sitharaman's remarks, arguing that they trivialised the impact of the controversy on students.The remarks also triggered widespread reactions on social media, with several users criticising Sitharaman's comments as 'deeply insensitive', while accusing the government of downplaying the impact of the paper leak controversy on students.Reacting to her statement, CJP leader Ashutosh Ranka said, "By this logic, every paper in this country should get leaked."In a post on X, the organisation's official handle wrote, "The Finance Minister is claiming NEET students took advantage of the paper leak and worked harder for the re-NEET.Now we're extolling the virtues of paper leaks? This is a shockingly insensitive comment when 20 students have died by suicide because of YOUR incompetence! Shame."The remarks also drew sharp reactions from Opposition leaders. Congress leader Supriya Shrinate took a swipe at Sitharaman, asking her to "please list the benefits" for the 22 students who allegedly died by suicide following the paper leak controversy.Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra also reacted on X, writing, "Honestly this entire Cabinet should resign."

World.title: Oppn rebuffs PM’s late-night video, proposed Fast Track Court law
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Opposition rebuffed PM Narendra Modiâs late-night video and proposed law on fast-track courts for paper leaks, as it reiterated that education minister Dharmendra Pradhanâs resignation is a must for restoration of normalcy in Parliament.

The aggressive stance has put a question mark on if introduction of the new bill in Parliament Monday would bring the opposition bloc back to proceedings after a week of washout.

The hostile tone was set late last night when Rahul Gandhi reacted to Modiâs video statement, saying students are demanding Pradhanâs resignation and âdonât insult their intelligence with this pathetic midnight videoâ. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said opposition is ready for a âdetailed discussion on the education systemâ after Pradhanâs resignation.

TMC MP Sagarika Ghose mocked Modiâs video as âan oh-so-imperious PM who has contempt for Indiaâs public...forced to mumble something in a midnight Insta reel. Sadly, too little, too lateâ.

The anti-BJP parties will meet Monday morning to take a final stand on the issue, but a flurry of statements from opposition leaders Friday suggested that they are unlikely to relent.

CPM MP John Brittas said the opposition is united that the ministerâs resignation has to precede any other business.





Asked if blocking the bill would not be politically risky, Brittas said the main issue is not the legislation but the intent of govt which is not coming through in its actions. âThe govt resolve for studentsâ cause is lacking,â he said.

There is likely to be more drama as TMC chief Mamata Banerjee will Monday visit the protesters at Jantar Mantar.

Senior members of the bloc said they are not bothered about the legislation which is âirrelevantâ to the debate, even though they cannot oppose it for the simple reason that it is propagated as targeting the âpaper leakâ menace.

That has raised a strong possibility of the opposition intensifying its protests to force a washout. Leader of a minor INDIA constituent said BJP will try to project any disturbance that blocks the bill as opposition working against the reforms.

Congress accused the govt of hyping the fast-track court bill as a pioneering move when these courts can be set up under existing laws. âIt is an attempt to show responsiveness when there is none,â AICC spokesman Jairam Ramesh said.

Ramesh said Fast Track Courts only work when investigations are time-bound and there is a political will to see the investigations through. In contrast, he said the Modi govt over 12 years chose to deny paper leaks, like in 2026 and 2024. He said the govt called Sanjeev Mukhiya the âkingpinâ of the 2024 leak, but the CBI is now calling him innocent.

World.title: Army rescues 57 stranded as major flood relief operation begins in Gujarat's Navsari
World.content:
The Indian Army on Saturday rescued 57 people stranded by floodwaters at Tata High School on Ring Road in Gujarat's Navsari district as heavy rainfall continued to batter parts of the state.

Seperately, Army personnel also evacuated vulnerable residents from Sanduri village in the Madhuban Dam area of Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

The rescue operations were launched under the Army's humanitarian assistance and disaster relief initiative following distress calls from flood-hit areas.

Responding to an emergency call, southern command deployed rescue teams to Sanduri village, where Army personnel worked in coordination with the civil administration and local volunteers to shift 23 vulnerable civilians to a designated relief shelter.

The Army said medical assistance was provided on-site, while essential rations and relief supplies were distributed to residents who remained in the village. It added that relief and rescue operations were continuing across the affected areas.

The flooding also disrupted road connectivity in Gujarat. The Ahmedabad district police announced the temporary closure of the Ahmedabad-Viramgam Highway after excessive water flow made the route unsafe.





"No vehicle from Sanand to Viramgam and Viramgam to Sanand is safe to ply over it. We are closing the entire highway for the time being," the Ahmedabad District Police said, according to news agency ANI.

Ahmedabad district collector Bhavya Verma told the news agency that the authorities remained on high alert despite the situation being under control.

"We have also deployed Indian Army and SDRF teams along the Ahmedabad-Rajkot Highway.

The situation is currently under control, though waterlogging persists in several areas. All administrative and rescue teams are actively deployed on the ground. A red alert for heavy rainfall remains in effect for Ahmedabad district tomorrow as well..." Verma told ANI.

He said Dholka and Viramgam recorded the highest rainfall in the district over the past 24 hours, adding that rescue operations were being carried out with the assistance of the SDRF, police and the local administration.

Meanwhile, Gujarat deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi visited flood-affected areas in Umargam of Valsad district on Friday, where he reviewed the situation, interacted with residents and urged people to avoid rumours and follow official advisories.

Earlier this week, the NDRF rescued 67 people, including 25 women and 22 children, from floodwaters in Navsari's Sarikhurad village. In Tapi district, the SDRF rescued 11 stranded villagers, while in Surat more than 4,800 people from urban and rural areas were shifted to relief centres and safer locations as rescue operations continued.

World.title: Ayush ministry seeks OPDs in all military, field hospitals
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has proposed expanding Ayush services across all military and field hospitals, with the Ayush ministry urging the defence ministry to set up dedicated outpatient departments (OPDs) and integrate traditional systems of medicine into healthcare for armed forces personnel.

In a letter to defence minister Rajnath Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush Prataprao Jadhav said the move would complement the armed forces medical services by strengthening preventive, promotive and rehabilitative care for soldiers serving in diverse and often challenging operational environments.

Jadhav noted that while Ayush treatment facilities are already available in a limited number of institutions under the ministry of defence, a large number of military and field hospitals still do not have dedicated Ayush services.

He said expanding these facilities would improve access to evidence-based traditional healthcare, particularly in preventive care, lifestyle management, rehabilitation and overall well-being.

The proposal seeks to integrate Ayush with the existing healthcare framework rather than replace conventional medical services. According to the ministry, the initiative is aimed at creating a more comprehensive and patient-centric model of care by combining modern medicine with traditional systems wherever appropriate.





Jadhav urged the defence ministry to establish Ayush OPDs and treatment facilities in all military and field hospitals, saying the Ayush Ministry was ready to provide technical support, professional guidance and institutional cooperation, including signing an MoU for implementation.

If approved, the proposal would significantly expand Ayush services within the armed forces, advancing the government's push to integrate traditional medicine with mainstream healthcare and improve access to holistic care for defence personnel.

World.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke diagnosed with typhoid
World.content:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday (July 25, 2026) said he had been diagnosed with typhoid, adding that he was undergoing treatment and receiving intravenous medication.

Earlier, he vowed that his illness would not slow the movement seeking Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation (Mr. Pradhan has resigned as Union Education Minister).

In a video message shared on social media, Mr. Dipke said he had been unwell for the past few days and was currently undergoing treatment.

Despite his illness, he thanked CJP supporters for keeping the protests alive across the country and said that the movement would achieve its objective.

"As you know, I have been unwell for the last few days. The reports are out and I have been diagnosed with typhoid," he said.

"The treatment is going on. I am getting IV drips every day. But I want to thank all the cockroaches who are protesting peacefully across the country," he said.

"Congratulations to all of you for making this movement such a big success. I am very sure that if we continue protesting like this, we will get Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation," he said earlier.

The CJP-led agitation, launched over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, has been demanding accountability in the examination system, reforms in recruitment and entrance tests, and Mr. Pradhan's resignation.

The protest gathered support from several public figures, including activist Sonam Wangchuk, who joined the agitation on June 28 and observed a 26-day hunger strike.

Mr. Wangchuk ended his fast earlier this week after the Centre gave written assurances that no cases would be registered against peaceful protesters, Parliament would discuss examination reforms and accountability, and compensation for families of students who died by suicide following the alleged NEET paper leak would be positively considered.

Despite Mr. Wangchuk ending his fast, the CJP has maintained that its protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until Mr. Pradhan steps down from his position.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Dharmendra Pradhan tenders resignation as Union Education Minister
World.content:
Dharmendra Pradhan, in a post on X on Saturday (July 25, 2026), announced that he has tendered his resignation from the post of Union Education Minister.

In a letter posted to X, Mr. Pradhan stated that in order to avoid “anti-national forces” from exploiting the situation at Jantar Mantar and across the nation, and “so that the unity of the country remains intact, so that the future of no student in India gets tangled in legal complexities, and so that our children spend their time studying and focusing on building their careers,” he has decided to quit from his position.

Prime Minister Narendra is yet to provide any public comment on this.

Also Read | The ‘cockroaches’ who refuse to crawl away

Earlier, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has called for a nationwide candle march on Sunday evening (July 26, 2026), in solidarity with victims of police brutality during July 20 march to Parliament.

Meanwhile, the number of FIRs have been filed by the Delhi Police against protesters who participated in the July 20 march to Parliament in the national capital. Among the CJP’s demands are a public apology to the protesting students who were “brutally thrashed” on July 20 and assurance that no FIRs will be lodged against any of them.

World.title: Dharmendra Pradhan tenders resignation as Union Education Minister
World.content:
Dharmendra Pradhan, in a post on X on Saturday (July 25, 2026), announced that he has tendered his resignation from the post of Union Education Minister.

Mr. Pradhan’s resignation comes amid Cockroach Janta Party-led protests at the Jantar Mantar, demanding his accountability over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak and irregularities in the CBSE’s on-screen marking process, besides seeking wider reforms in the conduct of public examinations.

In a letter posted to X, Mr. Pradhan stated that in over to avoid “anti-national forces” from exploiting the situation at Jantar Mantar and across the nation, and “so that the unity of the country remains intact, so that the future of no student in India gets tangled in legal complexities, and so that our children spend their time studying and focusing on building their careers,” he has decided to quit from his position.

Jantar Mantar protest updates on July 25, 2026

“Keeping all of this in mind, I have submitted my resignation to the honourable Prime Minister,” Mr. Pradhan’s letter read.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is yet to provide any public comment on this.

“I express my heartfelt gratitude to the Honourable Prime Minister for his guidance, trust, and constant support. I also extend my thanks to all my esteemed colleagues in the Council of Ministers, officials, and staff of the Ministry, as well as everyone I had the privilege to work alongside. Service to the nation remains the highest priority of my life, and I shall always stay dedicated to it,” Mr. Pradhan added.

Mr. Pradhan began his letter addressing the “young friends.” He noted that “for over four decades, I have been dedicated to students, teachers, and education reform. It has always been my firm belief that an empowered, inclusive, and forward-looking education system forms the bedrock of a strong nation.”

He went on to note that after irregularities came to light during the NEET-UG examination held on May 3, 2026, the Government took immediate cognisance, and “handed over the investigation to the CBI, cancelled the exam, and announced a new date for reexamination.”

“Additionally, it was decided that from next year onwards, this exam will be conducted in Computer-Based Test mode.”

“During this period, our utmost priority was ensuring that the exam for over 20 lakh students was conducted smoothly,” Mr. Pradhan said adding that with the cooperation of students, guardians, and parents, the exam was successfully completed on June 21, 2026.

“From day one, I took responsibility for this and never turned my back on the situation. My resolve was that we will not let the future of any meritorious student be ruined by exam mafias, nor will we allow injustice to happen to any student.”

“However, even during this time, individuals sitting in responsible positions attempted to mislead students and cause disruptions, which pained me deeply,” Mr. Pradhan said, likely referring to Opposition leaders.

“With the blessings of Lord Jagannath ji, I will continue to dedicate myself in every possible way to serving Mother India, the people of Odisha, and fulfilling the aspirations of the country’s youth in the future,” Mr. Pradhan concluded.

Jubilation at Jantar Mantar protest site

Meanwhile, Cockroach Janta Party’s Abhijeet Dipke declared victory at the Jantar Mantar protest site, conveying the news of Mr. Pradhan’s resignation to the protesters.

“We have done it! Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned!” Mr. Dipke told a jubilant crowd.

World.title: FIR against Karnataka BJP MLC C.T. Ravi over alleged hate speech
World.content:
An FIR has been registered against BJP MLC C.T. Ravi at Chikkamagaluru Town Police Station following allegations that he made inflammatory and derogatory remarks against the Muslim community during a protest over the NEET examination controversy.

According to the complaint filed by Mudassir Pasha (36), President of Jamia Masjid, Chikkamagaluru, Ravi allegedly made the remarks during a BJP protest held at Azad Park on July 23 against demonstrations over the alleged NEET examination irregularities.

Based on the complaint, the police registered an FIR against C.T. Ravi, charging him with section 353(2) BNS which deals with making, publishing, or circulating false statements, rumours, or reports with intent to create or promote hatred, ill-will, or enmity between different groups on grounds such as religion, race, language, caste, or community, or which are likely to disturb public tranquillity for further investigation.

‘Derogatory references to Muslims’

The complainant alleged that Ravi questioned the connection between “Mullahs” and the NEET issue besides referring to CAA, NRC, NEET and allegedly branding Muslims as a “tukde gang.” The complaint states that the speech was circulated on social media and contained derogatory references to the Muslim community, with the intention of promoting enmity, disturbing communal harmony, and provoking conflict between communities.

Based on the complaint, Chikkamagaluru Town Police have registered a case and initiated further legal action.

Muslim Okkuta accuses BJP of communal polarisation

Meanwhile, in a press release issued on July 25, the Karnataka Rajya Muslim Okkuta condemned Ravi’s alleged remarks as “shocking and highly provocative” and demanded his immediate arrest. The organisation alleged that the BJP leader had attempted to insult Muslim religious leaders, provoke communal divisions, and divert attention from the nationwide protests.

The Okkuta claimed that students and youth across the country have been protesting against the alleged NEET scam and demanding accountability from the Union Government. It accused the BJP of resorting to communal polarisation instead of addressing public concerns.

The organisation further alleged that Ravi’s comments could disturb communal harmony and spread hatred against a particular community. It urged the Karnataka government to initiate stringent legal action against him without delay.

World.title: Social media posts claim Jamia students detained; police say verification under way
World.content:
A number of X posts on Saturday (July 25, 2026), claimed that some students of Jamia Millia Islamia were detained by Delhi Police as they were returning from the Jantar Mantar protest site, even as police sources said that verification of around 150 persons detained on Friday (July 24, 2026), night was under way.

Several X handles alleged that the students returning to the university after attending the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar were picked up by police.

A police source said around 150 people were detained from different locations during security checks on Friday (July 24, 2026) night, and their identities and backgrounds were being verified. “It was too early to confirm whether those taken into custody included Jamia students,” it said. According to the source, police are examining the details of each detainee before releasing them.

The claims were circulated widely on social media, with users seeking information about those allegedly detained.

Security remained tight across Delhi on Saturday (July 25, 2026), with police maintaining heavy deployment and carrying out checks in the sensitive areas to prevent any breach of law and order.

World.title: T.N. CM Vijay should break silence on lock-up deaths: M.K. Stalin
World.content:
DMK president M.K. Stalin on Saturday (July 25, 2026) condemned Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for “remaining silent and failing to console the family” of a lock-up death victim in Thoothukudi.

“Lock-up deaths are continuing in Tamil Nadu. When will the Chief Minister finally break his silence?” Mr. Stalin asked in a post on social media.

Mr. Stalin recalled that Mr. Vijay had once delivered a forceful speech questioning whether merely saying “sorry” could ever deliver justice, but was now choosing to remain silent instead of acting.

“Are the words accountability and apology missing from the Chief Minister’s dictionary?” he asked.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Houthis claim missile attack on Saudi's Jizan; U.S. military 'disables' tanker trying to evade Iran port blockade
World.content:
Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile attack on the southern Saudi city of Jizan on Saturday (July 25, 2026) , after vowing retaliation against the kingdom for attacks this week. It came after U.S. ally Riyadh struck Houthi military targets, following the Yemeni group announcing a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and hitting its ships in the Red Sea.

The flare-up marks a new front of the West Asia war that has engulfed the region following U.S.-Israeli strikes on Tehran in February, and comes on top of Iran’s parallel blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh’s only other maritime route.

Meanwhile, the U.S. and Iran showed no sign of backing away from their conflict after as they continue to trade strikes. With fighting flaring again and diplomacy uncertain, both sides made moves suggesting an escalation was possible. Earlier on Friday (July 24, 2026), U.S. President Donald Trump described negotiations with Iran as “by far the most serious that we’ve seen”. Trump added that he’s “not in a hurry” to end the war. U.S.

Vowing that Iran “will not bow to U.S.” bullying, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi noted ongoing discussions with two global powers often at odds with Americans — China and Russia — and warned in an interview with the semiofficial news outlet Tasnim that the Islamic Republic is “neither intimidated by threats nor will we yield to pressure.”

World.title: Kandararu Brahmadathan to be appointed Sabarimala Tantri
World.content:
Kandararu Brahmadathan of the Thazhamon Madhom will be appointed the Tantri (Chief Priest) of the Sabarimala Temple, the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) decided on Saturday (July 25, 2026).

The decision was taken at a TDB meeting attended by TDB president K. Jayakumar and members K. Raju and P.D. Santhosh Kumar.

Mr. Brahmadathan, who is the son of former tantri Kandararu Rajeevaru, will hold the position for one year from Chingam 1 of Malayalam era 1202 (August 17, 2026) to Karkkadakam 31, 1202 (August 16, 2027).

Earlier this month, citing ill health, Mr. Rajeevaru had requested that he be relieved as the Tantri.

Mr. Rajeevaru had also been arraigned as an accused in the Sabarimala gold theft case. In a letter to the TDB, Mr. Rajeevaru had also requested that his son succeed him as Sabarimala Tantri.

The Kerala High Court had asked the Travancore Devaswom Board to take a call on the appointment of Mr. Brahmadathan as the Tantri. A Division Bench of Justices V. Raja Vijayaraghavan and K.V. Jayakumar wanted the Court to be informed about the Tantri position by July 27.

World.title: ‘To ensure anti-national forces don’t exploit Jantar Mantar’: Here is the full text of Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation letter to PM Modi
World.content:
Amid mounting pressure due to the nationwide protests by CJP and Opposition parties, Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan has stepped down from his post. He sent his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday.

I have been dedicated to students, teachers, and education reform for more than 4 decades. It has always been my conviction that an empowered, inclusive, and forward-looking education system forms the bedrock of an empowered nation.

I deeply respect the aspirations, emotions, and legitimate expectations of the nation’s youth. Fulfilling the dreams of India’s young generation has been the moral resolve of our political and social life. I express my gratitude to the Honorable Prime Minister for the opportunity to serve the nation under his visionary leadership.

However, irregularities came to light during the NEET-UG examination held on May 3, 2026. Taking immediate cognizance, the Government of India handed over the investigation to the CBI, cancelled the exam, and announced a new date. Along with this, a decision was taken to conduct this exam in CBT (Computer-Based Test) mode starting next year.

During this time, our main priority was to ensure that the re-examination for over 20 lakh students was conducted smoothly. For this, work was carried out using a “whole of government approach.” In this, state governments—especially district administrations—played a crucial role alongside the Government of India. With the cooperation of students, guardians, and parents, this exam was completed on June 21, 2026.

From day one, I took responsibility for this and never turned my back on the situation. My resolve was that we would not let any meritorious student’s prospects be ruined by the examination mafia, nor allow injustice to happen to any student.

The NEET-UG results announced on July 16 were satisfactory, with many meritorious students from underprivileged backgrounds achieving success.



However, during this period, individuals holding responsible positions attempted to create obstacles and mislead several students, which deeply pained my heart.

I have always had unwavering faith in the strength of our democracy and a deep respect for the aspirations, dreams, and expectations of the youth. They are not just India’s future, but the carriers, creators, and architects of a new and developed India (Viksit Bharat).

Looking at the sequence of events over the past 10 days, my heart is deeply distressed. This is not a matter of personal reputation for me.

The youth power of India is the true strength of this country.



My resolve is that we will not let the nation’s youth power fall prey to a web of confusion and misinformation.

To ensure that anti-national forces do not exploit the situation arising at Jantar Mantar and across the country, that national unity remains intact, that no student’s future gets tangled in legal complexities, and that our children can focus their time on studying and building their careers—considering all these factors, I have submitted my resignation to the Honorable Prime Minister.

I express my heartfelt gratitude to the Honorable Prime Minister for his guidance, trust, and continuous support. Additionally, I extend my thanks to all my esteemed colleagues in the Council of Ministers, ministry officials, staff, and everyone with whom I had the privilege to work. Serving the nation remains the highest priority of my life, and I will always stay dedicated to it.

With the blessings of Lord Shri Jagannath Ji, I will continue to dedicate myself in every possible way to serving Mother India, the people of Odisha, and fulfilling the aspirations of the country’s youth in the future.

World.title: As Dharmendra Pradhan resigns, Centre moves in cops to clear protest sites in Delhi

World.title: ‘I failed at it miserably’: Masaba Gupta reveals how a tennis setback shaped her success
World.content:
From missed shots to making bold moves in the world of business with her design and beauty labels, Masaba Gupta has carved a name for herself through sheer grit and determination. However, the road to success was not easy. During a recent conversation with One8 World, she opened up about almost going professional in tennis: “I tried to be a professional tennis player long back. I played pro tennis when I was very young, and I failed at it miserably. It’s because I couldn’t control my mind. I had a lot of physical strength, I was just genetically stronger than the other kids. I could hit the ball harder, reach for it quicker. But I could not control what was going on in my mind. It was that aggression that I couldn’t really harness to make something positive out of it.”

“Today, when I’m running my own businesses, that’s what I do. I use that aggression to my advantage, and try and see how I can harness it positively,” she further added.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by one8 (@one8world)

Dr Divya Shree K R, consultant psychiatrist, Aster CMI Hospital, Bengaluru, says that whether it’s a job application, a creative pursuit, or even a romantic approach, failing can be discouraging. Therefore, she believes understanding the complexity of a ‘victory’ in today’s world and the interplay of affluence, influence, and luck is important in evaluating each failure as it comes and helps us assign blame and assume responsibility for the right reason.

Moving on

However, failure is still a normal part of life, and it doesn’t define your worth. Dr Divya shares some tips to help you bounce back and turn setbacks into stepping stones:

Acknowledge your feelings: It’s okay to feel hurt, angry, or disappointed. Bottling up emotions can hinder healing. Allow yourself to process your feelings in a healthy way, like journaling, talking to a trusted friend, or engaging in a creative outlet.

Reframe the narrative: Don’t view it as a personal failure. Instead, see it as an opportunity to learn and grow. Maybe your skills need some honing, or perhaps the timing wasn’t right.

Analyse the situation: If the opportunity allows, try to understand the reasons for failure. Did they provide any feedback? This can be valuable information to help you improve for next time. However, avoid excessive self-criticism.

Focus on the positive: Failure doesn’t erase your strengths and accomplishments. Take a moment to appreciate your past successes, and remind yourself of your skills and value.



Learn and adapt: Use the experience as a learning opportunity. Did you discover a new skill gap you need to address? Perhaps your approach needs some tweaking. Growth comes from adapting to challenges.

Build Resilience: Failure can be tough, but it also helps build resilience. Each time you overcome a setback, you become better equipped to handle future challenges.

Celebrate small wins: Don’t get discouraged by aiming for giant leaps. Celebrate small victories along the way. This keeps you motivated and reminds you of your progress.

Keep moving forward: Don’t dwell on the rejection. Use it as motivation to keep striving towards your goals. There are many paths to success, so explore new opportunities and keep putting yourself out there.



DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.
