World.title: China’s Summer Hit Recasts the Eight Immortals as Con Artists
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018801/China’s Summer Hit Recasts the Eight Immortals as Con Artists
World.content:
Before they were immortals, they were scammers.

That’s the irreverent premise behind “All Wishes Come True!,” a new Chinese animated comedy that has turned a band of mythological figures from Taoist legend into a summer box-office hit.

Released July 18, the film recasts the Eight Immortals — traditionally symbols of people from all walks of life — as con artists who impersonate gods and deceive worshippers before achieving immortality themselves.

In less than a week, the film has grossed more than 370 million yuan ($51 million), becoming the second highest-grossing domestic animated film of 2026 behind “Boonie Bears: The Hidden Protector.” It also holds an 8.3 rating on Chinese review site Douban, the highest among this summer’s new releases.

The film’s biggest twist unfolds in Penglai, a fairyland where gods and humans coexist under a surprisingly modern bureaucracy governed by an immortals management bureau. Deities are assigned temples, evaluated on performance targets, and ranked on giant leaderboards based on the incense offerings they receive.

Unlike traditional tales of the Eight Immortals’ journey toward enlightenment, the film gives the legendary figures a new beginning: they first appear as schemers targeting the riches of Fu, Lu, and Shou, the three deities of fortune, prosperity, and longevity.

Zhongli Quan, traditionally portrayed as a general who became a Taoist immortal, is reimagined as a con artist who leads the group in impersonating deities. Cao Guojiu, traditionally linked to the Song dynasty (960–1279) imperial court, appears as an official in the immortals management bureau.

After taking over a temple, the group finds itself responsible for granting wishes — and eventually becomes known for catching thieves. Their journey later leads to a clash with the war god Yang Jian.

Director Mu Zhengyang said he designed Penglai as a “first-tier megacity,” where gods and humans operate within a modern social system. “At first, audiences should feel that they’re entering a traditional Eastern fairyland. But once inside, it becomes much more like an amusement park,” he told domestic media.

The film’s character-driven approach also extends to its voice performances. Voice director Chen Hao, who worked on the popular “Ne Zha” films, voices Zhongli Quan, while Tieguai Li’s Chongqing dialect adds regional flavor to the character.

The film’s cultural references have also fueled online discussion. On streaming platform Bilibili, videos decoding more than 100 Easter eggs and hidden details have each attracted nearly one million views.

One widely discussed clue is the Eight Immortals’ temple number — 1350, the same number associated with Sun Wukong, better known as the Monkey King, in the “Book of Life and Death,” a mythical register of the underworld in “Journey to the West,” hinting at his possible appearance later in the story.

The same reinterpretation has also drawn criticism from some viewers, who argue that the film alters the identities and values associated with traditional mythology.

Yang Jian, for example, traditionally portrayed as a righteous war god who protects ordinary people, is reimagined as a figure willing to sacrifice heaven and humanity to save his mother. The film’s other redesigns have also drawn attention, including Cao Guojiu’s portrayal as an overweight, flamboyant official and Lan Caihe’s depiction as a toddler.

The debate also extends to the film’s portrayal of immortality. Through the line, “Only immortals can do good deeds,” it offers a new interpretation that some viewers praised, while others argued it differs from traditional Taoist ideas of attaining eternal life.

The production team, based in southwestern China’s Sichuan province, said the Eight Immortals offer creative space for reinterpretation because many audiences know their famous stories but are less familiar with their broader legends. The filmmakers said they hoped to introduce the figures to a new generation through a fresh retelling.

“We didn’t want to simply bring the Eight Immortals in front of young audiences and tell the same story again,” producer Ying Xujun told domestic media. “We had to create something new for a new generation.”

Editor: Apurva.

(Header image: A poster for “All Wishes Come True!” From Douban)

World.title: At World AI Forum, Four Signs China’s AI Industry Is Growing Up
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018802/At World AI Forum, Four Signs China’s AI Industry Is Growing Up
World.content:
This year’s World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai was larger, more crowded, and more politically prominent than in previous editions.

President Xi Jinping attended the event for the first time, while more than 1,100 companies showcased computing systems, AI agents, robots, and other products aimed at workplaces, factories, and consumers. In-person visits topped 400,000, and tickets were reportedly resold for more than 1,000 yuan.

Xi called for wider access to open-source AI, and China launched a 29-country AI cooperation body, placing issues of governance, access, and international coordination alongside the usual displays of commercial technology.

Beyond the speeches and packed exhibition halls, the most revealing conversations were practical: lowering computing costs, putting AI agents to work, managing new safety risks, and building businesses that can last.

Here are four takeaways from this year’s WAIC.

Computing power gets practical

Computing power was one of the most discussed topics at this year’s WAIC, second only to AI applications by number of related forums. But the focus moved beyond building more data centers or training ever-larger models.

Two questions dominated: what the next generation of computing power might look like, and how to make today’s resources cheaper and more efficient.

At one flagship forum on the future of computing, scientists discussed emerging approaches including quantum computing and space-based computing. Among the speakers was Pan Jianwei, a leading quantum physicist and recent recipient of a top United Nations science award, who outlined recent advances in the field.

Pan also urged caution. Although the field has reached a series of important milestones, he said, building a general-purpose quantum computer capable of quickly solving problems with clear practical value will still require years of sustained research. The academic community, he added, has a responsibility to help the public assess the technology realistically and guard against an industry bubble.

Companies also seemed more focused on improving the efficiency of existing computing resources and reducing the cost of each AI query.

Some were working to improve the performance of models trained mainly on Nvidia chips when deployed on Chinese chips. Others focused on allocating and managing computing resources more efficiently.

Rather than chasing only the most powerful and expensive models, many Chinese AI companies appeared more concerned with making AI cheaper to run.

AI Governance and Safety

AI governance and safety were prominent throughout this year’s WAIC, from high-level forums to the opening ceremony and President Xi Jinping’s speech.

Brian Tse, an AI safety expert and founder and CEO of Concordia AI, said he has seen more discussion in China around cybersecurity and the protection of critical infrastructure, especially the risks posed by frontier AI models.

“The threat landscape is evolving rapidly,” Tse said. “Many experts at the forums expressed concern that threats and potential misuse are developing faster than society’s current defenses.”

The concerns also appeared to be shifting beyond large language models and the harmful content they can generate. More attention was paid this year to the risks posed by autonomous AI agents, which can plan tasks, make decisions, and interact with other tools.

On July 15, just before WAIC, China’s new rules on AI anthropomorphic interaction took effect, targeting services that simulate human personalities and sustained emotional interaction. The rules prohibit providers from offering virtual partners or relatives to minors and bar services from inducing emotional dependence or addiction.

In May, regulators also released guidance on the standardized application and development of AI agents, including plans to explore digital identity management for them.

“China is positioning itself as an architect of multilateral AI governance,” Tse said.

AI lands at work

One phrase heard often at this year’s WAIC was AI’s real-world “landing” — the push to move the technology out of demos and into everyday work. Companies ranging from Tencent and Alibaba to smaller startups showed AI products aimed at offices, factories, and consumer services. AI agents were among the most visible examples.

At booths run by major tech firms, exhibitors demonstrated how agents could be built into corporate workflows, from searching internal documents to generating reports and coordinating routine tasks.

The impact could be broad because many of these companies’ software systems are already embedded in Chinese workplaces. Adding AI agents to existing platforms may prove easier than persuading companies to adopt entirely new tools.

Still, genuinely effective applications appeared limited. Office productivity remained the most obvious use case, while other areas were less developed.

Robotics and embodied AI occupied an entire floor at this year’s WAIC. Visitors could still see robots performing awkward dances or taking six minutes to make a cup of tea. But some companies were beginning to move beyond staged demonstrations, showing robots designed for inspection, manufacturing, logistics, and other industrial uses.

The founder rush

Some of the most revealing conversations at this year’s WAIC took place after the official sessions ended.

Across after-hours gatherings, private meetups, and open-mic sessions, young founders and industry professionals swapped ideas on AI agents, robotics, and productivity tools. Some gatherings ran late into the night, with almost any topic open for discussion.

Many entrepreneurs seemed eager to absorb every new idea, experiment, business opportunity, and professional connection they could find.

But that urgency also carried risks. Some founders said their AI ventures were burning through years of savings. Many still lacked a convincing answer to a basic question: how their projects would generate lasting value and revenue.

That tension ran through WAIC: crowded halls, founders eager to share projects and failures, and a palpable fear of moving too slowly and missing the AI wave. The mood mixed optimism with anxiety, much of it fueled by the speed of the technology and the sheer volume of information surrounding it.

The conversations also suggested a maturing industry. More speakers and founders were asking not only what AI could do, but where it could be useful, how it could be governed, and which businesses could survive once the initial excitement fades.

(Header image: A humanoid robot from a Chinese robotics firm waves Chinese national flags during the 2026 WAIC in Shanghai, July 18, 2026. Ng Han Guan/AP Photo via VCG)

World.title: The Soybean That Built Northeast China
World.content:
In 2020, I traveled to Kaishantun, a town in the Yanbian Korean Autonomous Prefecture near the China-North Korea border. It fit every stereotype of the deindustrialized Northeast. Young people had left. The government had built two rows of barracks-style apartment blocks for the elderly residents who remained. Kaishantun railway station had long been abandoned. On the station sign, the space for the next stop was blank. North Korea lay only a few hundred meters away.

On the walk back, I wandered into a derelict movie theater and discovered several reels of old film. Later restored, they revealed something astonishing: clips of a symphony orchestra and a traditional folk orchestra.

What kind of small town could support two orchestras of its own?

As I dug deeper into the history of my home region, Northeast China, I found that part of the answer lay in a crop that today frequently appears in international headlines: soybeans. A century before China became a major importer of American soybeans, it was the world’s leading producer.

In August 1872, three Japanese army officers, disguised as merchants and acting on the orders of General Saigō Takamori, traveled through “Manchuria,” the term they used for Northeast China. Saigō was studying relations between Japan, Korea, and China as he prepared a future campaign against Korea. A year later, the officers submitted their “Report on an Inspection of Manchuria,” one of Japan’s earliest intelligence briefings on China. The report includes a detailed discussion of soybeans:

“From winter through spring, soybeans are continuously transported by inland waterways. Regardless of the cold, day and night, dozens of horse-drawn carts move in a single direction. Large merchants purchase the beans and pile them into circular mountains more than two rooms across and over 6 meters high … The quantity stored is beyond counting.”

In 1885, another Japanese military officer, Kikuchi Setsuzō, passed through Northeast China on his return from the Russian Empire. Along the way, he studied how Qing forces fed their military horses, which he regarded as superior to those of Japan and Russia. Qing troops processed the residue left after soybean oil extraction into pressed soybean cakes for animal feed. Each cake weighed about 12.5 kilograms and could feed three horses for a day. Kikuchi even claimed such soybean resources would be “indispensable” for training military horses.

In the 19th century, Kikuchi was among the few who grasped soybeans’ strategic significance. The crop had reached Europe and North America in the 18th century but remained largely a botanical curiosity. A handful of enthusiasts, such as the Austro-Hungarian agronomist Friedrich Haberlandt, sought to introduce soybeans into Western diets. Yet while they imported the crop, they did not import the culinary traditions that had made it a staple across Asia.

In East Asia, by contrast, people had accumulated more than a thousand years of experience cooking and consuming soybeans. They also recognized the crop’s value as animal feed. After the Meiji Restoration in 1868, Japanese rice farmers gradually abandoned traditional fish-based fertilizers in favor of soybean cake. Between 1882 and 1902, Japan’s soybean imports increased four-hundredfold.

The Russo-Japanese War of 1904–05 finally alerted the world to soybeans’ importance. European military observers noted that both sides relied heavily on the crop. Japanese forces consumed soybeans directly and used them in military logistics. Russian forces fed them to cavalry horses. Soybean oil served as a raw material for soap and as a lubricant for artillery equipment and wagon axles.

The soybean trade expanded rapidly. A 1911 report from the Customs Service in Shanghai observed that “It is only in the last three years that soya beans have become important in intercontinental commerce,” calling their rapid emergence from obscurity “one of the most remarkable commercial events of recent times.” In the same year, the U.S. ambassador in Beijing told the State Department that Northeast China had until recently been largely unknown for its commercial potential, despite supplying soybeans to global markets. He observed that its economic trajectory was now drawing attention in major cities including New York, London, Hamburg, and Seattle, and attributed this shift to soybeans, whose rapidly growing demand he characterized as “phenomenal in trade annals.”

Estimates suggest that Northeast China accounted for between 16% and 42% of global soybean production between 1908 and 1930, shipping soybeans, soybean oil, and soybean cakes to the rest of China, Japan, and Europe. Until the eve of World War II, China produced more than 80% of the world’s soybeans. The crop became widely known as the “Manchurian bean.”

Soybeans were also among the most important exports of a then largely impoverished China. After World War I, their importance grew rapidly, and by the 1920s they had overtaken tea and silk to become China’s leading export, accounting for more than 20% of export earnings.

As trade expanded, so did Japan’s territorial ambitions. In the run-up to Japan's formal annexation of Korea in 1910, Yanbian became a frontier along the China-Korea border where Chinese and Japanese spheres of influence met directly. Japanese strategists viewed the wider Yanbian area as a gateway to the interior of Northeast China and sought to build a railway linking the Korean port of Chongjin with China’s inland Northeast. General Hasegawa Yoshimichi, commander of Japanese forces in Korea, regarded Yanbian as a vital supply corridor for sustaining colonial rule on the peninsula. He advocated occupying the region to secure access to strategic commodities such as soybeans.

Over the following three decades, Japan steadily expanded its influence in Northeast China. In 1931, Japanese forces seized the region and took control of its economic resources. This expansion, justified in the name of protecting economic “lifelines,” would later extend across Asia during the Pacific War to the oil fields of Burma, Sumatra, and Borneo; the rubber plantations of Malaya; and the chromium and iron deposits of the Philippines.

In Yanbian, war and colonial rule only reinforced the region’s economic importance. Beyond soybeans, Japanese authorities coveted the region’s timber. In Kaishantun they established the Eastern Manchuria Rayon Pulp Company, whose output eventually surpassed that of most producers in Japan. After the Chinese Communist Party won the civil war and founded the People’s Republic of China in 1949, the new state’s flagship pulp and paper enterprise was established in the same town.

Factories brought more than jobs. They brought hospitals, movie theaters, and even symphony orchestras.

Yet by then Northeast China was no longer the sole center of the global soybean trade. By the early 20th century, American farmers were already familiar with soybeans, using them to replenish soil and support other crops. After the Russo-Japanese War, however, the crop’s industrial potential attracted growing attention.

One unlikely champion was Henry Ford. He used soybean protein and soybean-oil derivatives in automotive components and in 1941 unveiled a prototype car with body panels made largely from soybean-based plastic. To demonstrate its strength, he famously struck it with an axe.

Ford’s soybean car was hardly a commercial success, but it generated publicity for the crop. When Japan severed America’s access to Asian supply routes during the Pacific War, soybeans were transformed from an industrial curiosity into a strategic resource. Combined harvesters and advances in plant breeding helped American farmers scale up production.

By the 1950s, the center of gravity in soybean production had shifted decisively to the Americas.

One final piece was still missing from the modern soybean map: Brazil. In the early 1970s, a major El Niño event, a climate pattern that warms the Pacific Ocean, devastated the Peruvian anchoveta fishery, a key source of animal feed, driving demand for soybean meal. Prices surged, and in 1973 the Nixon administration imposed restrictions on soybean exports.

History then took an ironic turn. Japan, heavily dependent on imported American soybeans, increased its investment in South American agriculture, while Brazil’s agricultural research agency, Embrapa, developed soybean varieties suited to tropical conditions. The result was a dramatic expansion of Brazilian production.

In 2024, more than 70% of China’s soybean imports came from Brazil. When trade tensions between China and the United States intensified in 2025, Brazil became China’s principal alternative for former U.S. suppliers.

Northeast China remains the country’s most important soybean-growing region, producing the beans that become tofu and soy milk on Chinese tables. But it no longer supplies the world with soybean oil and soybean meal. Once-thriving industrial towns have been swept up in the tide of deindustrialization, leaving behind abandoned railway stations and empty movie theaters.

From an unassuming plant in Northeast China to one of the world’s most traded agricultural commodities, the soybean’s history is ultimately a story of globalization. A soybean harvested in Paraguay may be processed in Argentina, sold to China by a trading house in Geneva, and eventually find its way into milk, cakes, or meat products. It shapes what we eat, how we farm, and how nations interact with one another. It also shapes the fate of countless small towns, including places like Kaishantun.

(Header image: A soybean field in Xingkai Lake Farm, Heilongjiang province, 2023. VCG)

World.title: IBON Foundation: Upper-middle income milestone doesn’t reflect Filipinos’ realities
World.content:
BIRDTALK MIDYEAR 2026. Executive Director Sonny Africa and Research Head Rosario Guzman share their insights on the country's economic situation during IBON Foundation’s Birdtalk Midyear 2026 at UP Diliman.

Despite the World Bank's recent upper-middle-income upgrade, think tank IBON Foundation warns that the country's income classification masks deeper structural weaknesses in employment, inequality, and industrial development

MANILA, Philippines – Ahead of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s fourth State of the Nation Address (SONA), IBON Foundation warned that the Philippines’ recent economic upgrade to upper-middle-income (UMIC) status masks the daily struggles of millions of Filipinos, calling the figure detached from reality during its Midyear Birdtalk on Wednesday, July 23 at the University of the Philippines Diliman.

IBON Foundation executive director Sonny Africa described the World Bank classification as a “mere statistical classification,” saying it masks deeper structural problems in employment, inequality, and industrial development.

“The growth model that resulted in the statistical reclassification can expand economic output, but is unable to create decent work with livable pay for the majority of Filipinos,” Africa said.

The Marcos administration has described the World Bank reclassification as a “vote of confidence” in its economic policies, a characterization that IBON disputed during the forum.

A ‘disguised crisis of joblessness’

While the government frequently highlights low official unemployment rates, IBON’s analysis indicated that employment has increasingly become a coping mechanism rather than a pathway out of poverty.

According to the group’s data, a staggering 78% of the workforce, about 38.7 million Filipinos, are trapped in “vast informality”. The think tank noted that this includes millions of self-employed individuals, unpaid family workers, and laborers in unregistered establishments enduring volatile working conditions.

UPPER-MIDDLE-INCOME. IBON Foundation presents Philippines’ position among upper-middle-income economies based on the World Bank’s 2025 gross national income (GNI) per capita classification during its Birdtalk Midyear 2026 forum at UP Diliman on Wednesday, July 23. Image from IBON Foundation

Although the country’s economic growth was enough to qualify it for UMIC, IBON stressed that the purchasing power of the working class has eroded, estimating that the average minimum wage is worth 21% less today than it was in 1989.

The group’s presentation showed that 14.4 million families, representing roughly 70 million Filipinos or 62% of the population, remain poor or low-income. This reality, IBON argued, contrasts sharply with the immense concentration of wealth at the top of the economic pyramid, driven by an exclusionary growth model that favors large conglomerates.

The decline of domestic production

IBON argued that these labor market conditions stem from the long-term weakening of the country’s productive sectors.

“It is critical to reverse agricultural decline, industrial erosion, and worsening technological dependence, with a determined program of rural development and Filipino industrialization that qualitatively transforms the economy’s producing structure,” Africa said.

According to them, instead of building local industries, the Philippines has undergone decades of deindustrialization. IBON’s data showed that manufacturing has dropped to just 17.4% of the country’s gross domestic product, its smallest share in 76 years, since 1949.

Meanwhile, the agricultural sector has shrunk to a historic low of 7.9%. The think tank asserted that this lack of a strong industrial and agricultural foundation is exactly why the economy struggles to generate high-quality, secure jobs, exposing the “exhaustion” of the country’s growth model.

GROWTH AND POVERTY. IBON Foundation presents data comparing annual GDP per capita with self-rated poverty. Image from IBON Foundation

Pax Silica and foreign-reliant development

IBON cited the US-led Pax Silica alliance as an example of the development model it argues has deepened the country’s dependence on foreign capital. The initiative aims to transform a portion of New Clark City into an AI-native “Economic Security Zone” anchored by foreign tech giants.

However, IBON also warned that without deliberate state intervention, such as binding requirements for technology transfer and local supplier development, these high-tech hubs will not lead to genuine Filipino industrialization.

“Mega-hyped efforts like the US-led Luzon Economic Corridor and Pax Silica will not deliver promised industrialization because these will be implemented under the same one-sided foreign investment regime that has held the economy back for decades,” Africa said.

Under proposed “joint governance” frameworks with the United States, IBON raised concerns that the Philippines may simply remain locked in a subordinate role within the global value chain. The think tank argued that the country risks merely supplying prime real estate, critical minerals, and cheap labor for foreign supply chains, while foreign corporations retain control over operations, technologies, and profits.

“There will likely be a lot of optimism during the SONA. But this will ring hollow because the Marcos administration is unable to deliver real economic reforms while the people’s conditions continue to worsen,” Africa said.

IBON argued that national development cannot be measured by gross national income (GNI) averages alone or achieved solely through foreign investment enclaves. Instead, the group said the country needs secure employment, stronger domestic agriculture and manufacturing, and economic growth that translates into tangible improvements in Filipinos’ lives.– Rappler.com

World.title: Still swinging: What’s next for Manny Pacquiao’s boxing career
World.content:
At 47, Manny Pacquiao does not plan to stop fighting anytime soon as the Filipino boxing icon eyes both professional and exhibition bouts, with the postponed rematch against Floyd Mayweather Jr. still in the cards

Father Time is undefeated, but Manny Pacquiao keeps resisting.

At 47, Pacquiao does not plan to stop fighting anytime soon — the Filipino boxing icon eyeing both professional and exhibition bouts through 2026 and 2027, with a long-awaited rematch against Floyd Mayweather Jr. still firmly on the agenda.

So what is next?

Top priority

According to Manny Pacquiao Promotions chief executive officer Jaspreet “Jas” Mathur, reviving the postponed Mayweather rematch is the priority.

Pacquiao and Mayweather, who first met in their blockbuster 2015 showdown, had agreed to face each other again in a professional fight scheduled for September to be streamed globally by entertainment giant Netflix.

A quick look at Netflix’s catalog shows the rematch remains on the platform’s schedule, but the fight has been postponed indefinitely due to legal and contractual disputes involving Mayweather’s camp.

“He has a long way to go. He’ll definitely be in a lot of exhibitions over the next few years but we ran into a little bit of a hiccup with the Mayweather fight that was initially planned for September of this year,” Mathur said of Pacquiao.

“Based of that, we didn’t entertain other exhibition offers that were there around. We’re also looking at the right partners to work for exhibitions, and then from there, also the right opponents for pro fight. There’ll be a lot of things coming up.”

“There’s a plan to have a fight for this year and then to roll into next year with the big fight.”

Mayweather has been embroiled in legal trouble after CSI Sports Events, which was contracted to produce the American’s exhibition against former world heavyweight champion Mike Tyson and rematch against Pacquiao this year, sued him for breach of contract.

CSI Sports Events claimed that Mayweather breached their agreement when he agreed to fight Greek kickboxer Mike Zambidis in an exhibition bout scheduled for June 27. The fight, however, never took place.

Mathur, though, said Mayweather was not to blame for the postponement of his rematch with Pacquiao.

“It’s just a very, very big mess and just a very complicated situation that was really caused by one person. For the record, this whole mess that happened is not really Floyd’s fault but we have to untangle it. There’s been a lot of work and his team is working, they’re doing what they need to do to untangle certain things,” said Mathur.

“Next year, 100 percent, it’s going to happen.”

By the time the rematch rolls around, however, Mayweather — who will turn 50 in February — and Pacquiao are far removed from the fighters who squared off in their 2015 clash famously dubbed the “Fight of the Century.”

The fight shattered revenue records by generating over $600 million, although the action in the ring proved underwhelming, with a defensive-minded Mayweather warding off Pacquiao to score a unanimous decision win and stay unbeaten.

Mayweather has fought professionally only twice since, beating Andre Berto in 2015 and Conor McGregor in 2017 to raise his record to 50-0 before retiring for the third time in his career.

For Mathur, having Pacquiao and Mayweather back in the ring together is still a sight to behold despite their age.

“Everybody wants to see Floyd and Manny one more time. That’s what’s going to break all records. That’s what’s going to be the most viewed event again in today’s era, in the streaming era,” he said.

“I think people are always going to be interested in watching that fight. These guys, they’re an anomaly, each one of them, whether Floyd or Manny. Age doesn’t really matter in that spectrum between these two. Everybody’s going to watch the fight. The people that say they’re not going to watch the fight are going to be the first ones to watch the fight.”

“Floyd’s not backing down from this, and neither is Manny.”

Do more

Pacquiao had drawn the curtains on his legendary career in 2021 following his unanimous decision loss to Cuban Yordenis Ugas in their title fight for the World Boxing Association welterweight belt.

But after back-to-back election setbacks that saw him lose in both the presidential and senatorial races in 2022 and 2025, respectively, Pacquiao came out of retirement last year to challenge Mexican-American Mario Barrios for the World Boxing Council welterweight title.

Then 46 years old, Pacquiao fell short in resetting his record as the oldest welterweight world champion as Barrios — who is 16 years younger — narrowly retained the belt by way of a majority draw.

Pacquiao, boxing’s only eight-division world champion, believes he has plenty of gas left in the tank, especially with a longer preparation period for a fight.

The campaign period for the 2025 elections ended in May, with Pacquiao taking on Barrios just a little over two months after in July.

“I can do more. I can do more than that. I can still feel like I can still fight and I’m strong because I’m [a] disciplined person, [with] the way I eat, everything like that,” Pacquiao told the Ring Magazine program Inside The Ring in April.

“To prepare is not two months or two and a half months. You need long preparation because you need your body to have rest during the heavy training days.”

Even now that he is a grandfather, Pacquiao makes sure to keep himself in form.

“At the age of 30-plus, 40-plus, your metabolism is becoming slower. Your recovery is not that easy compared before when you were young. What I discovered is you’re getting slower if you don’t handle it. But there’s a way that you can stay fit, stay in shape, [retain] speed. You can get that as long as you’re taking care of your body,” Pacquiao said.

Other prospects

When it comes to other professional fights for Pacquiao, Mathur said anything is possible.

Talks were in place for Pacquiao to face reigning WBA welterweight champion Rolly Romero early in 2026, but negotiations fell through.

Romero is now set to tangle with Teofimo Lopez in August for his first title defense.

“I actually wanted to put the Rolly fight together. That was my plan from the beginning. I was even talking about it last year because I’m with Manny already and Rolly’s also with me, in my company, Limitless. Rolly is also a dear friend. That’s a very direct situation. But Rolly’s fighting, he has another fight against Teo,” said Mathur.

Mathur also confirmed the possibility of Pacquiao locking horns with reigning WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia, who won the belt following a unanimous decision victory over Barrios in February.

Garcia, though, already has a fight lined up as he is set to defend his title against Conor Benn in September.

“Everyone’s on the table. It’s all on the table,” said Mathur.

But for Mathur, the goal is to bring the Pacquiao-Mayweather rematch into fruition.

“We have to focus on what’s in front of us right now,” he said. “We want to break records right now. That’s what we want to do.” – Rappler.com

World.title: [OPINION] Para sa aking mga kapatid
World.content:
An INC member pens an open letter to his fellows: 'Ang hindi ko lang maunawaan, bakit ang imbestigasyon kay Pang. Ferdinand Marcos at kanyang mga kaalyado ay nararapat para sa hustisya at katotohanan, pero pagdating kay VP Sara Duterte at Sen. Rodante Marcoleta, ito ay panggigipit at pamumulitika lamang?'

“Huwag kayong padaya kaninuman sa pamamagitan ng mga pangangatuwirang walang kabuluhan, sapagkat dahil nga sa mga ito, ang Diyos ay napopoot sa mga suwail. (…)

Sapagkat pawang mabuti, matuwid at totoo ang ginagawa ng namumuhay sa liwanag. Sikapin ninyong matutunan kung ano ang kalugud-lugod sa Panginoon.

Huwag kayong makibahagi sa mga gawain ng kadiliman na walang ibinubungang mabuti. Sa halip ay ibunyag ninyo ang mga iyon.”

Efeso 5:6, 9-11

– Excerpt from a weekend INC worship service, June 6, 2026

Bago ang lahat, nais kong humingi ng paumanhin.

Sa aking mga kaibigan, kakilala, at kapwa Pilipino na nalilito, naguguluhan, at nagagalit sa mga nagaganap.

Sa ating Panginoong Diyos, dahil sa lungkot, pangamba, at pagkadismaya na bumabalot sa atin.

At sa aking mga kapatid sa Iglesia Ni Cristo, mga taong lubos kong tinitingala ngunit kailangan kong tawagan ng pansin. Mahal ko kayong lahat, ngunit ito rin ang nagtulak sa akin para ihayag ang matagal ko nang napapansin.

Pinakinggan ko kayo noon. Sana’y mabigyan niyo rin ako ng pagkakataon ngayon.

Selective justice

“Dapat panagutin ang lahat ng mapatutunayang sangkot sa kurapsyon na yan, sinuman sila, anuman ang kanilang posisyon sa gobyerno, dapat silang panagutin.”

– Bro. Bienvenido Santiago Jr., INC General Evangelist at Rally for Transparency and a Better Democracy, November 16, 2025

Matapos malantad ang matinding katiwalian kaugnay ng flood control projects, sunod-sunod ang mga demonstrasyon na nananawagan sa imbestigasyon at pagpapanagot sa mga maysala. Isa ang INC sa mga nagsulong ng parehong layunin at nanawagan sa administrasyong Marcos na seryosohin ito.

Kaisang-diwa ako dito. Tama lang na ipaglaban ang katotohanan at katarungan.

Ang hindi ko lang maunawaan, bakit ang imbestigasyon kay Pang. Ferdinand Marcos at kanyang mga kaalyado ay nararapat para sa hustisya at katotohanan, pero pagdating kay VP Sara Duterte at Sen. Rodante Marcoleta, ito ay panggigipit at pamumulitika lamang?

Oo, mas malaki ang trilyones na nilimas sa flood control kumpara sa milyon-milyong hindi maipaliwanag na confidential funds o undeclared campaign donations, ngunit hindi ba’t dapat mabigyang-linaw ang parehong isyu? Bakit nagbabago ang pananaw natin, depende sa personalidad na nasasakdal?

Tayo na ang nagsabi: “Selective justice is INJUSTICE”

Muli, tama at makatarungan lang na kalampagin ang gobyerno na panagutin ang mga sangkot sa flood control corruption, ngunit ang panawagang ito ay mawawalan ng kredibilidad at magiging kaduda-duda kung isasantabi na lang ang iba pang isyu ng katiwalian.

Tayo ba ay para sa katotohanan at katarungan, o nais lamang ipagtanggol ang kaalyado at tuligsain ang kalaban?

Accountability

“Kaya natin sila pinili at ibinoto sa ating pag-aakala na sila po ay gagawa ng mabuti sa kapakanan po ng sambayanang Pilipino.

Pero sila po ang sumira sa pagtitiwala nating iyon.“

– Bro. Arnel Tumanan at EDSA Rally, July 1, 2026

Una, naniniwala ako na may mga kritisismo sa INC na paninira o pang-uusig lamang. Hindi ako sang-ayon sa mga gawa-gawang paratang, at umaasa ako na mabigyan rin sila ng pagkakataong maunawaan ang ating pananampalataya.

Ikalawa, hindi rin ako sang-ayon na wala tayong karapatang mag-rally gayong binoto natin sila. Constitutional right ng bawat mamamayang Pilipino na ihayag ang kanilang mga saloobin, at dapat lamang na singilin ang mga opisyal na pinagkatiwalaan natin.

Ngunit, naniniwala ako na maling ituring na pang-uusig kaagad ang lahat ng puna, lalo kung ito ay nakaaapekto na sa buong bansa.

Para ba talaga saan, o kanino, tayo tumitindig?

Mula Pagsamba ng Kabataan hanggang sa katandaan, laging pinapaalala ang kahalagahan ng katapatan at pananagutan. Hinahanap sa bawat kapatid ang mga katangiang nakasulat sa Bibliya, at handa tayong tawagan ng pansin ang mga pagkukulang sa layong maging sakdal at kalugod-lugod ang ating paglilingkod sa Panginoong Diyos.

Masigasig tayo sa loob ng Iglesia, pero ganito rin ba tayo para sa bayan?

Ang pandarambong ni Joseph Estrada, pandaraya ni Gloria Arroyo, pork barrel sa ilalim ni Noynoy Aquino, at extrajudicial killings ni Rodrigo Duterte ay ilan lang sa mga isyung yumanig sa publiko, ngunit nakabibingi ang katahimikan natin noon. Tanda ko pa ang tagubilin na iwasan ang pakikilahok sa rally at anumang pagtuligsa sa gobyerno dahil ito ay pakikialam sa makalupa, maka-sanlibutan, at maruming mundo ng pulitika.

Ngayon, hindi na maikukubli ang ating kulay sa pangunguna ni Senator Marcoleta at sunod-sunod nating kilusan.

Ano po ang nagbago?

Ipinaglalaban ba talaga natin ang kapakanan ng bayan, o kung saan lang tayo makikinabang?

Opo, sumasampalataya ako na bumoboto tayo sa pag-aakalang gagawin ng mga pinuno ang tama at makatarungan, at wala na tayong kinalaman sa kanilang mga pasya lalo sa katiwalian.

Ngunit, mahirap na laging magtago at magpanggap na “nabudol”, lalo kung ang pinag-uusapan ay mga kandidatong may kasaysayan ng pang-aabuso, pandarambong, at paglabag sa karapatang pantao.

Lantad na iyon, at maraming nagbabala na maaaring maulit ang lahat nang iyon kung makabalik sa Malacañang ang pinatalsik na dinastiya. Sa kabila nito, kanino ulit natin ipinagkatiwala ang kapangyarihan?

Kay Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

Lagi nating sinasabi na hindi sila nakinig sa Iglesia, ngunit hindi ba tayo rin?

Hindi ba marapat lang aminin na nagkamali tayo at tama nga sila?

Maraming nagsasabing sila ay para sa pananagutan.

Sana ay pangatawanan natin ito at simulan sa ating sarili.

Iyon ang accountability.

We are one

Kasabay ng pagtatapos ng rally noong July 2, nagkaroon ng tahimik ngunit natatanging pagsamba sa Templo Central. Tila sorpresa at biglaan ito dahil hindi man lang napuno ang left and right wing, ngunit nagpasya akong saksihan ang pangangasiwa ng Kapatid na Angelo Eraño Manalo, ang pangunahing katuwang ng Tagapamahalang Pangkalahatan.

“Huwag kayong mabalisa tungkol sa anumang bagay. Sa halip, hingin ninyo sa Diyos ang lahat ng inyong kailangan sa pamamagitan ng panalanging may pasasalamat.

At ang kapayapaan ng Diyos na hindi kayang maunawaan ng tao ang siyang mag-iingat sa inyong puso at pag-iisip dahil sa inyong pakikipag-isa kay Cristo Jesus.“

Filipos 4:6-7

– Excerpt from a Special Worship Service officiated by Bro. Angelo Eraño Manalo, INC Central Temple, July 2, 2026

Muli akong nabuhayan ng loob.

Sa gitna ng sumasamang kalagayan ng mundo, narito ang Pamamahala, pinapaalala kung paano ba talaga pinatutunayan ang pananalig sa Ama ayon sa Biblia.

Lubos akong nasisiyahan sa tuwing nakikita ko ang bawat kapatid na masiglang nagkakaisa sa mga pagsamba, aktibidad, at paglilingkod sa Diyos. Ngunit sana, isaisip rin natin ito:

We are one, but for what cause, and at what cost?

Napakasama na ng sanlibutan. Laganap ang matinding katiwalian at mga hipokritong nagmamalinis para sa makasariling hangarin, kaya nararapat lamang na ipaglaban natin ang katotohanan at katarungan nang buong tapang, buong sigasig, at walang pinapaboran.

Ngunit, huwag sana tayong mahuhulog sa mga usapang puno ng poot, karahasan, pagtutungayaw, at pagbabanta. Matuto tayong manindigan ngunit mapagmatiyag laban sa pandaraya ng kadiliman na nais pagsamantalahan ang mabuti nating panawagan.

Tandaan po natin: tayo ay Iglesia Ni Cristo.

Taglay natin ang banal Niyang pangalan.

Huwag nating hayaang ito ay madungisan.

Para kay Rodante Marcoleta, hindi ka lamang senador: ikaw ay aking kapananampalataya. Hindi man ako parating sang-ayon sa iyo, nagpapasalamat ako dahil hindi tulad ng iba, nagpakatapang kang harapin ang iyong kaso. Nananalangin ako sa Ama na sana’y pagkalooban ka Niya ng lakas at mahayag ang buong katotohanan.

Para sa aking mga kababayan, muli akong humihingi ng paumanhin. Hindi man tayo nagkakasundo sa pananampalataya, sana ay magkaisa pa rin tayo tungo sa tunay na katarungan para sa bayan.

At para sa aking mga kapatid, marahil ay nagtataka kayo o baka masama ang tingin sa akin. Ako po ay lumaki sa Templo Central, naging masiglang mang-aawit sa PNK, pangulo ng kapisanan, naglingkod sa INCTV, at nakadapuang-palad ang Kapatid na Eduardo Manalo sa kanilang mga pagdadalaw at Balikbayan Day.

Hindi ako ministro, hindi manggagawa, at hindi nagmula sa ganoong sambahayan, ngunit tulad ninyo, mahal ko ang Iglesia Ni Cristo.

Taliwas sa hangarin ng mga lumalaban, hindi ko nais umalis dito o makita ang pagbagsak nito. Lubos akong nanghahawak sa ating pananampalataya, at paninindigan ko ito hanggang sa wakas.

Ngunit ang pag-ibig ring iyon ang nagtulak sa akin na tawagan ng pansin ang mga nakikita kong mali at paglabag. Hindi ko hahayaang mabulag at maligaw tayo ng kasamaang mapanlinlang, kaya’t sana ay alalahanin natin ang tunay na kahulugan ng pagiging Iglesia Ni Cristo:

Marangal,

Naninindigan sa tama,

At isinasabuhay ang katapatan at pananampalatayang itinuro ng Panginoong Jesucristo.

“Bilang pagtatapos, mga kapatid, lagi ninyong isaisip ang mga bagay na karapat-dapat at kapuri-puri: mga bagay na totoo, marangal, matuwid, malinis, kaibig-ibig, at kagalang-galang.

Isagawa ninyo ang lahat ng inyong natutunan, tinanggap, narinig at nakita sa akin. Sa gayon, sasainyo ang Diyos na nagbibigay ng kapayapaan.“

Filipos 4:8-9

Sa ating muling pagsasama-sama, sa kapilya man o lansangan, nawa’y maghari sa atin hindi ang galit o poot, kung hindi ang pag-ibig at paglingap ng Ama na Siyang magbibigay ng tunay na katarungan at pagtatagumpay.

Siya ang ating kanlungan.

Lagi lamang nating tuparin ang Kanyang kalooban.

Tulungan nawa tayo ng Panginoong Diyos. – Rappler.com

Nathaniel Ocampo (not his real name) is an active member of the Iglesia Ni Cristo in Metro Manila. He used to be a choir member and is now part of INC’s Christian Family Organizations.

Rappler agreed to allow the author to use a pseudonym for security purposes.

World.title: Ombudsman files 14 counts of graft vs Ilonggo lawmaker linked to contractor
World.content:
'While sitting in Congress, [Representative Jojo] Ang holds a stake in a construction firm that won ₱214 million in DPWH contracts — and was paid nearly ₱199 million for them,' the Ombudsman says

MANILA, Philippines – The Office of the Ombudsman filed 14 counts of graft with the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan on Saturday, July 25, against USWAG Ilonggo Representative James “Jojo” Ang Jr., who’s allegedly linked to a construction firm.

“While sitting in Congress, [Representative] Ang holds a stake in a construction firm that won ₱214 million in DPWH contracts — and was paid nearly ₱199 million for them,” the Office of the Ombdusman said in a statement.

“The Constitution is clear: no lawmaker may be financially interested in a government contract during his term. Conflict of interest is not a gray area. It does not require proof that a deal was rigged or that cash changed hands — only that a public official profited, or stood to profit, from a government contract while in office. Here, and in many cases, the clear and thick constitutional line is constantly and blatantly being crossed,” it added.

The cases are for alleged violation of section 3(h) of Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act or Republic Act No. 3019. This provision punishes individuals who have direct or indirect “pecuniary interest in any business or contract or transaction in connection with which he intervenes or takes part in his official capacity.”

These cases are bailable.

The filing came two days before President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s 4th State of the Nation Address on Monday, July 27. – Rappler.com

World.title: Marcos signs law ensuring support for public schools in far-flung areas
World.content:
LAST MILE. A teacher talks with her students at the Pulong Mindanao Elementary School, a last mile school in Sta. Maria, Laguna.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. enacts the Last Mile and GIDA Schools Act days before delivering his fifth State of the Nation Address

MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has signed into law a measure institutionalizing support for public schools located in geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas (GIDA) in the country.

Marcos enacted Republic Act (RA) No. 12321 or the “Last Mile and GIDA Schools Act” on Wednesday, July 22, and was made public on Friday, July 24. It was just days before delivering his fifth State of the Nation Address on Monday, July 27.

Under the law, last mile and GIDA schools refer to those located in “remote, hard-to-reach, underserved, or economically disadvantaged communities where access to safe, adequate, and quality basic education is significantly constrained by limitations in infrastructure, resources, personnel, and prevailing social and environmental conditions.”

The Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM 2) said that there are 9,000 last mile schools in the country, catering to 1.6 million students. Half of these schools are located in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao. (READ: 1,500 public schools don’t have electricity; 1,000 without toilets)

Many last mile and GIDA schools still have multi-grade classrooms. In this set-up, two or more grade levels simultaneously use a classroom, with only one teacher facilitating their lessons and activities.

RA 12321 institutionalized the Last Mile and GIDA Schools Program under the Department of Education (DepEd) to address gaps in resources, facilities, and other essential education inputs in schools and communities that have not met standard allocation criteria, particularly in the GIDAs.

Here are the indicators of last mile and GIDA schools:

Public schools with more than 75% of learners belonging to IP groups

Located in or serving communities affected by conflict, insecurity, disaster vulnerability, or other conditions that significantly impede safe access to education

Any other indicators deemed necessary by the DepEd

The law mandates that students shall have access to a public school within a walkable distance of three kilometers from their residence.

“Where access is not feasible due to terrain, geography, or safety considerations, the DepEd and local government units (LGUs) concerned shall provide support services to learners through the provision of alternative delivery modes and transportation, respectively,” the law provided.

With this, the DepEd is tasked to adopt and implement a national school accessibility standard for school sites, as well as construction standards for last mile and GIDA schools.

Also, the DepEd has one year from the law’s effectivity to develop a National Last Mile and GIDA Schools Mapping System, which will serve as basis for planning, resource allocation, and program implementation.

The DepEd will have to collaborate with various government agencies, LGUs, civil society organizations, and other stakeholders to provide roads, electricity, internet connectivity, and transportation, among others, to the last mile and GIDA schools.

According to the law, teachers and non-teaching personnel assigned to last mile and GIDA schools must have a comprehensive support package that includes the following:

Additional compensation and allowances

Housing and accommodation support

Professional development and teacher pipeline

Localized recruitment and engagement mechanisms

The EDCOM 2 found that only 0.13% of Grade 12 learners in last mile and GIDA schools, Indigenous Peoples (IP) Education, and Madrasah Education Program, and hardship post schools reached proficiency level in the National Achievement Test for school year 2023 to 2024.

“This suggests that proficiency gaps are even more severe in structurally disadvantaged school settings, reinforcing the need for equity-weighted learning recovery and school support so vulnerable learners are not left further behind as they complete basic education,” it said in its final report published in January. – Rappler.com

World.title: Phivolcs: 4.8-magnitude quake hits Balut Island, Sarangani
World.content:
INQUIRER FILES

MANILA, Philippines — Another aftershock from the Mindanao quake last June jolted Balut Island in Sarangani on Saturday afternoon, July 25, the Philippine Institution of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) reported.

In its earthquake bulletin, a 4.8 magnitude earthquake struck Balut Island at 2.46 p.m. The epicenter was found 10 kilometers southwest of the island with a reported depth of 10 kilometers, according to Phivolcs.

READ: Magnitude 5.0 quake strikes off Sarangani, Davao Occidental

World.title: No gun ban for Marcos’ 5th Sona, PNP clarifies
World.content:
Philippine National Police headquarters in Camp Crame. File photo

MANILA, Philippines — No gun ban will be in effect on Monday, July 27, during President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s fifth State of the Nation Address (Sona), the Philippine National Police (PNP) clarified.

“The PNP has not issued any directive imposing a nationwide gun ban for the event. However, existing laws, local ordinances, and established security protocols remain in effect,” the agency said in a statement on Saturday.

READ: PNP sees no security threat to Marcos’ 5th Sona

Article continues after this 

“As part of the security preparations for the Sona, police personnel will strictly enforce restrictions on the carrying of firearms and other deadly weapons in designated security areas and other locations where such restrictions are authorized,” it added.

This came after the National Capital Region Police Office announced earlier this week that all permits to carry firearms outside residences will be suspended on Monday for the Sona.

Over 21,000 law enforcers will be deployed for security measures for the Sona, the PNP previously said, noting that no threats had been monitored for the president’s annual address. /jpv

World.title: Gatchalian hopes Sona outlines plans to address PH education crisis
World.content:
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian. INQUIRER PHOTO / NIÑO JESUS ORBETA

MANILA, Philippines — As President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. prepares to deliver his fifth State of the Nation Address (Sona) on Monday, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian on Saturday expressed hope that the President would outline plans to address the country’s education crisis.

Gatchalian also said he expects Marcos to report on the implementation of the historic 2026 education budget, under which the sector received a record P1.35 trillion—the first time the Philippines met the United Nations’ recommended benchmark for education spending.

READ: SONA 2026: Where does Marcos’ 40,000-classroom promise stand?

Article continues after this 

“We allocated a historic budget for education to address the widespread crisis that this sector is facing. We are hoping that for the upcoming Sona, we will hear progress report and what we can expect to solve the education crisis,” Gatchalian said in Filipino in a press release.

Gatchalian served as the chairperson of the Senate committee on finance during the budget deliberations for the 2026 national budget.

Gatchalian also pointed out the classroom backlog across the country, noting that this year’s budget covers P12.3-billion funding deficiency in the free higher education program accumulated from 2022 to 2025.

READ: Education leaders urge cross-sector action to reverse PH learning crisis

Of the total budget allocated for the education sector, P1.015 trillion goes to the Department of Education (DepEd). The Senate chief said that P67.9 billion is allotted for the construction of at least 22,000 classrooms.

Article continues after this 

Citing the DepEd’s National School Building Inventory, the Second Congressional Commission on Education (Edcom 2) said that the current classroom backlog across the country exceeds 166,000. The commission also said that 51,222 classrooms will be at least 50 years old by 2028, or by the time Marcos ends his term.

An analysis made by Edcom 2 in January 2026 showed that proficiency rates among Filipino students plunged as they moved through the education system. In a statement, it said that “the proportion of students considered “proficient” to “highly proficient” begins at a low baseline and then becomes negligible by the time they reach high school.”

Article continues after this 

Meanwhile, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro recently said that Marcos did not disclose what he will announce on his Sona but she hinted on possible “earthshaking announcements.” /jpv

World.title: Iloilo City flooding eases; 35 barangays still inundated as Kiyapo exits
World.content:
INQUIRER FILES

ILOILO CITY — Floodwaters have begun to recede in several parts of Iloilo City after Tropical Cyclone Kiyapo (international name: Noul) intensified into a typhoon and exited the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR), but at least 35 barangays remained flooded while more than 500 residents continued to be affected as of 6 a.m. Saturday, July 25.

The Iloilo City Emergency Operations Center (ICEOC), in its Situation Report No. 3, said a total of 45 barangays had experienced flooding since the onset of heavy rains. Floodwaters have already subsided in 10 barangays, leaving 35 barangays still inundated.

Authorities have placed the city’s Emergency Operations Center under Blue Alert as response operations continue.

Article continues after this 

READ: Wind signals lifted as Kiyapo heads towards Southern China on Saturday

The city government reported that 132 families, or 508 individuals, were affected by the flooding. Of these, 73 families composed of 221 individuals were staying inside four evacuation centers located in nine affected barangays.

The evacuation centers are serving residents from Calubihan and San Vicente in Jaro; Ticud in La Paz; Alalasan and Don Esteban in Lapuz; Airport in Mandurriao; and San Antonio, Compania Central and Infante in Molo.

Initial assessment by the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) also showed three partially damaged houses affecting five families or 15 individuals. The damaged houses were located in Barangay Airport in Mandurriao, Barangay Compania Central in Molo, and Barangay San Vicente in Jaro.

Strong winds associated with the weather disturbance also uprooted five trees, with incidents recorded in Jaro, La Paz and Mandurriao. No toppled electric posts were reported.

Article continues after this 

Among the areas still experiencing flooding were portions of Arevalo, City Proper, Jaro, La Paz, Lapuz, Mandurriao and Molo, with flood depths ranging from a few inches to as much as 48 inches in parts of Ticud, La Paz. Several areas in Sinkway, Lapuz remained under 24 to 36 inches of floodwater, while Don Esteban in Lapuz and Desamparados in Jaro each recorded flood depths of 36 inches.

Meanwhile, several previously flooded barangays had already reported receding waters, including Kahirupan and Ortiz in City Proper; Timawa Tanza 2 and Inday in City Proper; Bantud in La Paz; Oñate de Leon and Navais in Mandurriao; Calumpang, South San Jose and West Timawa in Molo.

Article continues after this 

Rainfall during the past 12 hours remained generally light to moderate, with the highest accumulation of 11 millimeters recorded at the West Visayas State University monitoring station. Wind speeds reached up to 50 kilometers per hour at the Lapuz Depot weather station.

Despite improving conditions in Iloilo, the city continued emergency operations, including 24/7 monitoring, flood surveillance, public information campaigns, evacuation assistance, declogging operations, and coordination with barangay officials and response agencies.

The ICEOC also recommended the implementation of the asynchronous alternative delivery mode for students at all levels in Iloilo City on July 25 as a precaution against the lingering effects of flooding.

According to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), Kiyapo had intensified into a typhoon before moving outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility early Saturday.

World.title: Pangilinan on survey of front-runners for next polls: Too early for 2028
World.content:
Sen. Francis Pangilinan. — Photo from Senate Social Media Unit

MANILA, Philippines — Following the release of a Pulse Asia survey on voter preferences ahead of the 2028 elections, where Sen. Robinhood Padilla topped the senatorial race, Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan took to social media to say it’s too early to name the front-runners.

In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Pangilinan said the 2028 elections are still in the distant future.

“Malayo pa ang 2028. Walang bibitiw!! [2028 is still a long way off. No one is backing down!],” he said

Article continues after this 

He, moreover, said that voter preferences can change overnight, agreeing with Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson’s comment about surveys as mere ‘snapshots of voters’ preferences in the post.

READ: Sara Duterte, Bong Go top bets for President, VP in 2028, survey says

“We may have run under different alliances, but I am happy that you and Sen Bam not only made it but won strong and big. That being said, surveys are nothing but snapshots of voters’ preferences during specific timeframes,” Lacson said in the comment thread on Pangilinan’s post in X.

Pangilinan added that votes ‘can be gained or lost’ at an instant, primarily ‘in an electoral landscape wherein digital technology makes it possible for content online to be viewed by tens of millions overnight’

Earlier, he posted photos of a pre-election survey from April 20 to 24, 2025, where he ranked in the 16th to 18th place, only 4 percent shy of being included in the top 12. He highlighted that the survey had a ±2 margin of error, implying that the Senate race was “anybody’s ball game.”

Article continues after this 

“We aren’t on the list on page 1; we are on page 2. We are ranked 16th to 18th, trailing the top 12 by 4 percent, while the margin of error is plus or minus 2 percent. As the saying goes, it’s anyone’s game, and the race for the 12th through 18th spots is a tight contest,” he said in Filipino.

Pangilinan recalled the previous year’s survey result ended with Sen. Bam Aquino as the second preferred senate candidate from being in the rank 11th to 18th bracket during the pre-election survey, while he placed fifth.

Article continues after this 

“The important thing is, we did not give up and fought hand to hand until the end. The result? Bam came in number 2 and we came in number 5. While Risa’s Akbayan Partylist came in number 1 and Leila also won the ML Partylist. Remember. The people did not abandon us and I am confident that the people will not abandon us,” he added.

Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson expressed support for Pangilinan, adding that surveys are mere “snapshots of voters’ preferences” during specific periods.

““Yes, Sen. Kiko. We may have run under different alliances, but I am happy that you and Sen. Bam not only made it but won strong and big. That being said, surveys are nothing but snapshots of voters’ preferences during specific timeframes,” he said.

The Pulse Asia survey, conducted from June 28 to July 6, showed that Padilla was the top preferred candidate at 48.4 percent, followed by Pasig City Mayor Vico Sotto at 47.9 percent.

World.title: Biliran Bridge restores full 15-ton load capacity after repair
World.content:
t0726visbreak3: Biliran Bridge restores full 15-ton load capacity after repair of expansion joints

TACLOBAN CITY — The Biliran Bridge has been cleared to accommodate all types of vehicles again after the completion of repair works that restored its original 15-ton maximum allowable load capacity, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) said.

DPWH-Biliran District Engineering Office District Engineer Irwin Antonio said the lifting of vehicle-type restrictions followed the replacement of the bridge’s expansion joints, which had been identified for repair after the structure was placed under restrictions following a bridge-swaying incident in December 2024.

READ: Biliran Bridge rehabilitation nears completion

Article continues after this 

All vehicles may now cross the bridge, provided their total load does not exceed 15 tons, beginning on July 23, Antonio said.

However, motorists must strictly follow safety rules while crossing the structure. These include avoiding gear shifting, allowing only one vehicle at a time to cross and maintaining a speed of 15 to 20 kilometers per hour.

Antonio urged motorists to comply with the regulations to help ensure their safety and protect the structural integrity of the bridge.

The Biliran Bridge, built in 1976, is the only road link connecting Biliran Island to Leyte and the rest of Eastern Visayas. It serves as a critical route for the movement of residents, agricultural products, commercial goods and essential services.

The bridge had been under a 15-ton load restriction since December 2024 after a viral video showed the structure visibly swaying, prompting authorities to conduct a structural inspection. Vehicles exceeding the allowable weight were prohibited from crossing and were required to use barge services between Biliran and Leyte.

Article continues after this 

While the repair works have allowed the bridge to resume normal vehicle access, the DPWH is pursuing longer-term measures to preserve the aging structure.

The agency proposed a P266-million retrofitting project under its 2027 budget request. The project would include installing additional support systems and reinforcing aging steel components.

Article continues after this 

Plans are also advancing for a proposed P1.72-billion parallel bridge project, with funding support from the Asian Development Bank. The project remains subject to feasibility studies and other pre-engineering activities.

Despite the proposed new bridge, authorities said the existing Biliran Bridge will be preserved as an important landmark and enduring symbol of the province’s connection to Leyte and the wider Eastern Visayas region. /jpv

World.title: BI denies spreading false info on Romualdez’s alleged bid to leave PH
World.content:
Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez appears at the Independent Commission for Infrastructure, Fort Bonifacio, Taguig City on October 14, 2025, to attend hearings on alleged flood control project anomalies. INQUIRER PHOTO / NIÑO JESUS ORBETA

MANILA, Philippines — The Bureau of Immigration (BI) on Saturday stood by its statements regarding former House Speaker Martin Romualdez’s alleged travel plans, saying it did not disseminate false information on the matter.

BI’s statement came after the lawyers of Romualdez demanded an apology from the agency over its alleged fake reports that the lawmaker was attempting to leave the country.

In a statement on Friday, Romualdez’ spokesperson Ade Fejardo said that the Solis Media Fajardo & Malilong Law Offices sent a demand letter addressed to BI Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado stating that the information on the lawmaker’s plan to leave the country is “patently false.”

Article continues after this 

READ: Romualdez camp to BI: Apologize over fake news on attempt to leave PH

According to Viado, the agency responded to legitimate media inquiries, emphasizing that it only provides factual information within the agency’s mandate.

“The Bureau respectfully rejects the allegation that it disseminated false or fabricated information. We remain committed to providing honest, accurate, and responsible public information while respecting due process and the constitutional rights of all persons,” Viado said in a press release.

Viado noted that the information the BI gave regarding alleged travel plans that did not push through pertains to a supposed trip in April 2026.

The statement from Romualdez’ spokesperson said that the demand letter was prompted by a July 21 statement by BI spokesperson Dana Sandoval, which said that the BI “received information that there were plans that did not push through.”

Article continues after this 

The information was cited by the Office of the Ombudsman, which accused Romualdez of attempting to leave the country as plunder and money laundering complaints were being prepared against him.

“The Bureau’s response referred to information available to the Bureau at the time and was issued solely in response to legitimate media inquiries. The Bureau did not initiate the public discussion on the matter,” Viado added.

Article continues after this 

Romualdez’ camp also said that the information given by the BI “unfairly created the impression” that he was attempting to flee the country to evade the pending criminal investigation against him.

In April 2026, Romualdez’ request to travel out of the country for his angioplasty follow-up checkup was granted by House Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III and Secretary General Cheloy Garafil.
